Inscription on the memorial at Qinglan Port, 105 AG
What is New Red Dawn?

New Red Dawn is an alternate universe of Avatar: The Last Airbender in which the Fire Nation is the Empire of Tajisaki, a modern industrial state, and the Hundred Year War is the first total war of the age of steam and steel. The wiki is written as its own world's encyclopedia, with disputed figures and rival histories. Read more >

Featured article

The Sôen strike was the Empire's single use of a weapon of mass destruction, in which a capital was destroyed without the war being won. The page traces the program that built it, the decision to use it, the ground it fell on and the argument about it that has never ended.

Featured person

Qin the Great conquered most of the continent in the late Warring States and was killed in a rigged duel outside Ba Sing Se in 270 BG. The south then rose against his heirs in the War of Liberation, and Qianchan won independence in 255 BG. He is remembered in the south as the founder and in Ba Sing Se as the traitor.

The Hundred Year War was a global conflict that lasted from 0 AG to 100 AG, waged by the Empire of Tajisaki against the Earth Kingdom, the Water Tribes, the Air Nomads and, from 30 AG, the Qianchan Republic. It was begun by Fire Lord Sozin, who used the return of a comet to attack the four Air Temples and destroy the Air Nomads, among whom the next Avatar was to be born. Over the next hundred years the Empire occupied the whole west coast of the Earth Kingdom, subjugated the Water Tribes, and fought for the oil of the Si Wong Desert. It developed jets, power armor and a weapon of mass destruction on the scale of the comet. It killed about {{stat:hyw_deaths_direct}} people, a little under 8% of the world's population in 0 AG, and committed two genocides and the war's other atrocities with chemical weapons that only it possessed.

The war ended in July 100 AG, when the Empire fired the Sōen at Ba Sing Se and its ruler, Ozai, was killed the next day by the Avatar in the Battle of Qinglan Port. The Empire's central authority collapsed. The wars and famines that followed, which killed another {{stat:hyw_postwar_deaths}} people, are known as the Post-War Conflicts.

Prelude

The Fire Nation's industrial revolution

The Fire Nation's apothecaries discovered gunpowder in about 3000 BG (see the [[point_of_divergence|point of divergence]]), its armies began to use it in earnest in 1000–700 BG and, by 290 BG, had begun the world's first industrial revolution. By 80 BG it had a four-round bolt-action rifle, and in 27 BG its first aircraft flew. It discovered oil in the Si Wong in 28 BG. The Qianchan Republic, which had seceded from the Earth Kingdom in 255 BG, matched it in a technological race from 26 BG. The Earth Kingdom, a large agrarian state, lagged behind, and industrialized only in the 20s AG with Qianchan's help. Firearms had spread slowly in the earlier centuries, because the populations were small, the necessary equipment was scarce and bending had a sacred place in folklore.

Sozin's plan

Avatar Roku, Sozin's friend, died in 12 BG on Island Jezhi, and Sozin, who could have helped him, left him to die. Sozin knew that the next Avatar would be born among the Air Nomads. He militarized the Fire Nation for twelve years, and planned to use the comet's return to exterminate the Air Nomads, and then to subjugate the Water Tribes and conquer the Earth Kingdom.

The world in 0 AG

The world's population was about {{stat:world_pop_0}}: the Earth Kingdom {{stat:pop_ek_0}}, the Qianchan Republic {{stat:pop_qc_0}}, the Fire Nation {{stat:pop_fn_0}}, the Water Tribes {{stat:pop_nwt_0}}+{{stat:pop_swt_0}}+{{stat:pop_wt_other_0}} and the Air Nomads {{stat:pop_an_0}}. The Earth Kingdom, with its provincial lords, had little central authority outside Ba Sing Se. The Fire Nation was the most industrialized state in the world.

Early stage (0–30 AG)

The Air Nomad Genocide

On the night the comet arrived, the Empire attacked the four Air Temples at once, with zeppelins carrying aircraft that could reach 4,000 meters, and firebombs and napalm shells enlarged by comet-empowered firebenders. Within a week it had razed the Western and Eastern island chains with their civilians, firebombed the Northern Air Temple and kept its ruin for an airbase, and taken the Southern Air Temple, the home of the next Avatar. About 3 million Air Nomads, benders and non-benders, died, together with about 400,000 Water Tribe and other civilians killed as collateral on ships and islands. The last Air Nomad community was killed in the snow of the South Pole in 20 AG. About 300–400 people with airbending survived, deep in Qianchan or the Earth Kingdom, and most did not know what they were. The Empire occupied the Western and Southern chains completely and built bases on them.

The Water Tribes

A week after the genocide began, the Empire bombarded both poles on Sozin's orders. In the First Battle of Agna Qel'a (11–19 September 0 AG), the Northern Battlegroup and a zeppelin division attacked the Northern capital with an incendiary made for ice. The Northern Water Tribe, with elite riflemen and waterbenders, repelled the landing, at a cost of about 52,000 dead, and the Empire settled for a forward air base on the far eastern pole, from which it bombed Agna Qel'a periodically. In the South the landings succeeded. The leaders were captured and forced to cooperate, and the Empire ran an occupation of forced labor, reprisals and terror, aimed at working the Southern Tribe to death. Uprisings and insurgency followed, the last of the early ones in 29 AG, and the South's population fell to 75% of its pre-war number. This is described in the article on the Subjugation of the Water Tribes.

Yanakawa and the west coast

In January 1 AG the Empire launched the invasion of Yanakawa, the Earth Kingdom's western coastal province, from its bases on the Western Air Temple chain. Its landing at Yu Dao began the Yanakawan Campaign, in which provincial levies attacked in mass against entrenched Imperial machine guns, and the Empire introduced mustard gas, the first use of chemical weapons in the war. The Earth Kingdom never acquired chemical weapons of its own. The campaign took ten years and killed about 3.5 million Earth Kingdom people and 450,000 Imperial soldiers. By 10 AG the Empire held the whole west coast.

The northern and southern pushes

From 10 AG the Empire pushed north into the mountains, and in the 20s tried to reach Omashu and break east from the south of Yanakawa. It was foiled, and instead turned into the high mountains and, by 25 AG, had cut the southern Omashu front off from the rest of the Earth Kingdom, which Qianchan then supplied by sea. By 27 AG the Empire pushed toward the Si Wong for its oil. Throughout, the Fire Navy alone held naval superiority.

Qianchan enters the war

In 27 AG a Qianchan civilian ship was sunk near the Western Air Temple waters. The first naval engagement between the Imperial and Qianchan navies, in 30 AG, was a draw, and Qianchan entered the war and allied with the Earth Kingdom. It supplied it with arms and doctrine, and helped it begin to industrialize.

Middle stage (30–95 AG)

Eastern Push (30–50 AG)

The Empire's General Staff planned to push east across the grasslands to the Si Wong for its oil. It took the western grasslands in a series of tank battles, including the Hesha Plains (37–38 AG) and the siege of Dongping (41–43 AG), and by 50 AG the Imperial front ran from the north coast down the western plains to the desert's western edge and across the sea through the Western Air Temple chain. The Eastern Push killed about 6.8 million Earth Kingdom people.

Desert War (50–79 AG)

The Desert War was the Empire's first attempt on the oil fields, mostly an air war with small gains. It captured the fields four times, in 56, 63, 71 and 77 AG, and was thrown off each time by Qianchan–Earth Kingdom counter-offensives. About 1.1 million people died.

Si Wong Offensive (80–88 AG)

The second attempt, Plan Yellow, drawn up by General Iroh as the General Staff Directorate's Planning Director, was a ground offensive that took the Tongba oil basin and the desert's road and rail corridor between 8 July 80 and 23 August 88 AG. Coalition supply lines were forced around the desert, and the Empire held the oil until Ozai's death. About 1.9 million personnel fought on each side. The oil paid for the late war's technologies: the first jet flew in 81 AG, the mechanized Breaker armor in 83 AG, and the first assault rifle in 95 AG.

The South and the poles in the middle years

The Southern Water Tribe's population fell to about 50% by 99 AG, as the Empire turned the South into a colony and research base. Imperial raiding forces, the Southern Raiders, hunted the last waterbenders. The Northern Water Tribe, which had no navy, lost about 20% of its people to bombing by 40 AG. The Empire's policy toward both was elimination by labor and bombardment.

Jasmine Island (90 AG)

On 7 June 90 AG Rear Admiral Yueya destroyed the harbor town and fields of Jasmine Island, which killed about 2,000 civilians, in a mutiny that was stopped by the garrison, by Navy sailors who broke out of the brig of a battlecruiser, and by Captain Lu Ten of the Armored Corps. Lu Ten then submitted an Address on Conduct to the Diet, and became the center of a reform movement.

Late stage (95–100 AG)

Siege of Ba Sing Se (96–97 AG)

In 95 AG the Imperial eastern group took Hanxu and Babao, the junctions at the Si Wong's eastern edge, and the Empire, fueled by the Si Wong oil, launched its greatest offensive. Field Marshal Iroh's army besieged Ba Sing Se from 14 February 96 AG. Imperial bombers breached the Outer Wall in March with a super-heavy conventional bomb. The Empire's jets and turboprop bombers controlled the sky, and its aircraft dropped leaflets urging surrender, then bombs and chemical weapons across the rings. King Kuei's eyes were opened in the first weeks of the siege. Qianchan, which was in effect the southern province that had broken away, refused to commit troops until Kuei was evacuated, and kept its air force at the Omashu front. The city's western section was gassed and bombed, and civilians died in huge numbers: about 2.7 million of the siege's 3.5 million dead were civilians. In the Inner City, Imperial assault battalions took the Palace and held it for a week before civilian conscripts and metalbenders drove them out. Lu Ten was killed there on 25 November. A Qianchan-led counter-offensive retook Hanxu and Babao and cut the Imperial supply line, and the siege ended on 19 April 97 AG. Iroh was demoted, and Azulon, who had lost faith in him, issued an Ash Directive to raze the city, which Iroh opposed.

The Fire Nation: Azulon, Ozai and the Pardon Crisis

On 10 June 97 AG Fire Lord Azulon was poisoned at dinner and died in his sleep, in a killing that Ozai arranged and that the Court blamed on Qianchan agents. Ozai was crowned on 24 June, and on 3 July pardoned Yueya and Zhao, who had been convicted over Jasmine Island, and sent them to the Southern Water Tribe's small-scale insurgency. The Diet and part of the military lost faith in him. The opposition gathered around Iroh, who was forced to retire in 98 AG and given a seat in the Diet, and the Diet passed bills for veterans and for the people, but the Eastern Colonies Assimilation Bill, which would have given Yanakawa citizenship, was shelved. This polarized the Empire, as described in the Pardon Crisis of 97 AG.

The Earth Kingdom: the Dai Li coup attempt (98 AG)

In the early hours of 22 March 98 AG, the Dai Li, led by Grand Secretariat Long Feng, tried to seize King Kuei and rule through him, as they had murdered his father. The coup failed within fourteen hours, and killed about 1,900 people. The Dai Li were purged in the Great Review (98–99 AG), from 2,400 agents to about 700, and Kuei took direct command of the war from Ba Sing Se on the Northern Front. A second, smaller attempt in January 100 AG was also put down.

The polar operation (99 AG)

On 13 November 99 AG the Empire began a combined operation against both poles, to eradicate the Water Tribes so that no new Avatar could rise from them, and to scorch the poles clear for a new Fire Nation colony. In the South it crushed the Southern Uprising (12 May – 9 December 99 AG). The Avatar, Aang, was found in the ice by Southern guerrillas in late November and evacuated to Qianchan as the capital fell. In the North it launched the Siege of the North, the Second Battle of Agna Qel'a, with jets carrying chemical and napalm bombs and elite winter troops, many of them veterans of the South, in Arctic Breaker armor with flamethrowers. About 800,000 people died in the city in five weeks. The Chief and most of the Council were evacuated by Qianchan submarines. By June 100 AG the North's population had fallen to 50%, and the South's to about 30% by the end of the war.

The Coalition Northern Offensive and the Ba Sing Se Treaty (100 AG)

In February–March 100 AG a joint Qianchan–Earth Kingdom offensive tried to crush the Empire once and for all, and failed against Imperial air power, gas and fuel from the Si Wong. The Ba Sing Se Treaty (27 March) put the two armies under a Combined Coalition Command at Ba Sing Se, with Kuei as nominal head.

The Sōen

The Imperial Research Bureau had worked for decades, from 47 AG, to harness the comet and to build a nuclear-scale weapon of mass destruction. IRB scientists who refused to build a fission weapon were executed in 99 AG, and the program produced the Sōen, a fire-crystal array fed by firebending. It was built for one purpose, the strike on Ba Sing Se. On 17 July 100 AG Ozai, who was at the forward array at Qinglan Port, fired it, and the beam atomized the western Outer Wall and destroyed the Inner Wall. It killed about 380,000 people, blinded thousands and burned many more, and destroyed the Coalition's command for 36 hours. The Fire Nation army, which had been organized and ready, advanced into the disorganized defenders, and was thrown off by what followed.

Conclusion (July 100 AG)

Battle of Qinglan Port (18 July 100 AG)

The Yanakawan Liberation Front, which had been fighting the Empire since April, and Earth Kingdom and Qianchan units, with the Avatar, attacked Qinglan Port at noon on 18 July, to capture the Sōen array before a second discharge. The Imperial garrison was caught off guard, and Ozai, who had proclaimed himself Tentei (Emperor of the Sky) the day before, was killed by the Avatar in the Avatar State, with a stone lance through his lungs, 23 minutes after the first shells fell. Soldiers on both sides watched. At 12:27 an Imperial officer announced over the high command radio, "The Emperor is dead." The Empire's fanatical units fought on until 19:00, and the rest surrendered, fled or fought each other.

The succession crisis

The General Staff Directorate rigged the Privy Council's succession for Ozai's daughter Azula in a few violent days, over the Diet's resolution for the popular Zuko. The press was outraged, and the Diet's defiance in August was met with shooting. This was the start of the Fire Nation Civil War. Royalist propaganda later credited Zuko with the defeat of Ozai.

Aftermath

The Post-War Conflicts (100–120 AG)

The wars and famines that followed killed about 19 million people, and are counted as the third most deadly war in history, after the Hundred Year War and the Warring States wars.

  • Earth Kingdom warlord wars (100–112 AG). After the Sōen strike destroyed the command in Ba Sing Se, generals and warlords fought each other and starved the country, until Omashu, Ba Sing Se and Gaoling, the Qianchan capital, pacified them. About 13 million died.
  • Yanakawan War of Independence (100–110 AG). The YLF and its allies won independence in a war with twelve decisive battles, which ended on land with the Treaty of Qinglan on 28 April 105 AG. The Court faction under Azula continued the war at sea until 110 AG. About 1.2 million died. It led to the United Republic of Nations.
  • Fire Nation Civil War (100–118 AG). The Royalists under Zuko, the Ozai loyalists and the Salvationists fought for 18 years, with the Salvationists taking over most of the Court's field army from within and breaking with it in 116 AG. About 3.5 million died. The war ended with Azula's death in a duel with Zuko on 9 May 118 AG.
  • Holdouts and the polar famines accounted for the rest.

Zuko's reign and the United Republic

Zuko was crowned Fire Lord in 118 AG, survived an assassination attempt at his coronation, and spent his 50-year reign rebuilding. The United Republic of Nations emerged from Yanakawa, with a flag designed by Lord Sokka. Qianchan took custody of the Southern Air Temple and gave the remaining airbenders autonomy.

Casualties and demographics

Nation Dead Share of 0 AG population
Earth Kingdom about 29,600,000 about 13%

Fire Nation about 3,510,000 about 3%
Air Nomads about 3,000,000 about 100%
Qianchan about 1,090,000 under 1%
Total about 40,800,000 about 8%

About 30 million died before the Si Wong Offensive began. For every Fire Nation death there were about eight Earth Kingdom deaths, because of the industrial gap, the Earth Kingdom's mass-charge doctrine, its fragmented command, the Empire's chemical weapons and air power, and the occupation policy of genocide and famine. The ratio narrowed to about 1.4 to 1 at Si Wong, after Qianchan armed the Earth Kingdom, but the sieges of civilians kept the overall ratio high. The world's population was about 548 million in 100 AG, after about 81 million excess deaths (ledger).

War capabilities

Historiography

Imperial histories describe the war as a campaign of unification and economical conquest. Earth Kingdom histories tend to blame their provincial lords and give no casualty or famine figures. Qianchan archives, which hold the most complete record of ships, convoys, intercepts and gas casualties, are the main outside source. Royalist propaganda after 118 AG gave Zuko the credit for ending the war.

Also known as the Fire Nation. A totalitarian ethnonationalist state of the Fire Islands, ruled by the Fire Lord. The aggressor of the Hundred Year War.

Capital Caldera City
Government Absolute monarchy under the Fire Lord, with an Imperial Diet, a Cabinet and a General Staff Directorate
Population About {{stat:pop_fn_0|n}} (0 AG); about 172,000,000 (100 AG, before the civil war)
Armed forces About 8,000,000 (80 AG)
Ideology "The Truth": the Fire Lord's sacred authority; the Homeland Purity Initiative
War dead About 3,500,000 (Hundred Year War); about 3,500,000 (Fire Nation Civil War)

The Empire of Tajisaki is the Fire Nation as a modern industrial state. It began the Hundred Year War in 0 AG with the Air Nomad Genocide, and by 80 AG was the strongest military power in the world, with the largest industry, a monopoly on chemical weapons, and the world's first aircraft, tanks, jets and power armor. It lost the war because its central authority collapsed when Fire Lord Ozai was killed in 100 AG.

Current affairs, 170 AG

Inside the country

  • A new reign. Fire Lord Izumi has reigned since 168 AG, and Prime Minister Ryoko Sato's Cabinet governs with the Imperial Diet. The Restoration Party, the Veterans' League and the Ember Greens compete over reconstruction, the military budget and geothermal and civilian fission power.
  • The economy. It is about {{stat:gdp_fn_170}} ({{stat:gdppc_fn_170}} a person), second only to Qianchan, with the war industries converted to housing, rail and exports. Oil bought under the Si Wong Accord is its main strategic dependence.
  • The memory of the war. The anniversary of the comet is marked in silence and the Day of Ash is a day of mourning. The report of the Commission on Imperial Conduct still shapes debate about the army and the throne.

Geopolitical decisions

  • Paying for the peace. The Fire Nation pays no cash reparations, but funds the Rebuilding Fund for the Earth Kingdom's occupied provinces and is the largest importer of its grain.
  • A wary partnership with Qianchan. Joint research on fission goes on beside rivalry in heavy industry.
  • The United Republic. The government wants trade and a common language of commerce with its former colonies, without reopening old grievances. See [[united_republic_of_nations|United Republic of Nations]].

Government

The Fire Lord. Under the Imperial Constitution, the Fire Lord rules "in perpetuity" and without limit (Art. 1), is sacred and inviolable (Art. 2), commands the armed forces and alone makes war and peace (Art. 5), and may issue Rescripts and Proclamations that override all other law (Art. 7). The successor is designated by the reigning Fire Lord, and a designation is final. Without one, the Privy Council must meet within 72 hours and the claimant must produce fire at a confirmation ceremony within seven days (Art. 3).

The Diet. The Imperial Diet has two houses, the House of Lords (princes, peers and appointees) and the House of Representatives, which is elected by men who have completed their service (Arts. 20–22). It may legislate and pass the budget, but not investigate military operations, the Ministry of Truth or the Fire Lord (Art. 28), and succession is outside its authority (Art. 25).

The Cabinet. The Prime Minister and a cabinet of ministries (National Enlightenment, Truth, National Harmony, War, the Navy, Aviation, Colonial Affairs and others) serve at the Fire Lord's pleasure. The General Staff Directorate has a separate constitutional position and a right of direct audience with the Fire Lord (Art. 32). The Ministry of Truth runs internal security and is not subject to judicial review (Art. 33).

The empire. Colonial subjects were classified as Recognized Imperial Persons, Enrolled Colonial Subjects, Unenrolled Populations or Designated Threat Populations, and colonial administrators had combined executive, legislative and judicial power (Arts. 42–43). The Homeland Purity Initiative authorized "integration, resettlement and removal" (Art. 44), and Article 45 declared the Air Nomad Question "settled." All adults owed three years of military service, a precondition for voting.

Emergency powers. In a declared emergency, rights are suspended, the Cabinet rules by decree and the Fire Lord may declare martial law (Arts. 46–49). Only the Fire Lord can end an emergency, which in 100 AG left the Empire's emergency powers frozen with no one to lift them.

History

The Empire's ruling line, of which Sozin, Azulon and Ozai were the Fire Lords of the war, took the Fire Nation from industrial revolution (290 BG) through the Hundred Year War. After Ozai's death, a rigged succession split it into the Court, the Royalists and the Salvationists, and the Fire Nation Civil War followed. Zuko's Royalists won in 118 AG, and the Empire became the Fire Nation of his reign.

Country profile, 170 AG

The figures in this section describe the Fire Nation as it stood in 170 AG, fifty-two years after Zuko's Royalists won the civil war and the Empire became a constitutional kingdom. They are estimates, and many were compiled by the Ministry of Statistics, whose predecessor the Ministry of Truth is remembered for a different kind of arithmetic.

Names

The state's formal name was Tajisaki until 118 AG, after its ruling clan, and the Fire Nation is the colloquial name that outsiders and, increasingly, its own citizens used. After the civil war the constitution of 119 AG adopted Fire Nation as the formal name of the realm and kept Tajisaki as the name of the royal house. The word "Empire" was dropped from the title, and with it the Imperial Rescripts and the title of Tentei that Ozai had claimed. See History of the Fire Nation.

Geography

The Fire Nation is an archipelago in the south-east of the world, with four large islands and more than a thousand small ones. Its land is mountainous and volcanic, with narrow coastal plains, black-sand beaches and deep natural harbors. The great volcanoes supply geothermal heat, mineral wealth and fertile ash soils, and are also the country's chief natural hazard. The climate runs from warm-temperate in the north to tropical in the southern chain, with a monsoon season that brings typhoons. The islands have few large rivers and little arable land, which is why the Empire imported grain and why its agriculture is intensive and terraced. The capital, Caldera City, sits in the flooded caldera of an extinct volcano.

Government and politics

The Fire Nation is a unitary constitutional monarchy. The Fire Lord is head of state and a ceremonial and moral authority, retains the power to dissolve the House of Representatives on the advice of the Prime Minister, and no longer commands the armed forces alone. The 119 AG constitution restored the Imperial Diet and abolished Article 28's ban on investigating the military, the Ministry of Truth and the throne. The ministries of Truth and National Harmony were dissolved, and the General Staff Directorate was placed under the Cabinet. Suffrage, once tied to military service, became universal for adults in 125 AG. The House of Lords now holds the heads of the thirteen houses, now serving ten-year terms, and appointed life peers; the House of Representatives has 375 elected members. The old active-duty rule for service ministers was abolished.

Politics is dominated by three currents: the Restoration Party, heirs of the Royalists; the Veterans' League, the successor of the Army's reform wing; and the Ember Greens, who campaign for geothermal and civilian fission power. The Salvationist movement, suppressed by about 120 AG, has almost no following at home and survives mostly as a historical grievance and a literary motif, though a splinter, the Thunderbolt sect, broke from it in 169 AG, and its exiles abroad inspired later movements. A Commission on Imperial Conduct (125–131 AG) investigated the war's atrocities, and its report is a founding document of the postwar state.

Foreign relations

The Fire Nation is a member of the Concord of Nations, the loose body of states created by the Caldera Accord of 121 AG, and has full relations with every state. Its relations with the United Republic of Nations, born from its former colonies, are close and tense: the two share a language of commerce and a history of grievance, and the Republic's veterans remember the Eastern Territories. Relations with Qianchan have moved from rivalry to a wary partnership, with rival industrial sectors and joint research on fission. The Fire Nation pays no reparations in cash but funds the Rebuilding Fund for the Earth Kingdom's occupied provinces. It is the largest importer of Earth Kingdom grain.

Military

The armed forces of the Fire Nation number about 420,000 active personnel, a small fraction of the 8,000,000 the Empire fielded in 80 AG. Conscription was abolished in 122 AG. The Army, Navy and Air Service answer to the Ministry of Defense, and the old Army–Navy divide persists mainly as a rivalry over the budget. The Sōen arrays at Caldera were dismantled under the Caldera Accord, and the chemical stockpiles were destroyed under international inspection. The Fire Nation keeps the world's largest navy by tonnage, a carrier fleet inherited from the Empire, and a marine corps that remains the most prestigious unit in its forces.

Economy

The Fire Nation remains one of the world's three largest economies and the most densely industrialized. Its output is led by steel, shipbuilding, machinery, chemicals, electronics and rail equipment, and by a large services sector. It lost the Si Wong oil in 100 AG and now buys it under the Si Wong Accord; it generates a third of its electricity from volcanic geothermal plants and about a fifth from civilian fission. The postwar economy was rebuilt around housing, rail and reconstruction, with the war industries converted to civilian production. Inequality is moderate, with a persistent gap between the industrial cities and the rural south. The currency is the ryō. See Fire Nation economy and society.

Science and technology

The Imperial Research Bureau was dissolved and its western complex, seized by the Salvationists in 109 AG, became the civilian Tajisaki Institute of Science. The Fire Nation leads in jet propulsion, materials science, volcanic engineering and seismology, and shares a civilian fission program with Qianchan. Its universities are among the oldest in the world, and its Library of the Sages in Caldera City is the largest repository of its early records.

Demographics

The population of about 214 million is among the most urbanized in the world, concentrated on the coastal plains and in the five cities of more than five million: Caldera City, Harbor Kuro, Shinja, Port Hana and Taisu. The census of 168 AG found a population that is about 91 percent Fire National by descent, with large minorities of Earth Kingdom, Water Tribe and mixed origin, many of them descendants of those deported during the war. The state religion was abolished in 119 AG; the Fire Sages remain the largest religious body, with Sunnic, Air Nomad-inspired and Spirit traditions growing. Life expectancy is 79 years.

Culture

Fire Nation culture is known for its theater (the Ember Island troupes and the Caldera Opera), formal gardens, tea ceremonies, calligraphy, festivals and martial arts, among them the Agni Kai, the duel of honor, which survives in a regulated and non-lethal form. Cuisine is spicy and seafood-based. The country's memory of the war is divided between those who treat it as a national shame and those who treat it as a national tragedy, and public ceremonies on the anniversary of the comet are held in silence. The Day of Ash, on the date of the Sōen strike, is a day of mourning.
