The Qianchan Republic is the federal republic of the southern earth lands. It is in effect the southern province of the Earth Kingdom that broke away, and it was born out of war. Its founder in spirit was Qin the Great, a lord of Gaoling who set out to reform Ba Sing Se's absolute authority, with the Avatar Kyoshi, the King of Omashu and the Lord of Yu Dao behind him, and who was killed outside the capital in 270 BG, in a duel in which the Earth King cheated. His death did not end the movement. The southern earth lands rose against his heirs' enemies in the War of Liberation, many Earth Kingdom soldiers defected, and the republic's independence was recognized in 255 BG.

It is an industrial state with a citizen-militia tradition, a federal system, a strong navy and armored forces, and a politics that Ba Sing Se has never accepted as legitimate. Its citizens call themselves the "Fifth Nation," a name that began as a taunt from the kingdom's court and was adopted by the republic's printers and veterans. It was the only state in the world, besides the Fire Nation, that could build what the other could build, and for that reason it sits at the center of the Empire's case for the Hundred Year War.

Current affairs, 170 AG

Inside the republic

  • Coalition politics. No party governs alone. The Veterans' Union, the Commerce and Industry Party, the Agrarian Assemblies and the Federal Union form cabinets that are replaced regularly.
  • The largest economy. It is about {{stat:gdp_qc_170}} ({{stat:gdppc_qc_170}} a person), with about {{stat:pop_qc_170|m}} people, a figure that includes Earth Kingdom war refugees and their descendants.
  • Tieshan. The civilian fission program supplies about a quarter of the electricity, and its capacity for a weapon is a subject of treaty negotiation.
  • Exiles in the southern islands. Salvationist refugees who fled the Fire Nation after 120 AG live in the republic's southern island chain, and the cabinet watches them. See Salvationists.

Geopolitical decisions

  • Governing itself. Policy remains "we govern ourselves; we do not export governance". It is the Earth Kingdom's treaty ally and the Fire Nation's partner in research and rival in industry.
  • The United Republic. Qianchan is the principal sponsor of the republic. See [[united_republic_of_nations|United Republic of Nations]].
  • The Southern Water Tribe. Qianchan's close ties to the South, which it armed in the war, will be tested by the split that begins in 170 AG.

Origins

The land and the old grievance

The south of the Earth Kingdom was always a different country from the capital. Its provinces were wetter, richer in coal and iron, closer to the sea, and farther from the Inner City. Under the kings of Ba Sing Se they paid the same tribute as the north and received less protection, and the memory of the Yellow Neck Uprising (312–305 BG), in which the capital put down a peasant rebellion with little regard for the provinces that bore the cost, was not forgotten. The south's lords, merchants and farm assemblies shared a view that the kingdom existed for its capital. Qin was the first man to make that view an army.

Qin and the coalition

Qin came out of Gaoling as a reformer rather than a rebel. His program was to limit the Earth King's authority, regularize provincial taxation and make the kingdom's armies answerable to something other than the palace. He built a coalition of provincial lords, the King of Omashu and the Lord of Yu Dao, and with the support of the Avatar Kyoshi he marched on Ba Sing Se. He was killed outside the capital in 270 BG, in the duel that Ba Sing Se's court says it won and the south says it stole. The southern army walked home carrying his body, and it did not disband.

The Southern Army

The formation that fought the War of Liberation is usually called the Southern Army. It was assembled from Qin's surviving regiments, from Earth Kingdom units that deserted the capital's service, and from village militias that had armed themselves in the first years of the rising. It had no single commander. Authority was held by a collective command council of senior officers and delegates, which for fifteen years governed the territory it held, collected taxes, appointed administrators and issued decrees. This is the origin of two traits that the republic never lost: its distrust of any one person holding a sword and a treasury at once, and its habit of settling hard questions by committee.

The War of Liberation (270–255 BG)

The war lasted fifteen years and was fought over the southern provinces, the roads to the capital and the grain that moved on them. It was not a single campaign. The Earth Kingdom's armies were larger and held the walls of Ba Sing Se, but they were unreliable in the south, where entire units defected to the Southern Army once it was clear that the capital was not paying them. The republic's later image of itself as an army of citizens begins here: a militia that had won because its soldiers owned the fields they fought on.

The southern forces took the coalfields and the river ports first. In 255 BG the capital, weakened by the first of two peasant uprisings inside Ba Sing Se itself, accepted a settlement that recognized the south's independence. The Southern Army's command council signed for the south. The Earth King signed, but the kingdom's court never wrote the word "republic" into any document, and so the republic's legal standing has been disputed in Ba Sing Se ever since.

The founding of the republic

The republic was not proclaimed in a day. The process had four stages:

  1. The provisional council (270–262 BG). The Southern Army's officers governed alone. The council was effective but narrow, and it ruled by decree.
  2. Pressure from below (c. 262–258 BG). Peasant organizations demanded that the land they had won be theirs by law. Merchants, who paid for much of the war, demanded a currency and courts they could trust. Both groups pressed the council to include them or lose them.
  3. The conventions (258–255 BG). A series of district conventions elected delegates who drafted a constitution: a legislature of districts, a civilian executive, regular taxation, and an army placed under civilian authority.
  4. The settlement of 255 BG. The treaty with Ba Sing Se ended the war. The republic's first President took office the same year, and the council dissolved itself.

The date of the republic's founding is therefore debated in its own histories. The Qianchan state marks 255 BG, the treaty year. Constitutional scholars point instead to the last convention, a year or two earlier, and a few nationalists to the first council in 270 BG. Ba Sing Se, for its part, marks nothing, and refers to the period as "the secession."

The Qin house

Qin's family survived him. In the republic it became a political house rather than a dynasty: it kept its estates and its wealth, held seats in the legislature, and for several generations supplied officers and administrators. Its members were often the republic's most conservative voices and sometimes its most nostalgic, and there was friction between the house and the republicans who thought that no family should be remembered as the republic's owner. The house never made a claim to rule, and it was a condition of the constitutional settlement that it would not. In Ba Sing Se, the Qin house is remembered as a pretender line. In Gaoling, it is remembered as a family that was, on the whole, content to be honored.

Government

The republic is a federal republic with a President and a bicameral legislature, the Parliament, in Gaoling.

InstitutionRole
PresidentHead of state and of the executive. Appoints ministers with the consent of Parliament. Commander-in-chief in time of war, but the army answers to the legislature on funding and to the courts on discipline.
Parliament, upper houseRepresents the member states. Ratifies treaties, confirms the senior officers of the armed forces.
Parliament, lower houseRepresents districts by population. Originates taxes and the budget.
Member states and regionsHold powers not given to the federation: police, education, local courts and much of land law. Zaofu, governed by the Beifong family, is the best-known example of a region that wrote its own rules.
CourtsFederal courts hear disputes between states and cases that reach the constitution.

The federal system was strengthened in the Hundred Year War as a precaution against invasion: a republic whose provinces could govern themselves could survive the loss of its capital. This was a lesson taken, in part, from the fall of Ba Sing Se's centralized bureaucracy under pressure in earlier centuries. Both the Earth Kingdom's historians and Qianchan's treat it as the republic's most important constitutional choice.

Law and society

The republic recognizes its citizens' right to keep and bear arms in a citizen militia, a tradition that predates the constitution and that the army treats as a reserve. Every adult citizen is expected to have served in or trained with the militia, which in peace is a social institution and in war is the republic's second army. The press is free in law and often rowdy in practice. Churches and temples are not established. The state does not require loyalty oaths, a fact that its officials point to when criticizing the Empire's.

Politics and factions

The republic's politics are noisy, fragmented and coalitional. No party has governed alone for long. The main currents are described below in general terms; their names and fortunes have shifted across the centuries.

CurrentBasePosition
Veterans of the Southern Army and their successorsThe officer corps, militia associations, border districtsDefense first. Wary of Ba Sing Se and of any accommodation with the Fire Nation.
Merchant and industrial interestsPort cities, the coal and iron belt, the Academy of GaolingTrade, standard weights and currency, steady growth. Prefer deterrence to war but will pay for deterrence.
Agrarian assembliesFarming districts, the old village militiasLand rights, low taxes, local control. Skeptical of the army's budget and of foreign entanglements.
FederalistsMember states and regions such as ZaofuLimit the center's authority. Defend regional rule-making.
The Qin house and its alliesEstates, old officer familiesContinuity, symbolic honor for Qin, a cautious conservatism.

This fragmentation is both a strength and a weakness. It prevented any military faction from seizing the state, and it made the republic slow to commit to a long war. In the decades before 0 AG, its governments often fell over the question of how much to spend on rearmament, and the Fire Nation's planners counted this slowness among the republic's weaknesses.

Economy and technology

Qianchan's economy grew from coal, iron, river transport and a merchant class that had paid for a war and expected a return. Its engineers adopted coal-fired engines in 255 BG, the year of independence, and by the century before the Hundred Year War its railways, ports and mills were among the largest in the world. Its universities, centered on the Academy of Gaoling, trained engineers, chemists and physicists in numbers the Earth Kingdom could not match. The repeater, a rifle that fires multiple rounds without reloading by hand, was in service by 130 BG.

From 26 BG the republic and the Fire Nation were in a recognizable technology race. Each had a steel industry, a railway network and a research establishment, and each watched the other's patents, ship launches and exhibitions. The Empire's Imperial Research Bureau kept a department solely for Qianchan intelligence. In the republic, the Academy's journals, which printed freely, were a source the Fire Nation read closely. The race ended the Fire Nation's lead in mechanical engineering and, according to its own staff, narrowed it in chemistry and explosives.

Relations with the Earth Kingdom and the Dai Li

Ba Sing Se fought two suppression campaigns against the republic, in 240 BG and 225 BG. Both failed. The Preliminary Accord of 224 BG set a boundary but did not recognize the republic, which is why the kingdom's court has been able to claim for two centuries that it never conceded anything. To stop republican ideas from spreading north, the kingdom founded the Dai Li around 215 BG, and the republic has regarded it since as the kingdom's secret police. Dai Li agents operated in the southern provinces and the republic's border towns and, in turn, Qianchan's own services learned to watch them.

For two centuries the Long Cold Peace was a relationship of trade and hostility. Goods moved across the border; so did smugglers, spies and the occasional defector. When reformers in the Earth Kingdom asked Qianchan for help, the republic refused, and its answer, "we govern ourselves; we do not export governance," became a formal policy. It had two reasons for it. The first was principle: a republic that exports itself by force is an empire. The second was prudence: any support for rebels in the north would give Ba Sing Se the pretext it wanted for a third war.

The road to the Alliance

As the Fire Nation rearmed after 37 BG, the republic and the kingdom had to decide whether their quarrel mattered more than their danger. Both knew by the 20s BG that the Empire was building the largest army and fleet in its history. Both read the same warnings and drew different conclusions. Ba Sing Se believed that the Empire would think twice about an attack on the walls. Qianchan believed that the Empire would not.

The Alliance Treaty of 3 BG

The Alliance Treaty of 3 BG was a pact of mutual defense between the Earth Kingdom and Qianchan. The republic signed it only on condition that Ba Sing Se revise its language of non-recognition: the treaty's text refers to the republic by name, which the kingdom's court had never done. Even so, the treaty did not create a joint command, a shared intelligence service or a plan for who would defend what. The two powers could not agree on any of them without recognizing one another's authority. The result was a deterrent in form rather than substance, and the Empire's staff knew it.

The republic's own diplomats offered alternatives in the years before the war, among them a standing combined staff, a standardized railway gauge to the border and a naval convention with the Northern Water Tribe. The kingdom accepted none of them. In Gaoling, the failure of those proposals is remembered as the lost chance of the age.

Why the Empire attacked

The republic's historians do not accept that the Hundred Year War was inevitable. They argue that the Empire chose it, and that it chose it for reasons it believed were practical. They set out the reasons as follows.

  • Energy. The Fire Nation's own forecasts, commissioned by the Imperial Research Bureau, gave its domestic oil about a century. The only large oilfield in the world's reach lay in the Si Wong Desert, inside the Earth Kingdom. Qianchan's coal industry, by contrast, was secure, and its engineers were working on alternatives.
  • A rival that would not stay behind. The republic matched the Empire in steel, rail, shipbuilding and, by the 20s BG, in the sciences. The Empire's planners calculated that the Fire Nation's lead would not survive another generation of Qianchan growth, and that a war later would be harder than a war now.
  • The Avatar. The Avatar Roku had spared Sozin in 37 BG, and was the one person the Empire could not intimidate. Sozin left Roku to die in 12 BG, and the next Avatar would be born among the Air Nomads. The republic's analysts concluded, after the war, that the Empire had calculated its attack to fall in the gap before a new Avatar could be found and trained.
  • A hollow Diet. The Imperial Diet could not investigate the Fire Lord, the military or the Ministry of Truth, which meant that no one inside the Empire could stop the decision.

The republic's own analysts note that the Empire's case for necessity was built on assumptions it did not test: that the oil could not be bought, that the republic would not respond, and that the war could be won in a few years. The first assumption was never tested because the Empire's staff never asked. The republic had offered, in the late 20s BG, to discuss an oil-sharing arrangement through neutral brokers. The offer went unanswered.

In the Hundred Year War

Qianchan entered the war in 30 AG, after one of its civilian ships was sunk in 27 AG and a naval battle with the Imperial Navy was a draw. It supplied Omashu by sea after the southern front was cut off, helped the Earth Kingdom industrialize, taught it desert warfare, and fought a submarine war against Imperial shipping. In the Siege of Ba Sing Se, it refused to commit troops until King Kuei was evacuated, and kept its whole air force on the Omashu front. It evacuated the Northern Water Tribe's leaders by submarine in 99 AG.

Its war cost about 1,090,000 lives. Its armed forces reached about 4,500,000 by 80 AG. Its population, which was about {{stat:pop_qc_0|n}} at the war's start, was about {{stat:pop_qc_100|n}} by 100 AG, an increase which its demographers attribute in part to refugees from the Earth Kingdom.

After the war

After the war the republic pacified the Earth Kingdom's warlords from Gaoling, supplied the Yanakawan rebels with surplus weapons, and preserved the Southern Air Temple, granting the airbenders autonomy there. Its fission program is known as Tieshan.

Historiography

Qin's legacy is disputed.

ViewHeld byArgument
Qin the liberatorThe republic's schools, veterans' associationsHe was the man who first demanded that the kingdom answer to its people, and he died for it.
Qin the usurperBa Sing Se's court historiesHe raised an army against his king and was killed for it. The republic is a fruit of treason.
Qin the symbolModern academic historiansThe real founders were the Southern Army's council and the district conventions; Qin's name was attached to them afterward.

Historians also disagree on whether the republic was founded in 270, 258 or 255 BG, whether the Southern Army was an instrument of democracy or a military government that grew into one, and whether the Fire Nation's attack could have been avoided by an earlier, firmer alliance.

Country profile, 170 AG

The figures in this section describe the Qianchan Republic in 170 AG. They are published by the Federal Bureau of Statistics, whose numbers are generally regarded as the most reliable in the world, and by the Academy of Gaoling, whose economists are regarded as the most critical.

Names

Qianchan was the name of the southern lands in the old kingdom, and the republic kept it. The word is old and its meaning is disputed: "thousand fields" in the common etymology, "the thousand-fold" or "many-voiced" in the republic's own schoolbooks, which prefer the second. Its citizens are Qianchanese, and some of them still use Fifth Nation, a title that began as an insult from Ba Sing Se and was adopted, with the Yakuya Confederation's eastern heritage, by the republic's printers. See History of Qianchan and Yakuya Confederation.

Geography

Qianchan occupies the southern and south-eastern earth lands, and is the most varied country on the continent: fertile river plains, rolling coalfields, the iron hills of the east, the wetlands of the delta and a long coastline on the southern and eastern seas. The climate is temperate to subtropical. Its great cities are Gaoling, the capital, Port Tieshan, Zaofu, home of the Beifong metalbenders, and the eastern harbors that were once Yakuya bases. It has a long land border with the Earth Kingdom, which it has not defended against anyone since 224 BG.

Government and politics

Qianchan is a federal parliamentary republic with an executive President. The Parliament has two chambers: the Senate of the States, which represents the member states equally, and the Chamber of Districts, elected by population. The President is elected by the Parliament and holds executive power with a cabinet; the courts are independent and may review federal law against the constitution that the district conventions drafted in 255 BG. Member states, among them the autonomous Zaofu region, govern police, education and land. The Southern Air Temple, which the republic preserved after the war, is an autonomous district of the airbenders.

Politics is a coalition game. The main parties are the Veterans' Union, heir of the Southern Army; the Commerce and Industry Party; the Agrarian Assemblies; and the Federal Union, whose base is in the member states. The Qin house retains seats and a symbolic place in the republic's ceremonies. No party has governed alone in modern times, and cabinets are replaced regularly, which is a source of frustration and, its supporters say, of stability. Press freedom is protected by law, and the republic's papers are among the most outspoken in the world.

Foreign relations

The republic's policy remains "we govern ourselves; we do not export governance". It is the Earth Kingdom's treaty ally, the Fire Nation's partner in research and rival in industry, and the principal sponsor of the United Republic of Nations, whose independence it helped win. It is a founder of the Concord of Nations. Its relations with the Earth Kingdom were fully normalized in 113 AG by the Treaty of Gaoling, which for the first time wrote the word "republic" into a document signed in Ba Sing Se. It keeps close ties with the Southern Water Tribe, which it armed in the war, and with the airbenders of the Southern Air Temple.

Military

Qianchan maintains about 600,000 active personnel and a militia in which every adult citizen is expected to have trained. The Army is built on engineering and armor, the Navy on submarines, and the Air Force on the aircraft that fought on the Omashu front. The Zaofu Iron Guard is the best-known elite unit. The republic's civilian fission program, Tieshan, supplies about a quarter of its electricity, and its capacity for a weapon has been a subject of treaty negotiation. Civilian control of the armed forces is strict.

Economy

Qianchan has the largest economy in the world. It is a mixed economy with a high level of private enterprise and one of the most extensive railway, port and power networks on earth. Its leading sectors are machinery, electronics, chemicals, steel, shipbuilding, finance and agricultural exports. It has a long tradition of cooperatives and of regulated markets, and its high wages and widely shared prosperity have drawn millions of workers from the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation. The currency is the kuan.

Science and technology

The Academy of Gaoling is the world's leading university, and its journals, printed freely, have been a source for every state's intelligence services since 26 BG. Qianchan leads in electronics, fission engineering, metallurgy, medicine and metalbending technology. It built the repeater (130 BG), coal engines (255 BG) and many of the technologies that the Earth Kingdom's 23 AG industrialization used.

Demographics

Qianchan has about 268 million inhabitants, a figure that includes millions of Earth Kingdom war refugees and their descendants. The language of administration is Qianchan Common; Zaofu Cant, a metalbenders' dialect, and eastern coastal speech, descended from the Yakuya Confederation's creole, are also widely spoken. The republic is secular in law, with a mixed religious life of ancestor veneration, Spirit traditions and a number of modern movements. Literacy is almost universal, and the median age is 38.

Culture

Qianchan's culture is urban, argumentative and proud of its institutions. It is known for its press, cafés, theater, mechanical engineering, cooking, and a strong tradition of debate. The memory of Qin the Great is cherished in the south, and the Academy's historians are noted for writing candidly about the republic's own record. The "citizen militia" is also a social institution: each district holds an annual muster that is part parade, part picnic.

northern_water_tribe.title: Northern Water Tribe
northern_water_tribe.html:
The larger of the two Water Tribes, centered on Agna Qel'a. Later the Kingdom of Agna Qel'a.

Capital [[Agna Qel'a]]
Population About 3,600,000 (0 AG); about 1,800,000 (July 100 AG)
Military A small elite army of riflemen and waterbenders; no navy or air force after 0 AG
War dead About 1,800,000

The Northern Water Tribe is the Water Tribe state of the North Pole, a centralized nation under a Chief and a Council of Elders, with ice-walled cities and a navy that the Empire destroyed in the first weeks of the Hundred Year War. It was historically the stronger of the two tribes, and until 40 AG remained in contact with the South.

In the Hundred Year War

The North beat back the Empire in the First Battle of Agna Qel'a (0 AG) with the weather, ice and waterbending, and was bombed periodically for the next century from the Empire's base on the far eastern pole, losing about 20% of its people by 40 AG. In the Siege of the North (13 November – 19 December 99 AG) the Empire took Agna Qel'a, with about 800,000 dead in five weeks. The Chief and most of the Council escaped on Qianchan submarines, and the occupation and scorched-earth policy cut the population to 50% by June 100 AG.

Later history

The North's unity with the South ended in the civil war of 170–174 AG, and it became the Kingdom of Agna Qel'a.

southern_water_tribe.title: Southern Water Tribe
southern_water_tribe.html:
The smaller of the two Water Tribes, a federation of chiefdoms at the South Pole. Occupied by the Empire for ninety-nine years.

Capital Taluqqriaq (Wolf Cove)
Government Federation of chiefdoms under a Council of Chieftains and Elders
Population About {{stat:pop_swt_0|n}} (0 AG); about {{stat:pop_swt_100|n}} (end of the war)
War dead About 70% of the population dead or missing

The Southern Water Tribe was the more egalitarian and the weaker of the two tribes, with ice-walled towns and many skilled waterbenders. It was the target of the Empire's most prolonged campaign of subjugation, which began a week after the Air Nomad Genocide.

Occupation and insurgency

The Empire captured the leaders in 0 AG and forced them to cooperate, and ran an occupation of forced labor, reprisals and terror. The Southern insurgency raided Imperial convoys and industry for forty years. The last of the early uprisings (29 AG) left the South at 75% of its pre-war population, and by 99 AG, when the waterbenders had dwindled to a handful, it was about 50%. The Southern Uprising of 99 AG was crushed, and many survivors were conscripted or sent to work in the colonies. By the end of the war about 70% of the pre-war population was dead or missing.

Leaders

Chief Hakoda led the Southern resistance in 99 AG. The capital's name, Taluqqriaq, is the Water Tribe name for Wolf Cove, "the wolf cave."

air_nomads.title: Air Nomads
air_nomads.html:
A pacifist, stateless people of the four Air Temples, destroyed in the Air Nomad Genocide.

Homeland The four Air Temples and their island chains and mountains, with communities across the world
Population About {{stat:pop_an_0|n}} (0 AG)
Fate Almost entirely killed, 0–20 AG
Survivors About 300–400 people with airbending in 99 AG, deep in Qianchan or the Earth Kingdom

The Air Nomads were a pacifist people without a state or army, who lived in the four Air Temples and in communities across the Earth Kingdom, the Water Tribe lands and the Yanakawan coast. Most were non-benders. The Empire of Tajisaki, which wanted to stop the next Avatar from being born among them, destroyed them in the Air Nomad Genocide. The Imperial Constitution declared that the Air Nomads "ceased to constitute a distinct people" and prohibited their bending and spiritual practices (Art. 45).

The only known airbender in public was the Avatar, Aang. The several hundred surviving airbenders mostly did not know what they were, or hid it. After the war, Qianchan preserved the Southern Air Temple and gave the airbenders autonomy.

The United Republic of Nations, commonly known as the United Republics, is a council republic on the Yanakawan Peninsula, formed in 105 AG from the Fire Nation's former colonies. In 170 AG it is the third-largest economy in the world and the most cosmopolitan state in it, with {{stat:urn_fb_share}} of its people born abroad.

Current affairs, 170 AG

Inside the republic

  • The representation dispute. The Republic Council has six seats: one each for Fire, Earth and Air, two for Water (the Northern and Southern Tribes) and one for Non-Benders. Earth benders are {{stat:urn_bp_earth}} of the population but hold one seat in six. Non-benders ({{stat:urn_bp_non}}) hold one, and the {{stat:urn_b_air|n}} air benders hold one. The Progressives want seats weighted by population, while the Servants of the Republic defend the founding settlement that gave every people a seat.
  • A republic of newcomers. {{stat:urn_fb_total|n}} residents, {{stat:urn_fb_share}} of the population, were born abroad, and {{stat:urn_imm_total}} people have immigrated since 0 AG. Citizenship, language and housing for newcomers dominate debate in the National Assembly.
  • Growth strain. The population roughly doubled from {{stat:pop_urn_125|m}} in 125 AG to about {{stat:pop_urn_170|m}} in 170 AG, while output per person rose from {{stat:gdppc_urn_125}} to {{stat:gdppc_urn_170}}. Cities, rail and housing are the main budget fights.
  • The Equalists. A movement against benders, declared a terrorist organization in 170 AG after it attacked the probending arena in Republic City. Its leader is a former Harmonist. See Equalists.

Geopolitical decisions

  • The Water Tribe split. {{stat:urn_fb_wt|n}} residents were born in the two Water Tribes. As the unity of North and South begins to break down in the civil war of 170–174 AG, the Council has refused to recognize either side and keeps its ports and reception centers open to refugees.
  • The Fire Nation. Relations are close and tense. {{stat:urn_fb_taj|n}} residents were born there, Tajisakian is an official language and trade is heavy, but veterans still remember the Eastern Territories. The Council wants commerce without political alignment.
  • Qianchan. Qianchan sponsored the republic's independence and supplied its rebels with surplus weapons. It is the republic's closest partner, but the Council has avoided a formal alliance with any power.
  • The Earth Kingdom. The republic sits on land the kingdom lost. Relations are cool and respectful, and the {{stat:urn_fb_ek|n}} residents born in the Earth Confederation are its largest foreign-born group ({{stat:urn_fbp_ek}}).
  • The airbenders. The republic keeps a Council seat for the Air Nomads, which it treats as a debt of the war, although the survivors are few.

Government and politics

  • Executive: the Republic Council has six members (one Fire, one Earth, two Water, one Air and one Non-Bender seat), elected by the National Assembly for staggered six-year terms (two terms maximum). The Council elects a President among its members; in 170 AG it is Tarrlok, the Northern Water councillor. The Council of 170 AG: Tarrlok, Viku (Southern Water), Ilama (Fire), Zi (Earth), Tenzin (Air), Ujo (Non-Bender). A reform approved 4–2 on 18 July 170 AG replaces the Council with a president and adds a Senate (see Raiko).
  • Legislature: the National Assembly is elected from single-member constituencies for four-year terms (three consecutive terms maximum).
  • Judiciary: the Supreme Court has nine justices serving twelve-year terms.
  • Political parties: Servants of the Republic, Progressives, Federalists and the Nationalist Union.
  • Divisions: eight Regions and one Special Administrative Capital (the National Capital Region). Regions are divided into prefectures.

Military

The armed forces have three branches: the United Republic Navy, the United Republic Army and the United Republic Airforce.

Economy

The republic's economy is about {{stat:gdp_urn_170}}, behind Qianchan ({{stat:gdp_qc_170}}) and the Fire Nation ({{stat:gdp_fn_170}}) and ahead of the Earth Kingdom ({{stat:gdp_ek_170}}). The currency is the yuan, divided into 100 fen.

Geography

The main types of relief are coastal plains, grasslands, forests and mountains or hills.


Main types of relief.

History

The United Republic of Nations was established in 105 AG on the Yanakawan Peninsula following the [[hundred_year_war|Hundred Year War]] and the subsequent Decade of revolutions. The peninsula, once home to numerous Fire Nation colonies and settlements within territories claimed by the [[earth_kingdom|Earth Confederation]], became the center of a protracted struggle over sovereignty, colonial rule and national self-determination. Its Provisional Council sat at [[qinglan_port|Qinglan Port]] during the [[yanakawan_war_of_independence|War of Independence]].

The Hundred Year War, also known as the Great War, devastated the world, claimed an estimated {{stat:hyw_deaths}} lives, and brought the [[air_nomads|Air Nomads]] to the brink of extinction. Following the [[Treaty of Ba Sing Se]], the defeated Empire of Tajisaki faced the question of whether to retain, relinquish or negotiate the future of its colonies, while diplomats from Ba Sing Se pressed for the restoration of occupied territories and the resolution of competing territorial claims. The peninsula's diverse population and complex colonial history ultimately made independence the preferred solution, recognized by the [[treaty_of_qinglan|Treaty of Qinglan]] and culminating in the Declaration of Union in 105 AG.

The new republic adopted a council-based system of government, bringing together representatives of its constituent communities to prevent renewed conflict and establish a common political order. Its early years were marked by economic disruption, competing national interests, and the difficult task of integrating former colonial administrations and rival armed factions. Over subsequent decades, reconstruction, migration and industrial development transformed the United Republics into a cosmopolitan state whose population included people from across the western and eastern continents. Firebenders and earthbenders formed the largest bending communities, while nonbenders and waterbenders constituted significant minorities. Despite its emergence as a major center of commerce and cultural exchange, the republic's founding compromises and the social inequalities inherited from the colonial era continued to shape its politics long after independence.

sozin.title: Sozin
sozin.html:
Fire Lord of the Empire of Tajisaki and the instigator of the Hundred Year War.

Reign Before 0 AG – 20 AG
Died 20 AG
Known for The Air Nomad Genocide; the plan to subjugate the Water Tribes

Sozin was the Fire Lord who began the Hundred Year War. He was a friend of Avatar Roku, who refused to help him expand his empire and spared him in 37 BG. When Roku died on Island Jezhi in 12 BG, Sozin, who could have helped him, left him to die. He then militarized the Fire Nation for twelve years, knowing that the next Avatar would be born among the Air Nomads.

In 0 AG he used the return of the comet to destroy the Air Nomads, and a week later ordered the Water Tribes subjugated and worked to death, an order that his successors carried out for a hundred years. He sought the surviving Avatar until his death in 20 AG. His successor, Azulon, began the Sōen program in 47 AG.

azulon.title: Azulon
azulon.html:
Fire Lord of the Empire of Tajisaki, 20–97 AG. Murdered by his son Ozai.

Reign 20 AG – 97 AG
Died 10 June 97 AG (poisoned)
Heir Ozai
Known for The Sōen program; the Siege of Ba Sing Se; the Ash Directive

Azulon succeeded Sozin in 20 AG and ruled for 77 years of the Hundred Year War. He continued the subjugation of the Water Tribes, ordered the Sōen program in 47 AG, backed General Iroh's Si Wong Offensive and the Siege of Ba Sing Se, and, after the failure of the siege and the death of Iroh's son Lu Ten, lost faith in Iroh. In the siege he issued the Ash Directive to raze Ba Sing Se, which Iroh opposed.

On 10 June 97 AG Azulon was poisoned at dinner and died in his sleep. The Court blamed Qianchan agents, and the kitchen staff were executed, but the poisoning had been arranged by his younger son Ozai, which was established only after the civil war.

ozai.title: Ozai
ozai.html:
Fire Lord of the Empire of Tajisaki, 97–100 AG, and self-proclaimed Tentei, the Emperor of the Sky.

Reign 24 June 97 AG – 18 July 100 AG
Died 18 July 100 AG, Qinglan Port (killed by Aang)
Titles Fire Lord; Tentei (17 July 100 AG)
Heir Azula (disputed)

Ozai came to the throne after poisoning his father Azulon in 97 AG. He pardoned Rear Admiral Yueya and Captain Zhao in July 97, which began the Pardon Crisis, and polarized the Empire against his opponents, led by Iroh. In 99 AG he launched the combined operation against both poles, to eradicate the Water Tribes so that no new Avatar could rise.

In July 100 AG he went to Qinglan Port to oversee the Sōen, personally supplied the trigger input to fire it at Ba Sing Se on 17 July, and proclaimed himself Tentei. The next day, caught off guard by the allied bombardment, he was killed by the Avatar in the Avatar State, with a stone lance through both lungs, 23 minutes after the first shells fell. His death, announced on the high command radio, collapsed the Empire's central authority.

azula.title: Azula
azula.html:
Daughter of Ozai. The Court's Fire Lord, 25 July 100 AG – 9 May 118 AG.

Reign Claimed the throne 25 July 100 AG
Died 9 May 118 AG (killed by Zuko in the Duel of the Palace)
Faction The Court (Ozai loyalists)

Azula was named Ozai's successor in a sealed designation produced by the General Staff Directorate, and was confirmed in a ceremony on 25 July 100 AG, after the army rigged the succession over the Diet's resolution for Zuko. Her right to the throne was equal to her brother's, but he had the backing of the Diet and the people, and both claimed to be Fire Lord until the Duel of the Palace. She led the Court Government in the Fire Nation Civil War, with the General Staff, the Ministry of Truth, the Flame Guard and the cultists who revered her father, and continued a naval war against Yanakawa until 110 AG.

By 118 AG, with the Court's forces broken, she called her brother to a duel under the Way of the Warrior, blamed him for everything, and used lightning in breach of its rules. Zuko redirected it and beheaded her.

zuko.title: Zuko
zuko.html:
Prince of the Empire of Tajisaki, leader of the Royalists and Fire Lord, 118–168 AG.

Reign 118 AG – 168 AG
Faction The Royalists (Restoration Government)
Successor His daughter Izumi (abdicated 168 AG)

Zuko was the popular heir whom the Diet wanted as Fire Lord in July 100 AG. His claim rested on the legitimacy that the Diet and the people gave him, against a sister whose right to the throne was equal to his, and the two spent eighteen years disputing which of them was the Fire Lord. After the rigged succession for Azula, he left Caldera City on 5 August, and with his uncle Iroh led the Restoration Government at Shu Jing in the Fire Nation Civil War, supported by Qianchan supplies through the Western Air Temple island chain. Royalist propaganda later credited him with Ozai's defeat. He killed Azula in the Duel of the Palace on 9 May 118 AG and was crowned Fire Lord later that year. At his coronation an assassin was shot before he could fire.

His reign (118–168 AG) was a 50-year rebuilding of the devastated archipelago, with the economic recovery of 140 AG. In 168 AG, ill from a suspected poisoning, he abdicated to his daughter Izumi.

iroh.title: Iroh
iroh.html:
General of the Empire of Tajisaki, architect of the Si Wong Offensive and the Ba Sing Se siege, later the opposition leader.

Rank General; Field Marshal (94–97 AG); retired 98 AG
Son Lu Ten (killed 25 November 96 AG)
Died 9 March 101 AG, Shu Jing (Salvationist bomb)

Iroh was the General Staff Directorate's Planning Director, who designed Plan Yellow and the Si Wong Offensive (80–88 AG), and in 94 AG became Field Marshal for the Siege of Ba Sing Se. His son Lu Ten was killed in the Palace on 25 November 96 AG, and Iroh opposed the Ash Directive to raze the city. He was demoted to General after the siege.

After Ozai's accession and the Pardon Crisis, he became the leader of the opposition. He addressed the Veterans' Assembly in January 98 AG, was forced to retire later that year, and was given a seat in the Diet. In August 100 AG he joined his nephew Zuko, as the Royalists' Chief of Staff, brought defecting garrisons over, and opened the channel to Qianchan. On 9 March 101 AG a Salvationist bomb in a conference hall at Shu Jing killed him and ten others, and the Royalists made him their martyr.

Legacy: the martyr of Shu Jing

Iroh is remembered in the Fire Nation as a martyr. He was the general who had opposed the Ash Directive, the veteran who had stood against the Fire Lord in the Pardon Crisis, and the uncle who left Caldera with Zuko when the Court seized the throne, and he was killed on 9 March 101 AG by the bomb of the Salvationists, at the table where the Royalists were seeking an agreement with Qianchan. The Royalists used his death to sustain their cause through the harshest years of the war, and Zuko, who named his own reign a restoration, held to the principles of his uncle for the remainder of his life.

lu_ten.title: Lu Ten
lu_ten.html:
Known in the Imperial press as the People's Prince (民の王子, Tami no Ōji).

Rank Lieutenant (87 AG); Captain, Armored Corps (89 AG); Lieutenant Colonel (96 AG)
Family House of the Fire Lord. Son of General Iroh; grandson of Fire Lord Azulon; nephew of Prince Ozai
Education Imperial Military Academy (graduated 87 AG)
Service Si Wong Offensive (final action, 88 AG); Jasmine Island (90 AG); Siege of Ba Sing Se (96 AG)
Decorations Order of the Golden Flame (88 AG)
Died 25 November 96 AG, Ba Sing Se
Known for The Battle of the Rail Cut; stopping the Jasmine Island Mutiny; the Address on Conduct (90 AG)

Lu Ten was an officer of the Imperial Army and the only son of General Iroh, the Directorate's Planning Director and the architect of the Si Wong Offensive. He was the grandson of Fire Lord Azulon, and third in the line of succession after his father and his uncle Prince Ozai. He was the best-known serving officer of the Imperial family. A decorated tank officer, he became a public figure in 90 AG, when he refused to take part in the destruction of Jasmine Island by Rear Admiral Yueya, gave evidence against her at her court-martial, and then submitted a written appeal to the Fire Lord and the Imperial Diet that called for reforms against abuse of authority in the armed forces. It was the first time a member of the dynasty had publicly criticized the military's own conduct. The Address made him a political figure as well as a popular one, and it set the court, the General Staff Directorate and the Diet's reformers against each other on a question that had not previously been debated in public.

Early life

Lu Ten was born in the capital to Iroh and his wife, and raised in a household that combined the court and the General Staff. His father was away on campaign for much of his childhood. Unlike his cousins, who were educated at court, he was sent at the usual age to the Imperial Military Academy. Contemporary accounts describe him as an able but unremarkable student who was popular with his classmates, many of them sons of provincial officers and colonial families, and who had an unusual habit of eating in the cadet mess and not at the instructors' table.

Military career

Academy and Armored Corps

Lu Ten graduated as a lieutenant in 87 AG and chose the Armored Corps, a branch that the General Staff regarded as the future of the war and that suffered heavy losses. The choice was widely read as a decision to serve in the line and not on his father's staff, and Iroh is reported to have been displeased at the lack of consultation.

Si Wong

Lu Ten was posted to the Si Wong front a few months before the Offensive ended. He commanded a platoon of four medium tanks. By then the Empire held Tongba and the desert's road and rail corridor, and the front was a fortified line on the desert's eastern edge. The last major action of Plan Yellow was fought there in August 88 AG, when the Coalition counter-attacked the rail cut that anchored the Imperial line.

Lu Ten's platoon was attached to an infantry company that was cut off in the first hours of the attack. Imperial accounts say that he held the cut with his four tanks for most of a day, that two of them were lost, and that he went back on foot under fire to recover their crews. The platoon helped to cover the infantry's withdrawal, and the line held. He received the Order of the Golden Flame, and the Offensive ended five days later.

The Imperial press made much of the fact that he had fought in the offensive his father had planned. His critics, mainly in the Navy, noted that he had done so at the lowest officer rank, and that a prince had more protection than most lieutenants. Accounts by the men of his platoon say that he shared their rations, avoided the officers' mess and wrote letters for the wounded. Veterans' papers in the colonies printed these stories first, and the capital's press followed. After the battle he also submitted a report on looting by rear-area supply units in the occupied desert towns, which the Directorate filed without action.

Promotion and posting (88–90 AG)

Lu Ten was promoted to captain in 89 AG and posted to the Armored Corps' staff in the western command. In early 90 AG he was temporarily attached, as an Army liaison, to the Jasmine Island garrison, one of the Army's smaller commitments in the western island chain.

Public image

By 90 AG Lu Ten was the most popular member of the dynasty. He was popular for several reasons. He had fought in the ranks, and veterans said so. His family was known for its closeness to the army and its distance from the court. Unlike his uncle Ozai, who was associated with the court's hardliners, he spoke plainly and did not hide his opinions. In the colonies, where the Imperial family was a distant and often resented institution, his visits to veterans' associations were widely reported, and the phrase "the People's Prince" originated in the colonial press. His critics, mainly in the Navy and the court, called the title a creation of newspapers, and said that a prince who could be so popular with the troops was a political risk.

Jasmine Island incident

Background

Jasmine Island is a small Imperial possession in the western island chain, known for its tea and golden jasmine, governed by a three-member island council under Imperial supervision, with a small Army garrison and a local constabulary known as the protectors. It had no history of unrest. Rear Admiral Yueya commanded a Navy squadron in the western islands and had petitioned, in early 90 AG, for the post of garrison commander. The petition was denied, since the post was an Army one, and officers who served with her described her as obsessed with the island.

The attack

On the night of 7 June 90 AG, the island's New Moon Celebration, Yueya took her squadron, a battlecruiser and two destroyers, to the island and declared it in rebellion. There was no rebellion. Her second-in-command, Captain Zhao, planted explosive charges in the market square under the Monument to Peace, which fell onto the council chambers and killed two of the island's three councillors and a large part of the crowd. Her landing parties then burned the town and the fields.

Lu Ten's refusal

Lu Ten, who had landed with the Army company in the second wave, found no rebels, only burning houses and civilians. He stopped his men from taking part and ordered them to help with the fire-fighting and evacuation, and he met Lieutenant Akataa and the garrison's survivors, who had been fighting in the streets. He went to Yueya on the quay and demanded an end to the attack. She refused and ordered it widened, and at about 01:50 he sent his report to the Western Command from the company's radio.

The brig and the harbor

The killing grew through the night. Yueya's marines seized the battlecruiser, arrested its captain, executive officer and about 60 sailors who had refused to fire on the island, and locked them in the brig, and the ship's guns then shelled the refugees on the hillside and the market district. Near 04:30 the imprisoned sailors blew their way out of the brig with the ship's demolition charges, fought up three decks to the bridge, and retook it. At dawn Lu Ten, with the Army detachment, the garrison and the Navy officers who had refused to follow her, called on the mutineers to surrender, and arrested Yueya on her destroyer's bridge. About 2,000 civilians had been killed, and about half the main settlement and 80% of the island's fields were destroyed. Zhao's conduct after the first assault is unclear.

Court-martial

Lu Ten gave evidence against Yueya to the Directorate, and demanded a trial. She was court-martialed by a joint Army and Navy panel in the summer of 90 AG, convicted of exceeding her orders, of deceiving the War Council and of the unlawful killing of Imperial subjects, and sentenced to imprisonment. Zhao was tried with her and convicted on lesser charges. He argued that he had followed orders, and he was reduced in rank. The Navy resisted the verdict, and tried to limit the sentence by arguing that Yueya's actions were an unfortunate excess of zeal in wartime. It did not accept the account of the operation until the island's own witnesses had been heard.

Jasmine Island was placed under a civilian administrator, and the Directorate granted a program of aid and reconstruction. The island council, which had lost two members, was allowed to hold new elections.

The Address on Conduct

The trial did not satisfy Lu Ten. In the autumn of 90 AG he submitted a written appeal, the Address on Conduct, to Fire Lord Azulon and the Imperial Diet. It argued that Jasmine Island was not an exception. The war had given officers wide latitude, and the Empire's institutions had no means of checking them; Yueya had been stopped by chance, because an Army captain had been in the right place. It asked that "savages" not be allowed to taint the image of the Imperial military, by which Lu Ten meant officers and soldiers who used the Empire's uniform for private revenge or for cruelty, and it said that an army that burned its own subjects had lost the purpose it was fighting for. It proposed:

  • independent military tribunals that are not under the control of the service chiefs;
  • a requirement that any declaration of martial law or emergency be reported to the Directorate and the Diet within days, and that operations beyond their orders be halted;
  • legal protection for civilians in Imperial and occupied territory;
  • the prosecution of abuses of authority regardless of rank;
  • a clearer division between the Army and Navy in garrison appointments.

Reception

The Address was received very differently in different places. Reformers in the Diet, who had been a minority for years, welcomed it, and a group of colonial delegates asked that it be debated in full. The press and the veterans' papers praised it, and it was read aloud in several colonial cities. Public opinion in the capital and the colonies is strongly in Lu Ten's favor.

Azulon's court did not answer it directly. The Fire Lord could not punish a decorated grandson, and he did not endorse the proposals. The General Staff Directorate opposed independent tribunals as a threat to command authority, and the Navy was openly hostile. Prince Ozai praised the court-martial but described the proposed tribunals as "an insult to those who command", and aligned himself with the court's hardliners. Iroh has not spoken publicly in support of his son's proposals, though it is widely assumed that he approves. Observers in the capital note that the Address has put the dynasty's two lines on opposite sides of a public question for the first time.

Political views

Lu Ten's published views, so far, are limited to the Address. They show a preoccupation with accountability, and a belief that the military's legitimacy depends on its conduct. He has not yet taken a public position on the war's conduct beyond this, on colonial representation in the Diet, or on conscription.

Personal life

Lu Ten is unmarried. He is reported to be close to his father, and he is known to be a tea drinker, a habit that the press has linked to the tea ceremony the islanders offered him after the incident.

Later life and death (91–96 AG)

After the trial Lu Ten became the center of a reform movement in the Diet and among veterans, and the Navy and the General Staff Directorate watched him. He was promoted to lieutenant colonel and in 95 AG took command of a battalion of Breaker power armor. In 96 AG he served under his father, the Field Marshal, in the Siege of Ba Sing Se. In November his battalion was among the assault battalions that took the Inner City and the Palace. After the Imperial forces had held the Palace and the Forbidden City for a week, a charge detonated in the underground galleries beneath them, and on 25 November 96 AG he was killed.

Legacy

His death, and the reprisals that followed, hardened his father against the siege. Azulon, who had lost faith in Iroh, ordered the city razed in the Ash Directive, which Iroh opposed, and demoted him. The Address on Conduct, which was Lu Ten's only published statement, became the program of the reformers. It was the standard that the Diet's opposition used against Ozai's pardon of Yueya and Zhao in 97 AG, which began the Pardon Crisis, and Iroh, who had not spoken in support of it, became its leader. The reformers who followed Iroh and Zuko in the Fire Nation Civil War remembered him as the People's Prince.

Honours

  • Order of the Golden Flame (88 AG)

aang.title: Aang
aang.html:
The Avatar, the last known airbender, and the killer of Ozai.

Nation Air Nomads (Southern Air Temple)
Found Late November 99 AG, in the South Pole
Known for Killing Fire Lord Ozai at Qinglan Port, 18 July 100 AG

Aang was born at the Southern Air Temple and was frozen at the time of the genocide. Southern guerrillas found him in the ice near Taluqqriaq in late November 99 AG, during the Southern Uprising, and he escaped to Qianchan as the capital fell. In July 100 AG he joined the allied attack on Qinglan Port and, in the Avatar State, killed Fire Lord Ozai with a stone lance through both lungs. He was unconscious for two days. After the war he helped the United Republic of Nations rebuild. He died in about 153 AG, and the Avatar cycle passed to the Southern Water Tribe as Korra.

qin_the_great.title: Qin the Great
qin_the_great.html:
Also known as Chin the Conqueror. A lord of the south who tried to reform the authority of Ba Sing Se. Killed in 270 BG.

Seat Gaoling
Allies Avatar Kyoshi; the King of Omashu; the Lord of Yu Dao; the lords of Tongshui
Died 270 BG, outside the walls of Ba Sing Se (dishonorable duel)
Dynasty The Qin Dynasty (his heirs)

Qin the Great was a southern lord who rose in the chaos of the late Warring States, and wanted to reform the absolute authority of the Earth King in Ba Sing Se. With the Avatar Kyoshi, the King of Omashu and the Lord of Yu Dao, he conquered the northwest and brought the rest of the continent, apart from Ba Sing Se and Kyoshi's peninsula, under his banner. In 270 BG, at the city's outer walls, he fought a duel with the Earth King. The king cheated, with hidden crossbowmen and a poisoned blade, and Qin was killed, although he mortally wounded the king. Kyoshi then went into the Inner City and forced the reforms of the royal court.

His death caused a power vacuum. His heirs ruled as the Qin Dynasty, which the southern lands overthrew in the War of Liberation (270–255 BG). The revolt gave the Qianchan Republic its independence. The Qin Dynasty collapsed in famine in 255 BG, and Ba Sing Se, under Bao Kun, took advantage of it.

kyoshi.title: Kyoshi
kyoshi.html:
The Avatar of the Earth Kingdom's 3rd-century BG upheavals, a protector of the reform of Ba Sing Se.

Home Kyoshi Island (a peninsula of the Earth Kingdom)
Notable acts Allied with Qin the Great; reformed the royal court of Ba Sing Se (270 BG); the peasant uprising settlement

Kyoshi was an Avatar from the Earth Kingdom, who lived in the age of the Warring States. She thought Qin the Great's cause of reforming Ba Sing Se just, and joined his coalition. When Qin was killed outside the walls in 270 BG, in a duel in which the Earth King cheated, she went into the Inner City, and forced the royal court to accept a written constitution and to treat the peasants fairly, which ended a peasant uprising in the city. She spent the rest of her life keeping the peace between the nations and between the fifty-five states of the Earth Kingdom. Her warrior order, the Kyoshi Warriors, remained a power on her island. Her insistence on defending the Earth King's court from its own people while reforming it was criticized by the Qianchan republicans, who did not believe in the monarchy at all.

kuei.title: Kuei
kuei.html:
The 52nd Earth King, 81 AG onward.

Born About 77 AG
Crowned About 81 AG, aged four
Residence Ba Sing Se

Kuei became Earth King as a four-year-old after the Dai Li murdered his father, and grew up shut away from the war under the regency of Long Feng. The Siege of Ba Sing Se (96–97 AG) opened his eyes. After the siege he began to centralize command, which provoked the Dai Li's coup attempt of 98 AG. He put it down, ended the regency, and by 99 AG was running the war from Ba Sing Se on the Northern Front. He was in the Palace's command bunker when the Sōen struck in July 100 AG.

Death

Kuei died in 153 AG, aged about seventy-six. The court announced that he had died peacefully in his sleep. In fact his daughter Hou-Ting had him killed; the court physician who signed the certificate left the palace and was not seen again. He had cleaned up the corruption of the war years, given all adults the vote in 150 AG and left a larger and richer kingdom, and she reversed his reforms at once.
