caldera_city.title: Caldera City
caldera_city.html:
Capital of the Empire of Tajisaki and the Fire Nation's largest city.

Country Empire of Tajisaki (Fire Nation)
Island Capital Island
Settled Before 4440 BG; the seat of the Fire Lords since the unification, about 4440 BG
Population About 9.8 million in the city proper and about 21 million in the metropolitan area (170 AG estimate)
Seat of The Fire Lord, the Imperial Diet, the Cabinet, the General Staff Directorate and the principal base of the Imperial Navy
Sites The Imperial Palace; the Dragonbone Catacombs; the Academy of Caldera; Caldera Harbor; the Foundry Quarter; the Caldera Coastal Battery Complex (main Sōen array)
Sieges and battles See the table below, from the Taking of the Harbor (c. 4440 BG) to the Siege of Caldera (117–118 AG)

Caldera City is the capital of the Fire Nation. It stands on Capital Island around a flooded volcanic crater that forms its harbor, and it has been the seat of the Fire Lords since the unification of the islands about 4440 BG. It is the home of the Imperial Palace, the Diet, the Cabinet and the General Staff, and the largest industrial and naval base of the state. In its recorded history it has fallen to an attacking army only a few times, and almost always to Fire Nationals.

Setting

The city was built on the rim and floor of a drowned caldera, the crater of an old volcano whose seaward wall collapsed in prehistory. The crater is now Caldera Harbor, a deep, sheltered anchorage about eleven kilometers across, with a single channel to the sea, the Throat, which is less than a kilometer wide and has been fortified since the first Fire Lords. The Imperial Palace stands on the northern rim, above the harbor, in a walled district of its own, with the Dragonbone Catacombs, the tombs of the Fire Lords, cut into the rock beneath it.

The rest of the city climbs the rim in terraces and spreads down the outer slopes to the plain. It is divided into numbered wards. The inner wards (1 to 3) hold the government and the old houses, the middle wards (4 to 9) hold the Academy of Caldera, the markets and the middle class, and the outer wards, the Foundry Quarter and the Lower Docks, hold the factories, the rail yards and most of the working population. Hot springs and geothermal vents under the crater supply the city with heat, and since 150 AG a growing share of its electricity.

The Academy of Caldera argues that the name of the Tajisaki clan, and so of the whole realm, was taken from this harbor and the valley behind it, the place where the clan first held land, and not the other way round. The claim is disputed, but it is the reason that the Fire Lords have always held the city to be the place where the realm began.

History

The harbor lords (before 4440 BG)

The first settlements around the crater were the camps of fishermen and obsidian traders, and by the Warring States Era they had grown into a walled harbor town under a line of harbor lords who levied tolls on all shipping that used the Throat. The harbor was the richest and the most contested prize of Capital Island. According to the Sages' records, its lords were overthrown or murdered eleven times in four centuries.

The unification (c. 4440 BG)

The Tajisaki clan took the harbor in about 4440 BG after a two-year campaign, the Taking of the Harbor, that ended when the clan's war fleet forced the Throat at night with chained fire-ships and landed beneath the rim. Its leader was crowned first Fire Lord in the town the same year, and he chose the harbor town for his seat. The Palace was begun on the northern rim, and the Sages began to keep the Fire Lords' tombs in the Dragonbone Catacombs. The three-sided settlement among the clan, the Sages and the harbor lords was signed in the town, and gave the city a standing as the seat of the realm that it has never lost.

The long strife (4440–300 BG)

For more than four thousand years the city was the stage of the feuds of the thirteen houses. Each house kept a fortified compound on the rim and a private guard. The city was the scene of the Night of Nine Gates (about 3550 BG), in which a cadet house opened the rim gates to its own household troops and murdered two Fire Lords in one night, and of the Grey Fever siege (1214–1213 BG), when the Fire Lord of the time sealed the city to stop a plague and starved its poor wards for eleven months, which caused riots in which several thousand people died. In the Camellia-Peony War (c. 312–295 BG), the Battle of the Crater Rim (about 297 BG) put the Peony houses' forces on the northern rim for a summer, and the Camellia houses' fleet in the harbor. Neither side could dislodge the other, and the city was saved from a general burning only by the end of the war.

The end of the clans and the industrial city (295–12 BG)

After 295 BG the throne took away the houses' private guards and demolished the compounds on the rim, which is why the northern terraces are now parkland and the Academy Quarter has so many open courts. The city grew with the first engine (c. 500 BG) and the Industrial Revolution (from c. 290 BG), and gained its Foundry Quarter, its rail terminals and its first great shipyards. The last of the clan risings, early in the reign of Sozin, ended at the Cinder Gate in about 40 BG. General Oraso Eiko's army, with armored trains and artillery, broke the rebels' camp at the western foot of the city in a single day, and the revolt ended before it reached the Palace. The first aircraft in the Fire Nation flew over the harbor in 27 BG.

The capital of the Empire (12 BG – 100 AG)

Under Sozin the Palace district was walled and enlarged, and Caldera became the seat of the General Staff Directorate and the Imperial Research Bureau. The war was run from the city: Sozin died there in 20 AG, and Azulon founded the Sōen Program in 47 AG, and its main array was built in the Caldera Coastal Battery Complex on the seaward side of the crater. The anniversary of the comet is still kept in silence, and the Day of Ash is a day of mourning.

The city was never attacked during the first sixty years of the war, but it was raided once. On the night of 14 March 61 AG, Qianchan submarines passed the Throat behind a returning supply convoy and fired on the fleet anchorage in the Raid on Caldera Harbor. Two cruisers and a fleet oiler were sunk and about 640 sailors were killed before the submarines were found and sunk by the harbor's boom nets and depth charges. The raid did not change the course of the war, but it led to the first great expansion of the Coastal Battery Complex and the harbor boom.

Two later events in the Palace district defined the Empire's politics. Ozai was crowned on 24 June 97 AG, a few days after Azulon's death, and the Pardon Crisis of 97–99 AG set the Diet, the army and the Court against one another in the city's streets. In early 100 AG, Ozai gave control of the Kanbukyoku and of the city's administration to Azula.

The succession crisis (July–August 100 AG)

After Ozai died at Qinglan Port on 18 July 100 AG, the city was the stage of the succession crisis. Large demonstrations in the wards supported the confirmation of Zuko on 22 July. Troops took the Privy Council's chamber and arrested seven councillors between 23 and 25 July, and about 210 people were killed in the clashes. Azula was confirmed on 25 July. On 4 August, shooting broke out in the galleries of the Diet's House of Representatives, which had met in defiance of the Court, and killed 31 people. Zuko left the city on 5 August, and the Diet was dissolved on 8 August.

The Civil War and the siege (100–118 AG)

For the first seventeen years of the Fire Nation Civil War, Caldera was the Court's capital. The Court held the city and the western heartland, while the Royalists held Shu Jing and the east. The Court was invited to the Treaty of Qinglan in 105 AG and did not come. In 113 AG the city was hit for the first time by a ballistic missile: a Ryuusei-B2 that the Salvationists had captured in 109 AG fell in the Foundry Quarter and killed about 1,900 people. It was the first use of a ballistic missile on a city of the Fire Nation.

The Siege of Caldera began in 117 AG, when the Salvationists, who had broken with the Court in 116 AG, closed on the city from the west, and Royalist armies took the outer wards. It lasted about nine months and killed about 260,000 people, most of them civilians. The Royalists took the Foundry Quarter and the Lower Docks first, the Salvationists took the western rim, and the Court's defenders were driven back to the Palace district, with the Flame Guard, the remnants of the Ministry of Truth and the cultists of Ozai. About 18,000 died in the fighting for the Palace district alone. The war ended in the courtyard of the Palace on 9 May 118 AG, in the Duel of the Palace, in which Zuko killed Azula.

Reconstruction and the reign of Zuko (118–168 AG)

Zuko was crowned Fire Lord later in 118 AG, and the city was rebuilt over the next fifteen years. The Diet was restored in 119 AG under the Imperial Constitution, and the Caldera Accord of 121 AG, a settlement among the Fire Nation, the Earth Kingdom and Qianchan whose terms the wiki has not yet written, was signed in the Palace. The Diet building was rebuilt on its old site, and the galleries where the 31 died are now a memorial. In the 130s AG the first long-range rockets and satellites were launched from Capital Island, and in 166 AG the first wide-body jet landed at the new Caldera Airport. Zuko's reign ended in 168 AG, and he was buried in the Dragonbone Catacombs after a state funeral.

Caldera in 170 AG

The city is the capital of a state that is changing. Fire Lord Izumi has reigned since 168 AG, and Prime Minister Ryoko Sato's Cabinet governs with the Diet. The Restoration Party, the Veterans' League and the Ember Greens compete over reconstruction, the military budget and the use of geothermal and fission power. The report of the Commission on Imperial Conduct is still the subject of the debate about the army and the throne.

The city is the Fire Nation's financial, shipbuilding and electronics center, and it handles about a third of the state's overseas trade. Its working-class outer wards, rebuilt after the siege, are the numbered districts where the films of the war years were shown, among them Flame in Her Heart in the third and fifth. The Coastal Battery Complex has been disarmed, and its capacitor halls are closed to the public. The Academy of Caldera is the oldest university of the Fire Nation, and its philologists and historians are the main authorities on the realm's earliest history.

It fields the Tiejia-III, Qianchan's counterpart to the Breaker. Zaofu-trained metalbenders attached to Qianchan forces helped civilian conscripts drive the Empire from the Palace in Ba Sing Se in November 96 AG, and the Iron Guard Detachment led the attack on the Imperial armor line at Qinglan Port on 18 July 100 AG.

The Imperial Navy destroyed the combined Water Tribe fleets in the first weeks of the war and held naval superiority alone until 30 AG, when its first engagement with the Qianchan Navy, at the Western Air Temple Waters, was a draw. It blockaded the Earth Kingdom's coasts and Omashu's supply route, and its submarine war with Qianchan was one of the long conflicts of the middle war. Its carrier force was driven onto the defensive by Qianchan's submarines. In 90 AG, its Rear Admiral Yueya destroyed Jasmine Island, and its sailors who broke out of a battlecruiser's brig helped stop her. In the Siege of the North (99 AG) its Northern Fleet, with icebreakers, took Agna Qel'a. The Navy split by squadron in the Fire Nation Civil War in November 100 AG.

salvationists.title: Salvationists
salvationists.html:
A radical movement of war veterans, the third party in the Fire Nation Civil War.

Active 100 AG – 120 AG
Base Veterans of the non-bender Kern infantry; radicals
Later Thunderbolt sect (169 AG); the Harmonists and the Collective grew from its exiles and its ideas

The Salvationists began as veterans' committees in the Court's own army. They took over most of its field army from within between 107 and 113 AG, seized the IRB's western complex and its Ryuusei missiles and Tetsuken systems in 109 AG, and broke openly with the Court in 116 AG. They killed Iroh with a bomb in 101 AG.

Spread across the world

The Salvationists did not stay in the Fire Nation. During the civil war their committees sent organizers and propagandists abroad: to the Earth Kingdom's provinces, where they found peasant collectives in the warlord wars, to the Yanakawan peninsula and the cities of the new republic, and to the ports of Qianchan. Soldiers who served in the Court's armies and non-bender veterans carried the ideas with them.

Flight after 120 AG

When the insurgency was suppressed by 120 AG, many members fled. Most went to the United Republic, where the immigrant cities took in Fire Nation workers without questions, and others settled in the southern island chain of the Qianchan Republic, where the republic tolerated exiles who kept quiet.

Descendants

In the United Republic the exiles and their allies became the Harmonists, banned in 126 AG. In the Earth Kingdom the peasant committees became the Collective. In the Fire Nation a faction broke away in 169 AG to form the Thunderbolt sect. The unrest of 167–171 AG are the later result. The Red Lotus draws part of its membership from the exiles. The exiles' own accounts are not yet written, and nothing here says that every later radical movement began with them.

air_nomad_genocide.title: Air Nomad Genocide
air_nomad_genocide.html:
Also known as the Silencing (survivor usage) and, in Imperial records, the Purification of the Winds. The first major atrocity of the Hundred Year War.

Date 0 AG (principal assault, about one week); continuing operations to 20 AG
Location The four Air Temples; the Air Nomad communities and pilgrim routes of the Earth Kingdom, Water Tribe and Yanakawa coasts; shipping lanes; the South Pole
Perpetrator Empire of Tajisaki, under Fire Lord Sozin
Deaths Approx. 3,000,000, almost the whole Air Nomad population, including benders and non-benders, and including collateral deaths on ships and transports. Disputed.
Survivors Approx. 300–400 people with airbending in 99 AG, living in the interior of Qianchan or the Earth Kingdom. Most do not know what they are, or have repressed it.

The Air Nomad Genocide was the deliberate destruction of the Air Nomads by the Empire of Tajisaki, begun in 0 AG at the start of the Hundred Year War. The Empire's aim was to end the Avatar cycle by killing the Air Nomads, among whom the next Avatar was due to be born. Using the power of a passing comet, Fire Lord Sozin attacked the four Air Temples, occupied the Western and Southern island chains and built air bases on them, and in January 1 AG used the Western base to invade the province of Yanakawa. Over the following two decades Imperial forces hunted the Air Nomads wherever they lived. The Air Nomad population, about three million people living in every part of the world, was reduced to a small number of survivors. The genocide led to the Empire's Homeland Purity Initiative, and its victims included people killed by accident as well as design.

Background

The Air Nomads were a pacifist people with no state and no army. They lived in the four Air Temples and in communities, camps and settlements across the Earth Kingdom, the Water Tribe lands and the Yanakawa coasts, and traveled on pilgrim routes by foot, by glider and by sea. About three million people lived in all, most of them non-benders. Their pacifism made them a poor military target and a convenient political one.

The Avatar cycle runs from the Fire Nation to the Air Nomads, and Fire Lord Sozin, who had begun a war of expansion, saw the Air Nomads as the nation that would produce the Avatar capable of opposing him. In 12 BG the Avatar before the next had died on Island Jezhi. In 0 AG a comet passed, and Sozin used its effect on firebending to attack.

The assault (0 AG)

The comet and the zeppelins

The operation was timed to the comet, which arrived at night and was described in Imperial accounts as a fine sight and a sign. The Empire attacked the four Air Temples at the same time with a fleet of zeppelin airships, each of which carried small aircraft. The zeppelins could climb to about 4,000 meters, high enough to reach the Western Air Temple, and their approach was not detected until they were overhead. The Empire also used the comet's effect on firebending to enlarge its weapons. Firebenders aboard the airships and with the artillery batteries ignited and fed the firebombs and napalm shells with their own fire, and the blasts were several times larger than the same munitions produced without it. The explosions could be seen for more than a hundred kilometers.

The Western Air Temple and its island chain

The Western Air Temple stood in an island chain of fishing villages and Air Nomad communities. In about a week the Imperial forces wiped out the chain: the temple, the Air Nomad communities on the islands, and the villages of non-Nomad fishermen, farmers and traders who lived beside them. Several islands were burned bare, and survivors were shot. The Empire then occupied the whole chain and built a forward operating base and airfields on it, from which it launched the invasion of Yanakawa in January 1 AG.

The Eastern Air Temple

The Eastern Air Temple was destroyed in the same week. Whole islands were razed, including the villages of civilians who had nothing to do with the Air Nomads.

The Northern Air Temple

The Northern Air Temple was firebombed, and its mountain was burned, but the Empire deliberately kept the ruin. The Imperial directive for the northern operation was to take the site for a base, and the Empire built an airbase, resupply depot and supply hub there, first for airships and later with airfields. The base was used for the rest of the war.

The Southern Air Temple

The Southern Air Temple, the home of the next Avatar, Aang, fell on the same night, and the surrounding island chain was completely occupied. The Empire built a forward base and airfields there as well.

Conduct

The assault and its aftermath involved the mass killing of civilians, the burning of villages and the shooting of survivors. These acts, later classed as war crimes, were carried out as part of an operation whose second purpose was to clear sites for Imperial bases. Yanakawa itself was invaded in January 1 AG, from the occupied island chains (see the Yanakawan Campaign).

Mopping up (0–20 AG)

The Empire then pursued the Air Nomads who lived elsewhere. Imperial columns destroyed settlements and camps on the pilgrim routes, and the Imperial Navy hunted transports and pilgrim vessels at sea. This was the most indiscriminate phase of the killing. Ships carrying Air Nomads also carried other passengers and crews, and these were sunk with them. Estimates of collateral deaths on ships and transports run to the hundreds of thousands, and are the least certain part of the toll. The last organized group of Air Nomads, a community of monks, children and refugees, was killed in the snow of the South Pole in 20 AG.

Casualties

The Air Nomad death toll is estimated at about three million, almost the whole population, benders and non-benders included. Imperial records, which were not published until after the war, give lower figures and describe the operation as complete by 20 AG. The Qianchan archives, which are the most detailed outside source, hold the registers of ships lost in the Western Air Temple waters and elsewhere, and are the main source for the collateral deaths.

Survivors

In 99 AG about 300 to 400 people with airbending ability were alive. They lived in the interior of Qianchan or the Earth Kingdom, far from the coasts the Empire had hunted. Most of them did not know what they were. Their families had hidden their descent for generations, and the ability, which is rare and usually shows itself only in moments of stress, was often put down to luck or chance. Others knew, and had repressed it, from fear of the Empire and of their neighbors. Imperial law treated the Air Nomads as extinct, and the survivors had no reason to expect otherwise from anyone.

The only known airbender in public view was the Avatar, Aang, who had been absent during the genocide. Later reports from 171 AG of non-benders gaining airbending abilities may have been descendants of this remnant. That connection is unproven.

Consequences

The genocide made possible the Empire's Homeland Purity Initiative, which expelled or killed the Empire's non-citizens, and was the first step in a policy of treating non-Fire peoples as enemies of the state. It also gave Qianchan and the Earth Kingdom reasons to see the war as existential. The Western Air Temple waters became the setting of the 27 AG sinking of a Qianchan civilian ship and the first naval engagement between Qianchan and the Imperial Navy, and the Western Air Temple island chain was later occupied by Qianchan and used to supply the Royalists in the Fire Nation Civil War.

Historiography

Imperial accounts, which were rewritten during the war, describe the operation as a strategic strike on a hostile nation and avoid the number of dead. Qianchan and Earth Kingdom sources describe it as genocide. Survivor accounts, which are few, tend to give the highest figures. All three agree that the Air Nomads were destroyed as a people, and that the survivors are very few.

water_tribe_subjugation.title: Subjugation of the Water Tribes
water_tribe_subjugation.html:
Also known as the Long Winter (Southern usage) and, in Imperial records, the Polar Administration. Part of the Hundred Year War, 0–99 AG.

Date 0 AG – 99 AG (principal phase 0–40 AG; the Southern occupation and colony continued to the end of the war; the Southern Uprising of 99 AG was crushed)
Location The South Pole continent and the North Pole
Result South: Imperial occupation, with leaders forced to cooperate, forced labor and a long insurgency. North: Imperial landings repelled in 0 AG, a forward air base established on the far eastern pole, and periodic bombardment of Agna Qel'a until it fell in December 99 AG and was occupied.
Belligerents Empire of Tajisaki vs Southern Water Tribe and Northern Water Tribe
Population About 8,000,000 Water Tribers before the war, of whom about 6,000,000 lived at the poles (North approx. 3,600,000; South approx. 2,400,000; split estimated) and about 2,000,000 elsewhere.
Casualties South: about 75% of the pre-war population remained after the last early uprising of 29 AG, about 50% by 99 AG, and about 30% at the end of the war: about 70% (approx. 1,680,000) dead or missing, from uprisings, reprisals, forced labor, famine, and conscription or deportation to the colonies. North: about 80% of the pre-war population remained by 99 AG (approx. 720,000 dead from naval bombardment and aerial attack), and about 50% by mid-100 AG (approx. 1,800,000 dead or missing in all) after the fall of Agna Qel'a and the Imperial occupation of the North.

The Subjugation of the Water Tribes was the Empire of Tajisaki's campaign to break the Water Tribes between 0 and 40 AG. Fire Lord Sozin ordered that the Water Tribes be given the same treatment as the Air Nomads, but with the difference that they were to be subjugated into submission and then worked to death. The campaign began about a week after the start of the Air Nomad Genocide, with the bombardment of both poles. In the North, the Empire failed to land, and settled for a forward air base on the far eastern pole. In the South it succeeded: the Empire captured the tribal leaders, forced them to cooperate, and ran an occupation with forced labor that was compared by Southerners to the worst regimes of the age. The Southern Water Tribe's resistance, which raided Imperial convoys and industrial sites for forty years, halved the South's population but kept it from being destroyed. The conditions of this period led directly to the Southern Uprising of 99 AG.

Background

Before the war, the Water Tribes numbered about six million people, divided between the Northern Water Tribe, a centralized state with walled cities and the stronger navy, and the Southern Water Tribe, a federation of chiefdoms with ice-walled towns and a far smaller fleet. The Southern waterbenders were numerous and skilled. The Empire regarded the Water Tribes as the second obstacle to its plans after the Air Nomads, since the next Avatar might be born among them, and as a labor force that could be exploited.

Fire Lord Sozin's directive was set before the war: the Water Tribes were to be subjugated, not exterminated at once, and their people used for labor until they were worn out. The Empire's navy destroyed the combined Water Tribe fleets in the first weeks, which left both poles without sea defenses.

The first week (0 AG)

About a week after the assault on the Air Temples began, Imperial fleets and zeppelins bombarded both poles at once.

North

The bombardment of Agna Qel'a came by sea and by air. The city's ice walls and the polar terrain held, and the landings that followed were thrown back with heavy Imperial losses. The Empire did not try again at that scale. Instead it set up an outpost on the far eastern pole, which grew into a forward air base and forward operating base. From there, Imperial aircraft bombed Agna Qel'a from time to time for the next hundred years, and the base later served as a staging point for the naval invasion of the North in 99 AG.

South

In the South the landings succeeded. The fleet shelled the ice-walled towns, including Wolf Cove and Whale Harbor, and landed troops while the defenders were still recovering from the naval defeat. The Council of Chieftains and Elders and the leading chieftains were captured in the first weeks. Those who refused to cooperate were executed in front of their people. The rest were forced to take part in an Imperial administration.

The occupation of the South (0–40 AG)

Administration

The Empire governed the South through a Governor-General, with the captured Council kept in place under supervision. The Council was made to issue the Governor's orders as its own, to draw up registers of waterbenders and of able-bodied adults, and to supply laborers. A hostage system and collective punishments were used to make it comply. Some chieftains collaborated and others cooperated in order to protect their people, and the difference between them was disputed for generations.

Forced labor

The Empire's aim was to use the South's population until it was exhausted. Laborers were set to build harbors, dry docks and ice-cut channels for the Imperial fleet, to lay rail lines across the ice, to quarry ice, and to work in processing plants for seal and whale products. Waterbenders, who were the most valuable and the most closely watched, were used to cut ice and clear channels, and those who were captured were sent to prisons where they were denied water except for drinking. The camps, the work and the winters killed large numbers of people. Talekeepers and elders, who carried the tribe's history, were killed in large numbers, and much of the oral tradition was lost.

Insurgency (0–40 AG)

The occupation met resistance from the first year. There were countless uprisings and insurgent actions in the first forty years: raids on Imperial convoys, ice mines laid on the roads, attacks on rail lines and industrial sites, and the sinking and trapping of ships in the ice. Resistance groups hid in caves and under the glaciers. The most important of these hideouts was Taluqqriaq, the cavern settlement beneath Wolf Cove, known as the Wolf Cave, which became the Southern resistance's capital after the surface town was shelled. The Southern chiefdoms had no outside help at first. After Qianchan entered the war in 30 AG, surplus rifles and supplies reached the guerrillas by sea, and the Imperial Navy had to divert ships to escort its convoys. The last and largest of the early risings began in 29 AG. Southerners call it the First Uprising because it was the first to unite the chiefdoms under a single command, and it left the South with about 75% of its pre-war population.

The Empire responded with reprisals: the destruction of villages and towns, mass executions, and the starvation of districts that sheltered guerrillas. Together with the labor camps and famine, these reduced the population of the South to about three quarters of its pre-war number after the rising of 29 AG, and to about half of it by 99 AG.

After 40 AG

By about 40 AG the insurgency had been broken as an organized force. Imperial garrisons held the coast and the main towns, and the survivors of the resistance withdrew into hidden settlements in the interior and under the ice. Imperial raiding forces, known later as the Southern Raiders, continued to hunt the remaining waterbenders, and the number of free waterbenders fell steadily. Contact between the South and the North was lost around 50 AG.

Colony and research base

The South was never abandoned by the Empire. Over the following decades it was slowly built up as an Imperial colony. Yakutokai, the Imperial port city on the coast, with its red-tiled buildings, cranes and rail lines, became the colony's center, and the Southern Garrison, with Breaker units and half-tracks, held the surrounding territory. The Empire also built research stations on the ice, among them the Observation and Research Outpost 9, as cold-weather testing grounds. Fighting remained at a low level of skirmishes and missing patrol reports in 97–99 AG, when the Imperial Navy shelled Wolf Cove, and became a full uprising in 99 AG. By 99 AG only a few dozen waterbenders were known to be alive in the South, most of them children or people who concealed their ability.

The Northern Water Tribe, meanwhile, turned inward and defended Agna Qel'a against periodic bombing until the Siege of the North, which began on 13 November 99 AG and ended with its fall in December.

The Southern Uprising of 99 AG

The uprising of 99 AG, the largest since the First Uprising of 29 AG, was crushed by the Southern Garrison with Breaker units, mortars and rail-borne reinforcements. Taluqqriaq was destroyed, and its survivors, about a hundred people, were extracted by an Imperial team. The Empire's reprisals killed many more Southerners and reduced the population further. Large numbers of survivors, boys and young men above all, were conscripted into Imperial service or sent to work in the colonies, which removed them from the South. Remnants of the resistance fled south into the interior to build a new capital. See the article on the Southern Uprising.

Casualties

South. With an estimated pre-war population of about 2,400,000, the South had about 1,800,000 people (75%) after the last early uprising of 29 AG, about 1,200,000 (50%) by 99 AG, and about 720,000 (30%) at the end of the war. About 70% of the pre-war population, an estimated 1,680,000 people, was dead or missing, including those conscripted or sent to work in the colonies after the uprising of 99 AG and never accounted for.

North. About 720,000 Northerners had died by 99 AG, about 20% of the population, almost all from naval bombardment and aerial attack. After the fall of Agna Qel'a in December 99 AG, the Imperial occupation applied the methods learned in the South, and by the end of June 100 AG the population had fallen to about 50% of its pre-war number, about 1,800,000 dead or missing in all.

These figures do not include Water Tribe civilians killed in the Air Nomad Genocide, who lived in the island chains of the Western Air Temple and are counted with that atrocity.

Historiography

Imperial records describe the campaign as a pacification and give low casualty figures. The polar campaigns were also largely ignored in the public news of both the Fire Nation and the Earth Kingdom, and most people there knew little of them. Southern oral histories give much higher figures and name the occupation as a genocide. Northern accounts emphasize the defense of Agna Qel'a and are criticized in the South for the North's failure to aid it. Qianchan archives hold the most detailed record of the convoys and shipping losses.

  • Air Nomad Genocide
  • Southern Uprising (99 AG)
  • Agna Qel'a
  • Hundred Year War

yanakawan_campaign.title: Yanakawan Campaign
yanakawan_campaign.html:
Also known as the Eastern Meatgrinder (Earth Kingdom usage), the Ten-Year Harvest (Imperial soldiers' usage) and, in Imperial records, the Yanakawa Operation. Part of the Earth Kingdom land war, Hundred Year War.

Date 3 January 1 AG – 14 October 10 AG
Location Yanakawa, the Earth Kingdom's western coastal province, facing the Fire Nation (the land of the later United Republic of Nations)
Result Tajisaki victory. The Empire conquered Yanakawa in ten years and made it the base of its Eastern Territories.
Belligerents Empire of Tajisaki: Eastern Army, Eastern Fleet, Zeppelin Wing. Earth Kingdom: Yanakawan provincial levy, the Great Levy of the western provinces.
Commanders Tajisaki: General Ōmura Genzō (Eastern Army); Admiral Sakurai Jirō (Eastern Fleet); Air Colonel Hirata Kenji (Zeppelin Wing). Earth Kingdom: Governor Liang Shouzhi (Yanakawa); Marshal Feng Tianyu (Great Levy); General Bai Chengyu (Hengli).
Strength Tajisaki: about 140,000 at the start, about 420,000 at the peak (6 AG), 38 zeppelins carrying about 150 early aircraft. Earth Kingdom: about 600,000 levies at the start, more than 1,900,000 raised in all.
Casualties Earth Kingdom: approx. 3,500,000 dead, about half of them civilians. Tajisaki: approx. 450,000 dead. All figures disputed.

The Yanakawan Campaign was the Empire of Tajisaki's invasion and ten-year conquest of the Earth Kingdom's western coastal province of Yanakawa, which began on 3 January 1 AG, a few months after the Air Nomad genocide. The Empire launched it from the air bases that it had built on the Western Air Temple island chain. It opened with a landing at the site of the modern city of Yu Dao, where the Empire used mustard gas, which was the first use of chemical weapons in the war. For the next decade the campaign was a meatgrinder. Earth Kingdom provincial levies, raised in mass and thrown against entrenched Imperial positions, died in very large numbers, at a ratio of about eight to one against the Empire's dead. By 10 AG the Empire held the province and made it the base of its Eastern Territories.

Background

After the Air Nomad genocide the Empire occupied the Western and Southern Air Temple island chains completely and built forward operating bases and airfields on them. The Western chain lay within a day's flight of Yanakawa's coast. The Empire's aim was a continental base from which to advance on the Earth Kingdom's interior and on the walls of Ba Sing Se. Yanakawa was a good choice: a coastal province with ports and a large rural population, far from the capital, with weak provincial defenses and a governor who had been warned of the threat and had not believed it.

Imperial plan

The Imperial General Staff's plan, called the Harvest Plan by its authors, was one of attrition by firepower. The Empire would land on two beaches, dig in behind trenches, wire and machine guns on a defensible line, and let the Earth Kingdom's far larger numbers destroy themselves in assaults. The line it chose ran inland from the coast and was called the Yellow Line, after the color it was marked in on the staff's maps.

Earth Kingdom response

The Earth Kingdom had no standing army in the east. The provincial lords raised levies of peasants, armed with old rifles, spears and swords, and led them in mass assaults. The doctrine, which went back centuries, was the "mountain rush": a charge in such numbers that the enemy would be overrun or run out of ammunition. Earthbenders attached to the levies raised walls and collapsed trenches, but could not stand up to machine guns and gas for long.

Course

Phase I: Landings and the coastal strip (January–December 1 AG)

Yu Dao. On 3 January 1 AG, aircraft and zeppelins from the Western Air Temple base struck Yanakawa's coastal garrisons, and the Eastern Army landed at the river landing of Yuhe, on the site of the modern city of Yu Dao. The Yanakawan levy counter-attacked the beachhead on 5 January in three waves of about 40,000 men each. The Empire fired mustard gas shells (the Type 0 Kiiro-dan, "yellow shell") into the second and third waves, which were caught in open ground. About 52,000 Earth Kingdom soldiers died, against about 1,100 Imperial soldiers, and the beachhead held.

Seiran Bay. On 21 February the Eastern Fleet landed a second force at Seiran Bay, 190 kilometers up the coast, on the site of the later Qinglan Port. Governor Liang had split his levies to cover both landing sites, and the two beachheads linked up by 14 April.

The Reed Fords (April 1 AG). Marshal Feng's Great Levy of about 300,000 attacked the linked beachheads at the Reed Fords on the Yu River, in the first of the great mass charges. It lost about 88,000 dead in four days.

Phase II: The Yellow Line (1–3 AG)

By the end of 1 AG the Empire held the coastal strip behind the Yellow Line, and the Great Levy gathered against it. The Siege of Hengli (June 1 – March 2 AG), a river city held by General Bai Chengyu, ended with its fall after nine months, when the Empire's blockade starved the garrison and the city's 300,000 civilians. About 140,000 civilians died. The Autumn Levy Charges (September–October 2 AG) were a series of mass attacks at Shuangshan Ridge in which the Great Levy lost about 80,000 dead in three days, to machine guns and artillery, without taking the ridge.

Phase III: Gas (3–5 AG)

In 4 AG the Empire took the region of Yu Dao, an Earth Kingdom territory since 4292 BG, and its flag was retired.

In 3 AG the Empire gassed an Earth Kingdom corps at Liangkou with a heavier phosgene mix, killing about 8,000 men in one morning. The Earth Kingdom never acquired chemical weapons, and its only protection was wet cloth over the face, while the Empire's troops wore rubber and glass masks. Chemical warfare in the war was entirely the Empire's. At the Battle of the Salt Marshes (4 AG), an Earth Kingdom attack through low ground was caught in a gas cloud that settled in the marsh, and about 70,000 men died, most of them from the gas. In 5 AG the Zeppelin Wing's first bombing of a city, Taigu, killed about 20,000 people in a night.

Phase IV: The breakthrough (6–8 AG)

In 6 AG the Empire fielded the Type 1 tank, an armored vehicle carrying machine guns, which could cross wire and trenches. The first tank had been built in 2 AG, and oil had fueled vehicles since 5 AG. Eastern Army attacked out of the Yellow Line at the Nine Bends (6–7 AG), where the tanks, with artillery and gas, broke the Great Levy's last defensive line in eight weeks. The Empire reached the central plain in 7 AG. The Siege of Jinzhou (8 AG), the provincial capital, lasted five months, and its fall gave the Empire control of the central river valley.

Phase V: Pacification (9–10 AG)

The remaining Earth Kingdom forces fell back on Anshan, a fortified mountain town in the northeast. The Fall of Anshan (9 AG – 14 October 10 AG) ended the campaign. The Empire starved the town for a year and shelled it for the last three months, and the defenders surrendered. The Empire then ran a pacification campaign through the hills and swamps, where bands of levies and earthbenders had survived.

Major engagements

Battle Date Outcome Est. dead (Earth Kingdom / Tajisaki)
Yu Dao (Yuhe landing) 3–6 Jan 1 AG Imperial beachhead held; first use of mustard gas 52,000 / 1,100
Seiran Bay landing 21–25 Feb 1 AG Second beachhead taken 9,000 / 800
The Reed Fords Apr 1 AG Great Levy repulsed 88,000 / 3,000
Siege of Hengli Jun 1 – Mar 2 AG City starved and taken 190,000 / 4,000
Shuangshan Ridge (Autumn Levy Charges) Sep–Oct 2 AG Great Levy repulsed 80,000 / 2,500
Liangkou 3 AG Earth Kingdom corps gassed and broken 8,000 / 100
The Salt Marshes 4 AG Gas cloud destroys the attack 70,000 / 1,500
Bombing of Taigu 5 AG First strategic bombing 20,000 / 0
The Nine Bends 6–7 AG Great Levy's last line broken 150,000 / 14,000
Siege of Jinzhou 8 AG Provincial capital taken 110,000 / 9,000
Fall of Anshan 9–10 AG Last stronghold falls 90,000 / 5,000

Casualties

By phase, the Earth Kingdom lost about 520,000 dead in Phase I, 900,000 in Phase II, 800,000 in Phase III, 900,000 in Phase IV and 380,000 in Phase V, about 3.5 million in all, and the Empire about 40,000, 90,000, 110,000, 130,000 and 80,000, about 450,000. About half the Earth Kingdom's dead were civilians, who died in sieges, bombings, gas attacks and the Empire's starvation of districts that resisted. Imperial sources give the Earth Kingdom's dead as about a third of this figure.

Atrocities

The Empire used chemical weapons against fortified positions, and also against villages, whose populations it gassed when they were suspected of helping the levies. The blockade and siege of Hengli, the burning of the Red River villages in 2 AG and the bombing of Taigu were all treated as war crimes by the Earth Kingdom's post-war tribunals. The Eastern Labor Bureau, established in 6 AG, conscripted hundreds of thousands of people from the conquered districts into labor on roads, ports and airfields. The Earth Kingdom's mass charges, in turn, were criticized by its own officers after the war as a waste of lives.

Aftermath

By 10 AG the Empire controlled the whole of the west coast, and its advance beyond Yanakawa is described in the article on the Early Land War (0–30 AG). By 10 AG the Empire controlled Yanakawa. It settled colonists there and made the province the core of its Eastern Territories, with the airbases and ports that later served the whole western coast. The province's people were classified under the Imperial system of integration, and many were put to forced labor. The Empire used the province as the base for its later offensives, including the Hu Xin Provinces campaign. The province remained under Imperial rule until the Yanakawan War of Independence (100–105 AG), when Seiran Bay, which the Empire had made a harbor, became the Provisional Council's capital, Qinglan Port.

Historiography

Imperial histories describe the campaign as a model of economical conquest. Earth Kingdom accounts, which were written under the later reforms, describe it as a massacre, and blame the provincial lords for the loss of life. Qianchan observers, who were not yet in the war, kept some of the best records of the gas casualties.

  • Yanakawan War of Independence

early_land_war.title: Early Land War
early_land_war.html:
The Empire of Tajisaki's advance on the Earth Kingdom, 0–30 AG, until Qianchan's entry into the war.

Date 0 AG – 30 AG
Location The western Earth Kingdom: the west coast (Yanakawa), the northern mountains, the Omashu front and the western edge of the Si Wong Desert
Result The Empire occupied the whole west coast by 10 AG, cut the southern Omashu front off from the rest of the kingdom by 25 AG, and reached the Si Wong's edge by 27 AG. It held naval superiority alone until Qianchan's entry in 30 AG.
Belligerents Empire of Tajisaki vs Earth Kingdom (supplied at Omashu by Qianchan)
Casualties About 9,200,000 Earth Kingdom and about 900,000 Fire Nation dead (part of the Earth Kingdom land war's total). All figures disputed.

The Early Land War was the first thirty years of the Empire's land campaign against the Earth Kingdom. It began with the occupation of the Western Air Temple island chain in 1 AG, which gave the Empire its air and naval base, and its conquest of the whole west coast in ten years. The Empire then pushed north along the mountain chain and south toward Omashu, was foiled in its attempt to break east, and instead cut the southern Omashu front off through the high mountains and pushed toward the Si Wong for its resources. Throughout the period the Empire alone held naval superiority. The war ended its first phase in 30 AG, when the sinking of a Qianchan ship brought the Qianchan Republic into the war.

Territorial phases

Date Event
1 AG The Western Air Temple island chain, south-west of the continent, is completely occupied. The Empire builds forward operating bases and airfields there.
1–10 AG The Yanakawan Campaign: the Empire conquers the whole west coast, the bright-red zone of the maps, by 10 AG.
10–30 AG The northern push: the Empire advances into the northern mountains and plains, which include the Northern Air Temple, and holds that line in 30 AG.
10–25 AG The southern push: the Empire attacks from the southern part of Yanakawa to reach Omashu and to break east, and is foiled. Instead it pushes into the high mountains. By 25 AG it has cut the southern Omashu front off from the rest of the kingdom.
27 AG The Empire pushes toward the south-west and the western edge of the Si Wong, to take its resources.
30 AG Qianchan enters the war.

The west coast (1–10 AG)

The Empire's occupation of the Western Air Temple chain in 1 AG gave it a base within reach of Yanakawa, and the invasion in January 1 AG opened the Yanakawan Campaign. By 10 AG the whole of the Earth Kingdom's west coast was in Imperial hands, and it became the base of the Eastern Territories.

The northern push (10–30 AG)

From 10 AG the Empire pushed north into the mountain chain and its plains, in a long, slow advance that was supported by the Northern Air Temple base. By 30 AG it held the northern mountains, and it threatened the central river basin.

The southern push and the Omashu front (10–25 AG)

The Empire's attempt to push from the southern province of Yanakawa to Omashu and to the east was foiled. The Earth Kingdom's levies held the lowlands, and the Empire's columns could not break through. Instead, it turned toward the high mountains, and by 25 AG it had cut the southern Omashu front off from the rest of the kingdom. Omashu, which was now isolated by land, was supplied from the sea by Qianchan, which was not yet at war. The supply route ran through the waters south of the continent, near the Western Air Temple island chain, where in 27 AG a Qianchan civilian ship was sunk.

The push to the Si Wong (27 AG)

By 27 AG the Empire was pushing toward the south-west and the western edge of the Si Wong Desert, where oil had been found in 28 BG. The oil was needed for its new tanks and aircraft, and the desert's resources were the reason for the push. It reached the desert's edge, which began the fighting that continued until the Desert War.

Naval superiority

Throughout 0–30 AG the Empire alone held naval superiority. The Earth Kingdom had almost no navy, and the Water Tribes' fleets had been destroyed in 0 AG. It used its fleet to blockade, to land troops and to bombard, and to sink the ships that supplied Omashu. This ended in 30 AG, when the Qianchan Navy fought the first naval engagement with the Imperial Navy and the battle was a draw.

Casualties

The Earth Kingdom lost about 9.2 million people in the thirty years, most of them civilians, and the Empire about 900,000. The heaviest losses were in the Yanakawan Campaign, which accounts for about 3.5 million of the Earth Kingdom's dead.

Historiography

Imperial histories describe the thirty years as a methodical conquest of the west and the mountains. Earth Kingdom accounts emphasize the loss of Omashu's land links, and the Qianchan archives record the supply route in the most detail.

See also

  • Yanakawan Campaign
  • Eastern Push
  • Desert War
  • Air Nomad Genocide
  • Hundred Year War

eastern_push.title: Eastern Push
eastern_push.html:
Also known as the Grassland Campaign (Earth Kingdom usage) and, in Imperial records, the Oil Plan. Part of the Earth Kingdom land war, 30–50 AG.

Date 30 AG – 50 AG
Location The western grasslands and river plains of the Earth Kingdom, the western shore of the inland sea, and the western edge of the Si Wong Desert; at sea, the waters around the Western Air Temple island chain
Result Tajisaki victory. The Empire took the grasslands and by 50 AG held a front line running from the north coast to the western edge of the Si Wong. The Desert War began.
Belligerents Empire of Tajisaki vs Earth Kingdom and, from 30 AG, Qianchan Republic
Casualties Earth Kingdom approx. 6,800,000 dead; Fire Nation approx. 700,000; Qianchan approx. 100,000. All figures disputed.

The Eastern Push was the Empire of Tajisaki's advance east across the Earth Kingdom's western grasslands between 30 and 50 AG. After the thirty years of the Early Land War, the Empire's General Staff planned to push east to the Si Wong Desert, whose oil its tanks and aircraft needed, and it did so, taking the grasslands in two decades of campaigning. By 50 AG the Imperial front line ran from the northern coast down the western plains to the desert's western edge, and then south-west across the sea, through the Western Air Temple island chain. The Eastern Push began in the year Qianchan entered the war and brought the Empire to the Si Wong, where the Desert War began in 50 AG.

Background

By 30 AG the Empire held the whole west coast, the northern mountains and the isolated southern Omashu front, and had pushed to the western edge of the Si Wong in 27 AG. Oil, which had been found in the desert in 28 BG, was now the Empire's most important resource, since its new tanks and aircraft consumed far more than the home islands produced. The General Staff Directorate's plan, which its authors called the Oil Plan, was to push east across the grasslands, to gather the forces needed for the desert, and to take the oil fields.

In 30 AG the Qianchan Republic entered the war after one of its ships was sunk, and the Earth Kingdom, which had begun to industrialize with Qianchan's help in 23 AG, started to receive Qianchan equipment and doctrine. This slowed the push, but did not stop it.

The front line, 50 AG

The Imperial front line in 50 AG ran north to south as follows:

  • North. From the northern coast it ran through the northern mountains and river lands, which the Empire had held since the northern push of 10–30 AG.
  • Centre. It ran south along the western shore of the inland sea and down the grasslands of the western plains, which the Empire had taken during the Eastern Push, to the western edge of the Si Wong Desert.
  • South. From the desert's edge it turned south-west across the sea, and passed through the Western Air Temple island chain, which was by then divided between the Empire in the west and the Qianchan Navy in the east.

Course

Consolidation (30–35 AG)

The first years were spent consolidating the lines and moving the Eastern Army's reserves forward. The Empire built rail lines and airfields across the plains and brought up its new oil-fueled tanks. Qianchan's navy and the Earth Kingdom's first modernized divisions arrived in the grasslands.

The grasslands (35–45 AG)

The Empire's advance across the plains was a series of set-piece battles in country that favored tanks. At the Battle of the Hesha Plains (37–38 AG), its armored columns broke an Earth Kingdom army that had tried to hold the plain with massed infantry, and at the Siege of Dongping (41–43 AG), the Empire took the main rail junction of the central plains after a two-year siege. The Earth Kingdom's industrialization produced its first tanks and rifles in these years, but not enough, and its army retreated east.

The desert's edge (45–50 AG)

By 45 AG the Empire had reached the western edge of the Si Wong, and spent the next five years bringing up supplies for an attack on the oil fields. The Battle of the Reed Sea (46 AG), a river and marsh fight on the plain's last water line, and the Fall of Chenlu (49 AG), the Earth Kingdom's last fortified town before the desert, ended the push. The Coalition, which now included Qianchan's desert-trained units, fell back into the Si Wong.

The sea

Qianchan's entry in 30 AG ended the Empire's sole naval superiority, but not its lead. The Qianchan Navy won the eastern half of the Western Air Temple chain's waters, and the front at sea ran through the islands. Imperial ships continued to blockade, and Qianchan convoys continued to supply Omashu and the Earth Kingdom's southern ports under escort.

Casualties

The Earth Kingdom lost about 6.8 million dead, the Empire about 700,000, and Qianchan about 100,000. Most of the Earth Kingdom's dead were civilians, who died in sieges, bombings, the Empire's occupation policy and famine.

Aftermath

By 50 AG the Empire stood at the Si Wong's edge, and the Desert War began, in which the Empire spent thirty years trying to take the oil fields.

See also

  • Early Land War
  • Yanakawan Campaign
  • Desert War
  • Hundred Year War

desert_war.title: Desert War
desert_war.html:
Also known as the Oil Cycle (Qianchan usage). Part of the Hundred Year War.

Date 50 AG – 79 AG
Location The Si Wong Desert and its approaches
Result Stalemate. The Empire seized the oil fields four times and was thrown off each time. The Empire's second attempt, the Si Wong Offensive (80–88 AG), held them.
Belligerents Empire of Tajisaki vs Earth Kingdom and Qianchan Republic
Casualties About 1,100,000 dead (Earth Kingdom about 550,000; Qianchan about 250,000; Fire Nation about 300,000). All figures disputed.

The Desert War was the Empire of Tajisaki's first attempt to take the oil fields of the Si Wong Desert, which lasted from 50 AG to 79 AG. It was mostly an air war, fought with early aircraft and bombers over a desert that the Earth Kingdom's armies had not fought in since the Warring States period, and it produced only small gains. The Empire captured the fields at least four times, and each time the Coalition threw it off again, in a cycle of capture, counter-attack and retreat. The Empire learned from the failures, and its General Staff concluded that the oil could be held only by a ground offensive, which it launched in 80 AG.

Background

Oil was discovered in the Si Wong in 28 BG, and by 5 AG the Empire was using it to fuel its vehicles, since the new tanks and aircraft consumed far more than the home islands produced. Fighting in the desert had begun in 27–31 AG, when the Empire's Kern formations deployed in the wrong camouflage and suffered for it. The Qianchan Republic, which entered the war in 30 AG and had desert-fighting doctrine of its own, taught the Earth Kingdom how to hold the Si Wong. The Desert War began in 50 AG, when the Empire's Eastern Push (30–50 AG) took the western grasslands and brought it to the desert's western edge.

Course

The Empire's strategy was to use its air force, based on the Northern Air Temple airfields and later at the desert's edge, to break the Coalition's rail and road network and to support small ground forces that seized the fields. It achieved this four times.

Attempt Captured Lost How
First 56 AG 58 AG A Qianchan–Earth Kingdom counter-offensive cut the field's supply line
Second 63 AG 66 AG The garrison was cut off and starved
Third 71 AG 74 AG Tank-led counter-attack from the south
Fourth 77 AG 79 AG Combined air and ground attack

Each time the Empire's gains were too small and its supply too thin to last. Its air force could destroy trains and depots, but could not hold ground, and the Coalition's desert units, which wore the tan Huanglin pattern and used the QR-7's range advantage, retook the fields in each case.

Casualties

About 1.1 million people died, about 300,000 Imperial, 550,000 Earth Kingdom and 250,000 Qianchan, most of them soldiers. Civilians were few in the desert, but the bombing of the rail towns killed tens of thousands.

Aftermath

After the fourth failure the General Staff Directorate concluded that the oil could be held only by a ground offensive that took and kept the whole basin and its roads. In 79 AG it adopted Plan Yellow, and the Si Wong Offensive began in 80 AG. This second attempt, unlike the first, held the fields until the end of Ozai's reign.

See also

  • Si Wong Offensive
  • Hundred Year War
  • Qianchan Republic

si_wong_offensive.title: Si Wong Offensive
si_wong_offensive.html:
Known in Imperial records as Plan Yellow (黄色計画, Kiiro Keikaku) and in Qianchan archives as the Reroute. Part of the Hundred Year War.

Date 8 July 80 AG – 23 August 88 AG
Location The Si Wong Desert and its approaches, western Earth Kingdom
Result Tajisaki victory. Plan Yellow achieved its objective: the Empire seized the oil basin at Tongba and the desert road and rail corridor, and occupied Miando, Tangshu and Xutong. The towns affected were damaged, plundered or evacuated, and some were destroyed. Coalition supply lines were forced around the desert.
Belligerents Empire of Tajisaki vs Coalition Desert Front: Earth Kingdom and Qianchan Republic
Commanders Tajisaki: Marshal Kuroda Tatsuo. Earth Kingdom: General Wu Zhenhai. Qianchan: Lieutenant General Shen Yuwen.
Strength Tajisaki: 1,983,000 personnel, 8,350 artillery pieces, 3,174 tanks, 5,878 aircraft. Coalition: 2,153,000 personnel (Earth Kingdom 1,291,800; Qianchan 861,200), 3,250 artillery pieces, 3,955 tanks, 6,530 aircraft.
Casualties Tajisaki: 755,358 combat casualties; 2,582 aircraft, 1,092 tanks and 3,521 guns destroyed; 1,436 guns captured. Coalition: 1,357,800 combat casualties (Earth Kingdom 950,460; Qianchan 407,340); 4,879 aircraft, 2,589 tanks and 1,538 guns destroyed. Civilian losses not tallied. All figures disputed.

The Si Wong Offensive was an eight-year Imperial campaign across the Si Wong Desert, which the General Staff Directorate planned and conducted under the codename Plan Yellow. It ran from July 80 AG to August 88 AG and was one of the few large offensives of the Hundred Year War that the Empire won. Its objective was the desert's oil, which the Empire needed to fuel its mechanized and aviation expansion, and not an advance on any Earth Kingdom city. By the end of the campaign the Empire held the Tongba oil basin and the desert's road and rail corridor. The Coalition's armies lost the corridor, which had carried Qianchan supplies to the Earth Kingdom's western and central fronts, and had to move those supplies on much longer routes around the desert.

Background

The Si Wong theater

Fighting in the Si Wong theater dated back to at least 27–31 AG, when Imperial Kern formations deployed in the desert wearing the dark Kage-Madara camouflage pattern and suffered heavily because it was unsuited to the terrain. The IRB developed a separate desert pattern, Suna-Iro, for the campaign.[1] Qianchan's infantry used a tan variant, Huanglin, for the same reason.[2] Qianchan had entered the war in 30 AG, after one of its civilian ships was sunk in the waters near the Western Air Temple in 27 AG and the first naval engagement with the Imperial Navy ended in a draw. From 50 AG to 79 AG the desert was the scene of the Empire's first attempt on the oil fields, which was mostly an air war with small gains. The Empire captured the fields more than once and was thrown off them each time, and the cycle repeated. The 80–88 AG offensive described here was the second attempt.

The oil

By 79 AG the Empire's war economy was short of fuel. Its mechanized and aviation programs consumed far more than the home islands produced, and Qianchan's long submarine interdiction campaign against Imperial shipping, which had driven the Imperial Navy's carrier fleet onto the defensive,[1] made imported fuel unreliable. The Si Wong basin was the only large oilfield within reach of the Imperial armies. In 79 AG the General Staff Directorate adopted Plan Yellow, which called for the seizure of the oil basin and the roads that fed it, and for a halt once they were taken. The plan was drawn up by General Iroh, then the Directorate's Planning Director.

The Coalition position

The desert's roads and railway carried Qianchan supplies westward to the Earth Kingdom's western and central fronts, including the Omashu front and the plains approaches to Ba Sing Se. The Earth Kingdom's garrisons in the desert were under a fragmented command, and Qianchan's reserve was committed on the Omashu front. Qianchan's QR-7 rifle gave its infantry a range advantage on open terrain,[2] which was real in the desert but could not make up for the Empire's numbers or the Coalition's supply problems.

Plan Yellow

The plan used three axes. A northern thrust from the coast near Wangshapai would swing around the bay toward Yixin and Tongzou, cutting the desert's northern approaches. A central drive from Luokeng, at the desert's western edge, would encircle Tongba, the oil city, and seize the road network behind it. A southern thrust from the Kusi–Yancheling line would hold the Coalition's southern forces away from Omashu and the desert's southern roads. The Empire opened with its air force, and its armor and Breaker formations advanced behind it under air cover. A map prepared by the Imperial staff one month into the offensive, on 8 August 80 AG, shows all three axes.

Course of the campaign

Opening phase (July 80 – 82 AG)

The offensive began on 8 July 80 AG. In the central sector the Imperial armor broke the Coalition line in the Battle of Luokeng (July–August 80 AG) and began the encirclement of Tongba. In the north, the Imperial northern group took Yixin and Tongzou by 82 AG. In the south, the Battle of Kusi (August 80 – March 81 AG) was a long fight in which Earth Kingdom infantry counter-attacked under smoke cover, and the Imperial armor held and then took the town.

Siege of Tongba (82–85 AG)

Tongba was encircled in 82 AG and defended for three years by Earth Kingdom garrison troops and Qianchan detachments, which were supplied by air and by convoys across the desert. The siege ended in 85 AG with the fall of the city and of the oil basin around it. The Imperial armies found the fields damaged but intact, and had them in production within a year.

The corridor (85–87 AG)

After Tongba, the southern group took Yancheling and cut the southern roads to the Omashu approaches, and the Imperial central and northern groups took the desert's road and rail network. In 86–87 AG the Empire occupied Miando, Tangshu and Xutong, three towns that had served as the Coalition's rear bases. These towns were damaged, plundered or evacuated, and some were destroyed.

Consolidation (87–88 AG)

The Imperial General Staff halted the offensive on the desert's eastern edge and built a fortified line. The last major action of Plan Yellow was the Battle of the Rail Cut (18 August 88 AG), a Coalition counter-attack on the rail cut that anchored the Imperial eastern line. An infantry company holding the cut was isolated in the first hours of the attack, and a platoon of four medium tanks under Lieutenant Lu Ten, the son of General Iroh, held the position for most of a day, losing two tanks, until the line was restored. The Coalition's attack failed. The campaign ended five days later, on 23 August 88 AG.

Supply rerouting

With the corridor lost, the Earth Kingdom and Qianchan armies had to move their supplies on new routes. Qianchan material for the western and central fronts was sent north around the desert through the Omashu highlands, or south and east through the Earth Kingdom's central road and rail net. This lengthened the supply line by an estimated 1,100 kilometers and about doubled transit times. The longer routes were vulnerable to Imperial air attack, and they absorbed the Earth Kingdom's already strained rail capacity. The shift forced the Coalition to concentrate its forces on the Omashu front and the approaches to Ba Sing Se, where the Empire was to attack in 96 AG (see Siege of Ba Sing Se).

Significance

The Fire Nation's oil output from the Tongba basin rose from almost nothing to about 140,000 barrels per day by 90 AG. It fueled the Imperial war economy's late-war expansion: jet aircraft, mechanized warfare and the long-range bombing campaigns of 80–99 AG, and the 96–97 AG siege of Ba Sing Se. The Coalition fought the final decade of the war on longer supply lines, with less reserve and against an enemy that no longer had a fuel shortage.

The Empire held the fields from 88 AG until the end of Ozai's reign in 100 AG. It did not use its success to advance on Ba Sing Se. This is regarded as a deliberate choice by the General Staff Directorate, which valued the oil more than the cities beyond it. The campaign nevertheless led directly to the 96–97 AG siege of Ba Sing Se: its oil paid for the mechanized and aviation programs that made the siege possible, and the same planners, with Iroh as field marshal, led it.

The Si Wong's role as a technological battlefield continued through the 90s, and after the Hundred Year War the desert was used for nuclear testing.

Historiography

Qianchan archives call the campaign "the Reroute" and describe it as a failure of Coalition coordination. The Earth Kingdom's authorized history describes it as a "strategic withdrawal" and gives no casualty figures. Imperial records describe it as the first campaign in which the Empire's mechanization and fuel supply were decisive.

References

  1. Imperial Research Bureau, Consolidated Technology Status Report, 99 AG, Parts I, III.
  2. Qianchan Infantry Doctrine (NRD), Parts II–III.

southern_uprising.title: Southern Uprising
southern_uprising.html:
Also known as the Winter Rising and, in Imperial records, the Southern Pacification of 99 AG. Part of the Hundred Year War.

Date 12 May – 9 December 99 AG
Location The South Pole continent; the resistance capital, Taluqqriaq (the Wolf Cave), beneath Wolf Cove
Result Imperial victory. The uprising was crushed and the capital fell. The Avatar was found in the South during the uprising and was evacuated.
Belligerents Southern Water Tribe resistance, with Qianchan-supplied arms, vs Empire of Tajisaki: Southern Garrison, Breaker units, armored battalions, Fire Navy
Commanders Resistance: Chief Hakoda. Imperial: Admiral Zhao; Prince Zuko (commanded a task element).
Casualties Southern: approx. 150,000 killed in the fighting; approx. 90,000 killed in reprisals; approx. 240,000 conscripted, deported or missing by the end of the war. Imperial: approx. 12,000 killed. All figures disputed.

The Southern Uprising was the last great rising of the Southern Water Tribe against the Imperial occupation of the South Pole. It began in the spring of 99 AG, after two years of skirmishes and missing patrol reports, and lasted about seven months. The Empire crushed it with mortar bombardment, Breaker units and an armored assault on the Southern capital, Taluqqriaq. The uprising killed or displaced a large part of what was left of the South's population, which had already fallen to about half its pre-war number. It is also the setting of the discovery of the Avatar, who was found by Southern guerrillas in the winter of 99 AG and evacuated as the capital fell.

Background

After the failure of the earlier risings, notably that of 29 AG, which left the South with about three quarters of its pre-war population, the Empire slowly turned the South Pole into a colony and a research base, with a permanent garrison, ice mines and settlements. By 99 AG the Southern waterbenders had dwindled to a handful, and the population was about half of what it had been before the war. From 97 AG there had been small-scale skirmishes and patrols that failed to report in. Taluqqriaq, the cavern settlement beneath Wolf Cove, known as the Wolf Cave, had become the resistance's capital after the surface town was shelled, and its main base.

The Empire had sent Admiral Zhao and, in 97 AG, the officers pardoned after the Jasmine Island Mutiny to the South to pacify it. Qianchan, at war with the Empire since 30 AG, had supplied the guerrillas with surplus rifles by sea.

Course

The rising (May–October 99 AG)

The rising began on 12 May 99 AG, with coordinated attacks on Imperial depots and convoys. For about five months the resistance raided supply columns and ice mines, and ambushed patrols. Imperial reprisals fell on the villages near the attacks. By the autumn the resistance was under pressure from informers, whose reports led to ambushes on its patrols, and its losses were heavy.

The bombardment of Taluqqriaq (November–December 99 AG)

On 13 November, as part of the Empire's combined operation against both poles, the Southern Garrison began a bombardment of the glacier above Taluqqriaq with mortars, which collapsed tunnels and caverns. Breaker units dug into the ruined tunnels from above, and the town's defenders were driven back through the passages. Taluqqriaq was destroyed. About a hundred of its survivors were later taken out by an Imperial extraction team.

The Avatar

In late November a party of guerrillas, among them Chief Hakoda's children Katara and Sokka, brought a boy with arrow tattoos out of the ice near Taluqqriaq. He was in shock and said nothing for days, and some of the fighters suspected that he was a spy or an experiment. He was the Avatar, Aang, who had been frozen since 0 AG. Imperial command learned within days that the Avatar had been found in the South, and the offensive became a hunt.

The fall of the capital (December 99 AG)

On 9 December the Empire launched its final assault with light Tekkō-class tanks, Honō-class medium tanks, and Kagutsuchi II heavy tanks, supported by Breaker units. The defense of the capital collapsed that day. In the Imperial bunker complex the Avatar fought his way through the corridors against elite Arctic troops, while the wounded and the children of the resistance were taken out through the tunnels and by sea. Prince Zuko, who commanded part of the Imperial force, is recorded as badly burned in the last fighting.

Aftermath

The Empire crushed what remained of the organized resistance and punished the South severely. Villages that had sheltered guerrillas were destroyed, and about 90,000 people were killed in reprisals. Young Southerners were conscripted into labor battalions, and many were deported to work in the Empire's colonies, including the Eastern Territories, and many of them were never accounted for. By the end of the war the South's population was about 30% of its pre-war number, with about 70% dead or missing.

The Avatar's party reached Qianchan by sea, and its capital, Gaoling. Imperial intelligence heard rumors that the surviving leadership was building a new capital far to the south, and the Empire kept the interior under watch. The Southern waterbenders, who had dwindled to a handful before the uprising, were reduced further. The uprising has been called both the last act of the Subjugation of the Water Tribes and the first act of the war's end.

coalition_northern_offensive.title: Coalition Northern Offensive and the Ba Sing Se Treaty
coalition_northern_offensive.html:
A failed joint offensive by Qianchan and the Earth Kingdom, and the treaty that followed it. February–March 100 AG.

Date 12 February – 27 March 100 AG
Location The northern front: the Omashu approaches, the Hanxu–Babao line and the western plains
Result The offensive failed. The Ba Sing Se Treaty (27 March 100 AG) put the Qianchan and Earth Kingdom armies under a single command.
Belligerents Coalition: Qianchan Republic, Earth Kingdom. Empire of Tajisaki: Western Army Group.
Casualties Coalition: approx. 210,000 casualties, about 70,000 dead. Tajisaki: approx. 90,000 casualties, about 30,000 dead.

The Coalition Northern Offensive was a joint operation by the Qianchan Republic and the Earth Kingdom in the first months of 100 AG, which was meant to push north and crush the Empire of Tajisaki once and for all. It failed within six weeks, and it ended with the Ba Sing Se Treaty, which put the two armies under one command. It was the Coalition's last major offensive of the war, and the failure of its planning and security shaped the Coalition command that the Sōen strike struck in July.

Background

By the end of 99 AG the Coalition had held the Empire at the Omashu front and the Hanxu–Babao line for years, and the Empire's attention was on the poles, where it had taken Agna Qel'a in December. King Kuei, who had taken command of the war after the Dai Li coup attempt of 98 AG, and the Qianchan general staff both wanted to use the lull in the north to strike before the Empire's western army could be reinforced. The plan was for a combined armored push north from the Omashu approaches, to reach the Empire's colonies in the Hu Xin Provinces and to cut the western army's supply line.

The second Dai Li attempt

In January 100 AG, while the plan was in preparation, a group of Dai Li officers who had escaped the Great Review tried to seize the Council of Five's war room. The attempt was put down within hours, but it exposed the plan's details, forced the Coalition to change its security, and delayed the start by three weeks.

Course

The offensive began on 12 February 100 AG, with a Qianchan armored corps and an Earth Kingdom army group attacking north from the Omashu approaches. It took the first Imperial lines in three days and advanced about 60 kilometers. The Empire's response, which used air superiority and the fuel of the Si Wong oil basin, was fast. Imperial jet fighters and turboprop bombers hit the Coalition's columns and rail lines, since Qianchan's air force was committed to the Omashu front and the Earth Kingdom had none, and gas shells were used against the advance. The Western Army Group counter-attacked on 2 March from the north with armor that was fueled and supplied from the Si Wong corridor, and the Coalition's supply line, which ran back across the plains, was cut in two places. The Coalition recalled the offensive on 20 March, and withdrew to its start line.

The Ba Sing Se Treaty (27 March 100 AG)

The failure convinced the two governments that their separate commands had cost them the offensive. The Ba Sing Se Treaty, signed in the capital on 27 March, put the Qianchan and Earth Kingdom armies under a single Combined Coalition Command at Ba Sing Se, with King Kuei as its nominal supreme commander and a Qianchan general, Lieutenant General Shen Yuwen, as its chief of staff. The treaty also committed Qianchan's air force to the defense of Ba Sing Se and pooled the two states' supply. It was the first time the two allies had had a single command.

Casualties

The Coalition suffered about 210,000 casualties, about 70,000 of them dead, and the Empire about 90,000, of whom about 30,000 died.

Aftermath

The treaty gave the Coalition a unified command for the first time, but it did not have time to work. On 17 July the Sōen strike on Ba Sing Se destroyed the garrison headquarters in the Inner Ring, and the command was lost for 36 hours.

post_war_conflicts.title: Post-War Conflicts
post_war_conflicts.html:
Also known as the Famine Wars (Earth Kingdom usage). The wars and famines that followed the Hundred Year War in the Earth Kingdom, Yanakawa and the Fire Nation, 100–120 AG.

Date 100 AG – 120 AG
Location The Earth Kingdom, Yanakawa (the later United Republic of Nations) and the Fire Nation archipelago
Result The Earth Kingdom's warlords were pacified by Omashu, Ba Sing Se and Gaoling (Qianchan). Yanakawa won its independence. The Royalists won the Fire Nation Civil War. Holdouts resisted until 120 AG.
Dead About 19,000,000, mostly from famine. The third most deadly war in history.

The Post-War Conflicts were a series of connected civil wars, wars of independence and famines that followed the Hundred Year War between 100 and 120 AG. They killed about 19 million people, most of them from famine, and are counted as the third most deadly war in history, after the Hundred Year War and the Warring States wars. They were fought in three regions: the Earth Kingdom, where generals and warlords fought one another once the central command had collapsed; Yanakawa, where the colonies fought for independence; and the Fire Nation, where the Court, the Royalists and the Salvationists fought a civil war. Regional warlords, Earth Kingdom and Fire Nation alike, held out in all three until 120 AG.

Earth Kingdom warlord wars (100–112 AG)

The Earth Kingdom's war machine collapsed in the summer of 100 AG. The Sōen strike of 17 July destroyed the Coalition's command in Ba Sing Se for 36 hours, the Dai Li made a second attempt at a coup, and the provincial lords and generals, who had been held together by the war, began to fight for their own provinces, for food and for power. The Earth Kingdom, which had been starved by decades of occupation and by the siege famine, "had another seizure", as its historians put it. Imperial garrisons in the occupied northwest were cut off, and many became warlord holdings or joined them.

The fighting was less a series of battles than a long collapse of order, with provincial armies, deserters and former Imperial auxiliaries seizing granaries and rail lines and fighting each other. The famine that followed spread across the central plains and the northwest, and was the main killer. Order was restored by three powers: Omashu, which under its king kept its army intact and its western provinces fed; Ba Sing Se, where King Kuei used the centralized command he had built after 98 AG; and Gaoling, the Qianchan capital, whose armies and food convoys moved north into the southern provinces. By about 112 AG the three had pacified the warlords, who were either defeated or bought into the Kingdom's new order. About 13 million people died, most of them of hunger and disease.

The Yanakawan War of Independence (100–110 AG)

The rebellion in the Earth Kingdom's western colonies, which had begun in April 100 AG, became a war of independence after Ozai's death. It lasted until 105 AG on land, and then continued as naval skirmishes and landing attempts by the Court faction under Azula until 110 AG. The war killed about 1.2 million people. It led to the United Republic of Nations.

The Fire Nation Civil War (100–118 AG)

The war between the Court, the Royalists and the Salvationists killed about 3.5 million people, and displaced 7–10 million. See the main article.

Holdouts (to 120 AG)

Some regional warlords, in the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation, resisted stubbornly after the main wars ended. Some were former Imperial commanders, some Earth Kingdom generals, and some Salvationist remnants. They fought, or held their districts as small fiefdoms, until 120 AG, and are counted at about 800,000 dead.

Casualties

Conflict Years Dead
Earth Kingdom warlord wars and famine 100–112 AG about 13,000,000
Fire Nation Civil War 100–118 AG about 3,500,000
Yanakawan War of Independence 100–110 AG about 1,200,000
Holdouts and regional warlords to 120 AG about 800,000
Polar famine after the Imperial withdrawal 100–105 AG about 500,000
Total about 19,000,000

Historiography

Earth Kingdom histories, which are the main source for the warlord wars, give the famine as the cause of most deaths and credit the three powers with ending it. Qianchan relief records give the most detailed record of the grain convoys. The Fire Nation's and Yanakawa's histories treat their wars separately and do not count the Earth Kingdom's.
