hou_ting.title: Hou-Ting
hou_ting.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Hou-Ting
OfficeEarth Queen; 53rd monarch of the Earth Kingdom, 153–171 AG
Bornc. 126 AG
PredecessorHer father, Kuei, whom she had killed
BrotherYuhan
HeirPrince Wu, her nephew
Died8 June 171 AG, killed by a bomb at the founding parade in Ba Sing Se
ReputationHated by nearly every class from the first year

Hou-Ting was the 53rd monarch of the Earth Kingdom. She had her father King Kuei killed, and the court called it a natural death. She took the throne in 153 AG and reversed his reforms at once. Her reign was hated from the start, by peasants, merchants, lords, officers and reformers alike.

Succession

Hou-Ting was about twenty-seven and spoiled and power-hungry when she inherited the throne. Her brother Yuhan, sickly and naive, had been made a diplomat to the Fire Nation. She had been kept out of government in her father's reign and held his reforms in contempt.

Her father's death

Kuei died in 153 AG, officially peacefully in his sleep. In fact Hou-Ting had him killed. The court physician who certified the death left the palace and disappeared, and the few who knew said nothing while she held the guard. The year was that of Avatar Aang's death, when the world had no Avatar to ask questions. The rumor that the king was murdered was told in the capital from the first week, and the Collective and the Equalists repeated it in later pamphlets. How she did it is not settled.

The reversal, 153–154 AG

Within months she repealed the vote that Kuei had given to all adults in 150 AG, dismissed his ministers, restored the sale of offices and provincial tax farming and raised the land tax. In 154 AG she suspended the Assembly of the Estates and gave the Office of Public Security the power to hold prisoners without trial. Kuei had spent his reign cleaning up the war years' corruption, and she put it back.

A hated reign

She was unpopular from the first year. Peasants resented the taxes, merchants the licenses and monopolies sold to the court, the provincial lords and kings the loss of their voice, officers the sale of commissions, and Reformers the end of the Assembly. Even the Loyalists defended the throne more than they defended the queen. The Reformers proposed an “Earth Confederation” flag and constitution in 159 AG, and she buried it. The revival of the Collective in 169 AG and the movements of the unrest of 167–171 AG all grew out of her rule. The kingdom's later histories treat it as the cause of the collapse.

Death

On 8 June 171 AG the queen was killed by a bomb at the annual parade in Ba Sing Se Square, which celebrated the founding of the Earth Kingdom. The Red Lotus leader Zaheer is named as the assassin. Her nephew, Wu, succeeded her as the 54th monarch, and her death began the First Earth Civil War. The Ba Sing Se press ran the headline “The Kingdom Has Fallen!”, and mourning was small.

Open questions

Her method, her accomplices, her consort and the details of her laws are not yet written.

Wu grew up in the palace at Ba Sing Se under his aunt's rule. Both the Royalists and the Reformers named him as the ruler who might undo her work.

Puppet

Hostile newspapers called him “Traitor Prince Wu”, Hou-Ting's nephew and puppet, who made Captain Kuvira the major of the Ba Sing Se garrison after the bomb.

Exile

After the Earth Queen's death he fled to the United Republic for asylum. The Royalist armies of Ba Sing Se and Omashu fought in his name, and Kuvira was charged with protecting him in the first weeks.

Betrayal

In 174 AG Kuvira launched a military coup against King Wu. On Victory Day, 30 November 176 AG, she denounced him as a traitor and a puppet of the western nations. Later coalitions treat him as the king of a restored confederation. See Earth Empire.

kuvira.title: Kuvira
kuvira.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Kuvira
Born17 February 148 AG, in the Qianchan Federal Republic
Died4 September 181 AG, in the Western Agricultural Sector of the Earth Empire
FamilyA Qianchan father and an Omashan mother (killed c. 156 AG); adopted by Suyin Beifong
HeritageOmashu
RankCaptain (June 171 AG); major of the Ba Sing Se garrison; general (December 171 AG, the first woman general in the kingdom's history); Generalissimo
TitleGreat Uniter of the Earth State, 174–176 AG; Empress of the Earth Empire from 30 November 176 AG

Kuvira was an officer of the Earth Kingdom, of Omashan and Qianchan descent, who became the most powerful Royalist commander in the First Earth Civil War, turned on the king she had sworn to protect, and founded the Earth Empire.

Childhood

Kuvira was born in the Qianchan Federal Republic to a Qianchan father and an Omashan mother, a family whose roots were in Omashu. She had an ordinary, loving childhood.

The Heritage District, c. 156 AG

When she was eight, her family traveled to Zaofu to visit old relatives in the Heritage District. A Red Lotus bomb destroyed the building they were in. Her parents were killed, and she lived. It was later found that the attack was a terrorist plot to steal Iron Guard secrets and technology, with a young Zaheer among the plotters. See the bombing.

Zaofu

Suyin greeted her warmly and promised the orphaned girl that she would be safe in Zaofu, and adopted her. Kuvira grew up as a Beifong and learned metalbending there, and she was haunted all her life by the loss of the parents who had been taken from her, and by a promise of safety that had been broken on the day she made it.

Soldier

She left Zaofu for the Earth Kingdom's army, as a cadet, and rose quickly. By 171 AG she was a captain commanding a company of the 85th Infantry Division of Omashu, later the “Kuvira's Arms” division. The Ba Sing Se press called her Captain Kuvira Beifong.

8 June 171 AG

Her company marched in the founding parade at Ba Sing Se when the bomb exploded and the Earth Queen died. She led her unit's fight against the attackers through the night until 3 AM, in one of the sectors the fighting devastated. Prince Wu, whom hostile papers called Hou-Ting's puppet, then made her the major of the Ba Sing Se garrison. A hostile tradition says she was involved in the queen's death. See the First Earth Civil War.

For the throne, 171–174 AG

She held Ba Sing Se for the royal family, fiercely opposed the rebels and the Equalists, used her metalbending and her troops to crush the uprising, killed anyone who resisted and tried to protect the heir, Wu. She drove the rebels out of the capital, rose from captain to general in a year, and became the Generalissimo of the Eastern Army, the “grim reaper” of the war. She told her soldiers: “I will stand by the principles of the people!” She avoided human-wave attacks, saying that she valued her soldiers' lives, and her enemies called her cowardly.

The coup and the Empire

After the two Royalist armies were reunited in 174 AG, she argued that the monarchy should be reformed or abolished and that she should lead. Her rival King Shikaei of Omashu was assassinated. She launched a coup against King Wu, declared herself the Great Uniter and renamed the kingdom the Earth State. On Victory Day, 30 November 176 AG, she declared the Earth Empire. The purges of her regime, the “Green Terror”, killed or disappeared thousands.

Death

She died on 4 September 181 AG, in the Western Agricultural Sector of her Empire, in the second civil war. The circumstances are not yet written.

Open questions

Her years at Zaofu, her break with Suyin and what she knew of the Red Lotus are not yet written.

raiko.title: Raiko
raiko.html:
Raiko
OfficeMember of the National Assembly (170 AG); President of the United Republic (from 171 AG)
NationUnited Republic of Nations
Known forThe constitutional reform of 170 AG; the Raiko Amendment (171 AG)
OpponentZoltan, leader of the opposition

Raiko is a member of the National Assembly of the United Republic who in 170 AG carries the reform that replaces the council republic with a presidential state, and who becomes its first president. His name is attached to the Raiko Amendment of 171 AG.

The reform

He proposed a presidential system modeled on the Qianchan Republic, but unitary, without Qianchan's states, so that the government could act "quickly and decisively" in a crisis. He first wanted a single-chamber parliament; the compromise kept the Assembly and added a Senate chosen by proportional representation. In the Assembly debate the firebender Zoltan called him a liar and a would-be dictator; Raiko answered that the republic needed change, that the Equalist threat was "a problem solved by dialogue" and by more representation, and challenged Zoltan to a presidential election. The Republic Council approved the reform 4–2 on 18 July 170 AG, after the Supreme Court found it constitutional. The council republic was to be replaced by a president and a Senate after a transition period, and a referendum confirmed it. See Republic City crisis of 170 AG.

In the crisis

On 22 September he supported the martial law authorization "with oversight", saying that "security without restraint is not security; it is instability in another form". A police officer at a checkpoint that night said that Raiko, unlike Tarrlok, was "genuinely awake" over it. The inventor Varrick backed his candidacy; the governor of the National Capital Region, Ailani, who thought Equalists deserved a place in the Assembly, was spoken of as a rival.

The presidency

The Raiko Amendment takes effect in 171 AG and Raiko becomes President of the reformed republic. In the First Earth Civil War he sends expeditionary forces to support the Royalists.

Amon

Amon is the masked leader of the Equalists, who claims that a firebender triad scarred him for life. In fact he is Yan the Unfortunate, a former Harmonist of Water Tribe birth whose father was executed by the United Republic.

Family

Yan was born into a Water Tribe family that had settled in Republic City. His father, Yakone, was a dock foreman who was arrested after the Dock Bombing of 126 AG, which killed a member of the Republic Council. Yakone was convicted of spying and treason and executed by the republic's forces. Yan was about eight.

The Harmonists

With the Harmonists banned that year, Yan grew up in the care of its underground cells, and left them as a young man. His nickname, the Unfortunate, comes from this time.

In 170 AG

In the Republic City crisis he is "Yan" to the police and "Amon" on his leaflets. He left typewritten leaflets where a photographer would find them, and let the story of Dava reach the press at a moment of his choosing. His cells in the eastern districts were organized in groups of seven and fed through a laundry on Fengdao Street. A member of his Longshore cell, Rill, came to doubt that he had told them what he knew about Jianyu. See Republic City crisis of 170 AG.

Rise

He led the first peaceful Equalist rally in 167–168 AG. His story of the scar was invented to hide his real history, and his hatred of benders followed from it: five of the six seats on the Council that executed his father are held by benders. The movement's later escalation followed his line.

The Equalists are an anti-bender movement in the United Republic and the Earth Kingdom, founded in 167–168 AG by a masked man who calls himself Amon.

Origins

The movement held its first peaceful rally in 167–168 AG. Its leader claimed to be a victim of a firebender triad. He was in fact a former Harmonist, and the movement took in the Harmonists' grievances and some of their cadres.

Escalation

In 168 AG the Equalists attacked large companies that employed mostly benders, and in September and October they bombed rural police stations. The United Republic declared them a terrorist organization in 170 AG, after they attacked the probending arena in Republic City and began a guerrilla war.

The crisis of 170 AG

In July–October 170 AG the movement's leaflets, demonstrations and (according to the police) its bombs reshaped the republic; the account is at Republic City crisis of 170 AG.

The Harmonists' ideas descend from the Salvationist refugees', but the Equalists' politics are against benders as a class.

Red Lotus
Flag[flag image: a black lotus with a wheel at its centre on dark red]
FoundedBefore 150 AG (not settled); out of the White Lotus and the Salvationist movement
RegionInternational
IdeologyAnarchist, tied to the international leftist groups; opposition to every state
LeaderZaheer (at large)
StatusActive, 170 AG

The Red Lotus is an international underground movement that attacks the governments of the world. In 171 AG it bombs targets in the Earth Kingdom, and its bomb kills the Earth Queen Hou-Ting.

Origins and network

The Red Lotus is not a single cell but an international network tied to the leftist groups of several nations. It grew out of members of the White Lotus who broke with it and of radicals of the Salvationist movement who fled abroad after 120 AG. Its cells share people, money and safe houses with groups such as the Harmonists and the Collective, and borrow their ideas, but it does not take orders from them. This is why the same name turns up in attacks in different nations, in Zaofu in about 156 AG and in Ba Sing Se in 171 AG, with no single plot behind them.

Activity

In January 171 AG the remnants of the movement attacked the prisons where captured members were held. On 8 June 171 AG a bomb planted by Zaheer's cell at the founding parade in Ba Sing Se killed the queen and began the Earth Civil War.

Zaofu, c. 156 AG

A Red Lotus cell, with a young Zaheer, infiltrated Zaofu to steal military secrets and technology and blew up a building in the Heritage District as cover. See the Zaofu Heritage District bombing.

LocationThe Earth Kingdom
ResultThe rebel People's Republic is destroyed. The Royalist side splits, and Kuvira founds the Earth Empire
CombatantsRoyalists: the Eastern Army (Kuvira, at Ba Sing Se) and the Western Army (King Guan Shikaei, at Omashu), supplied by the United Republic and the Fire Nation; Qianchan neutral, joining the war late. Rebels: the People's Republic of Earth (Equalists, Harmonists, Collective)
TriggerThe assassination of Queen Hou-Ting by the Red Lotus leader Zaheer (8 June 171 AG)
CasualtiesNot established; thousands in the purges that followed

The First Earth Civil War (8 June 171 AG – 30 November 176 AG), also known as the Earth Kingdom Civil War, was a major internal conflict fought across the Earth Kingdom between the royalist government and a coalition of revolutionary movements seeking to overthrow the monarchy and establish a new political order. The war began during the political crisis following the assassination of Queen Hou-Ting in Ba Sing Se on 8 June 171 AG. It developed into a nationwide civil war involving royalist armies, revolutionary forces, peasant insurgencies, radical urban organizations, and competing regional authorities.

The conflict pitted the Royalists, principally divided between the Eastern Army under the rising commander Kuvira and the Western Army under King Guan Shikaei of Omashu, against the revolutionary People's Republic of Earth, a coalition encompassing the Equalists, Harmonists, and Collective. Although these organizations shared opposition to the existing political order, they differed considerably in their ideological objectives, preferred methods of government, and visions for the future of the Earth Kingdom.

The assassination of Hou-Ting was the immediate catalyst for the war, but its origins extended back decades. The reversal of King Kuei's reforms, the expansion of authoritarian government, corruption, economic grievances, regional inequality, and the suppression of political opposition weakened the monarchy's legitimacy. Underground revolutionary organizations exploited these conditions, attracting support among sections of the peasantry, industrial workers, students, political radicals, and disaffected officials. The monarchy's attempts to suppress opposition further intensified the crisis.

The Royalists initially retained control of the principal administrative centers, but the rebellion spread across the kingdom. By the end of 171 AG, revolutionary armies had established extensive territorial control, while the Eastern and Western Royalist commands pursued separate campaigns with differing equipment, logistics, and military doctrines. The war subsequently became characterized by conventional offensives, guerrilla warfare, urban fighting, political purges, and widespread civilian suffering. 

The revolutionary coalition gradually disintegrated because of internal factionalism, competing political objectives, and increasingly violent struggles over territory and authority. Royalist forces regained the initiative during 173 AG and launched major reunification operations in 174 AG. The resulting victory destroyed the principal institutions of the People's Republic, but the Royalist alliance itself subsequently fractured. Following the death of Guan Shikaei and the seizure of power by Kuvira, the monarchy was displaced by an increasingly centralized military dictatorship.

The war formally ended on 30 November 176 AG, when Kuvira proclaimed the Earth Empire. Isolated revolutionary guerrillas continued operating into 177 AG. Although the Royalists defeated the revolutionary coalition, the conflict did not establish a lasting political settlement and contributed to the conditions preceding the Second Earth Civil War in 181 AG.

Background

The Earth Kingdom under King Kuei

The political origins of the civil war lay in the long deterioration of the Earth Kingdom's governing institutions. Although the monarchy retained its historical legitimacy and the kingdom possessed enormous territory and population, effective political authority was unevenly distributed. Provincial officials, military commanders, court factions, and entrenched bureaucratic institutions frequently exercised considerable autonomy.

King Kuei, who died in 153 AG, had attempted to address several of these structural weaknesses through reforms intended to improve government accountability and restore the authority of the central state. His reform program sought to reduce the influence of entrenched court interests and improve the administration of the provinces.

Kuei's death ended this period of reform. His daughter, Hou-Ting, succeeded him and reversed important elements of his father's policies. Her government increasingly relied on coercion, political patronage, surveillance, and the suppression of opposition to maintain its authority.

Although the monarchy continued to claim that it represented the unity and historical continuity of the Earth Kingdom, its ability to command popular loyalty deteriorated. The reversal of reforms alienated sections of the bureaucracy and educated elite, while corruption and uneven administration contributed to resentment among ordinary inhabitants.

The circumstances surrounding Kuei's death later became controversial. Although officially reported as a death in his sleep, accounts within the setting attribute his death to Hou-Ting herself. The allegations contributed to the later delegitimization of her reign, although their precise political significance varied among competing historical interpretations.

Hou-Ting's government and the growth of opposition

During the years following her accession, Hou-Ting's government increasingly centralized political authority around the monarch and her immediate circle. Institutions that might otherwise have mediated disputes between the monarchy, provincial authorities, and the population became less effective.

Political opposition developed through several overlapping channels. Reformist scholars and former officials objected to the reversal of Kuei's policies. Students and urban intellectuals criticized corruption and the absence of meaningful political representation. Workers and peasants expressed grievances over economic inequality, administrative abuses, and the concentration of power in the hands of privileged groups.

These groups did not initially constitute a unified revolutionary movement. Many sought constitutional reforms, accountable government, or limits on royal authority rather than the immediate destruction of the monarchy. Others advocated republicanism, socialism, regional autonomy, or the abolition of established political and social hierarchies.

The government's response helped radicalize the opposition. Restrictions on political activity, suppression of demonstrations, and the treatment of reform advocates as threats to state security convinced some opponents that peaceful reform was becoming impossible.

Consequently, underground political organizations gained influence. Exiled radicals from the United Republic, Qianchan, and the Water Tribes contributed to the circulation of revolutionary ideas, organizational methods, and political propaganda. By the 160s AG, networks that had previously appeared marginal had begun establishing contacts across provincial and urban boundaries.

Revolutionary movements

The revolutionary opposition was ideologically diverse. Its eventual coalition brought together organizations whose common hostility toward the monarchy concealed substantial disagreements over the society they intended to create.

The Equalists opposed the political and social privileges associated with bending. Their ideology presented bending as a structural source of inequality and argued that a just society required the destruction of the institutions that enabled benders to dominate government, security, and public life. The movement attracted radicalized non-benders and militants influenced by Equalist organizations operating outside the Earth Kingdom.

The Harmonists advocated a socialist political order intended to replace the monarchy and existing economic hierarchy. Their program appealed to some workers, students, and radical intellectuals who believed that economic inequality could not be corrected without a fundamental transformation of the state. Their methods became increasingly violent as the conflict intensified.

The Collective opposed the concentration of authority in Ba Sing Se and supported the transformation of the kingdom into autonomous or independent political units. Its adherents included regional separatists, local revolutionary committees, and insurgents who regarded the central monarchy as incapable of governing the kingdom fairly.

The three movements differed in their ultimate objectives. Equalist politics centered on the relationship between bending and power; Harmonist politics emphasized revolutionary social and economic restructuring; and the Collective prioritized regional self-government and the dismantling of centralized authority.

Their cooperation was therefore tactical rather than ideological. A common enemy enabled them to coordinate their activities, but their disagreements would eventually become one of the principal weaknesses of the revolutionary coalition.

The Red Lotus occupied a separate position within this political landscape. Although it opposed established authority and shared certain revolutionary assumptions, it was an extremist organization with its own objectives and operational structure. Its role in the assassination of Hou-Ting should not be confused with the entire leftist opposition or treated as proof that every revolutionary organization directly participated in the attack.

Outbreak of the war

The assassination of Hou-Ting

On 8 June 171 AG, during the annual parade in Ba Sing Se Square, an attack against Queen Hou-Ting's motorcade triggered the decisive breakdown of political order. The parade was a major state ceremony with a history extending back approximately four thousand years and was intended to demonstrate the continuity and authority of the monarchy.

The Red Lotus, led by Zaheer, carried out the assassination operation. An explosion struck near the royal motorcade, killing Hou-Ting and numerous other people. Armed militants subsequently attacked security personnel and targets in the square using firearms and explosives.

The ensuing battle continued into the early hours of 9 June. Royalist troops and security forces fought to regain control of the area while the authorities attempted to determine the extent of the attack and establish the fate of senior government officials.

The assassination removed the monarch at a moment when the political system was already weakened by years of unrest. It also disrupted the normal succession of authority and intensified uncertainty within the government, security services, and military command.

Prince Wu fled to the United Republic, further complicating efforts to restore the monarchy's authority. The royalist establishment retained loyal military formations, but it no longer possessed an uncontested political center capable of commanding universal obedience across the kingdom.

The attack did not, by itself, create the revolutionary movements or their grievances. Rather, it provided the immediate opening through which existing underground organizations, armed groups, and popular opposition could challenge the state openly.

The beginning of the civil war

Most historians in the setting identify 8 June 171 AG as the beginning of the First Earth Civil War. The date marks the transition from prolonged political unrest and underground opposition to an open armed struggle over control of the Earth Kingdom.

The classification reflects the broader character of the conflict. Although the assassination was the immediate trigger, the war emerged from the interaction of revolutionary organization, popular grievances, regional discontent, and the monarchy's inability to manage a political succession crisis.

In the days following the attack, revolutionary groups and local insurgents mobilized across multiple provinces. Some peasants and workers joined armed organizations out of ideological commitment; others acted in response to local grievances, coercion, or the collapse of established authority. In several areas, existing political disputes escalated into armed confrontations between revolutionary committees, royal officials, and loyalist military units.

The revolutionaries presented the crisis as an opportunity to destroy the monarchy and establish a fundamentally different state. Royalist authorities, by contrast, characterized the uprising as an assault on public order and the territorial unity of the kingdom.

The first days of the conflict were marked by confused command arrangements, contradictory reports, and localized fighting. Neither side initially possessed complete control over the wider political situation. As the rebellion expanded, however, the conflict developed into a nationwide struggle involving organized armies and competing claims to national legitimacy.

The fall of the old political order

The initial royalist response focused on restoring control over Ba Sing Se and preventing the revolutionary organizations from establishing a permanent presence in the capital.

By 10 June 171 AG, royalist forces had suppressed the principal uprising within the city. This success prevented the immediate loss of the capital but failed to end the wider rebellion. The government's subsequent crackdown, including arrests and violent repression, intensified resistance in areas where revolutionary groups had already established underground networks.

The capital's survival therefore concealed a broader strategic problem. Royalist forces could retake individual districts and suppress urban demonstrations, but they could not simultaneously restore political legitimacy, secure the provinces, and eliminate the revolutionary organizations operating beyond the capital.

The insurgency expanded as local movements, radicalized citizens, and armed groups exploited the disruption of central authority. In some areas, revolutionary forces received substantial support; in others, they imposed control through intimidation and violence. The degree of popular participation varied considerably between regions.

The war consequently became more than a contest between the monarchy and a single revolutionary organization. It developed into a struggle among competing political projects, each claiming to represent the future of the Earth Kingdom.

Belligerents

Royalist coalition

The Royalists sought to preserve the territorial unity of the Earth Kingdom and defeat the revolutionary coalition. Their forces were divided principally between two major military commands.

Eastern Army. Based around Ba Sing Se, the Eastern Army became the principal royalist force in the central and eastern theaters. It initially operated under the pressure of defending the capital and suppressing the rebellion in the surrounding provinces. Captain Kuvira, serving with the 85th Infantry Division during the opening events, rose rapidly through the command structure as the conflict intensified. Her performance in the capital and subsequent campaigns established her reputation as an effective and ruthless military commander.

Western Army. Based around Omashu, the Western Army was led by King Guan Shikaei. It operated under a different strategic and political environment from the Eastern Army, drawing support from western royalist territories and benefiting from access to external supply routes. Its equipment, logistical arrangements, and operational methods differed from those of Kuvira's command.

Despite their common objective, the two armies were not politically identical. Their commanders maintained separate power bases and pursued the war under different regional conditions. This division initially complicated coordination and would later become a central issue in the postwar struggle for authority.

The Royalists received external assistance from the United Republic and the Fire Nation. The United Republic provided expeditionary support, while Fire Lord Izumi's government supplied medical materials and firearms, including outdated weapons inherited from earlier conflicts.

Qianchan initially maintained a neutral position while allowing royalist troops and refugees to use its borders. Its policy reflected concern over the instability spreading across the western frontier and the uncertain political future of the Earth Kingdom.

Revolutionary coalition

The principal revolutionary forces organized under the banner of the People's Republic of Earth, a provisional political project intended to replace the monarchy. Its armed forces were divided into Northern, Central, and Eastern armies, supported by regional revolutionary committees and affiliated organizations.

The coalition's three principal political components were the Equalists, Harmonists, and Collective. Their cooperation provided the rebellion with a broad ideological base, but the absence of a universally accepted political program made the coalition difficult to govern.

The Equalists sought to eliminate bending-based privilege and establish a political order in which bending could no longer determine social status or access to power. Their methods included clandestine organization, urban militancy, and suicide attacks.

The Harmonists sought a socialist republic and the transformation of the kingdom's economic and political structure. Their armed organizations employed bombings, terror attacks, and chemical or gas-based attacks during the war.

The Collective pursued the fragmentation or radical decentralization of the kingdom. Its forces relied heavily on guerrilla warfare, local mobilization, and attacks against royalist communications and administrative structures.

The People's Republic's nominal unity concealed considerable disagreement. Some commanders prioritized conventional military victory, while others favored prolonged insurgency or local political control. These differences became increasingly damaging as the war progressed and the coalition began losing territory.

Course of the war

171 AG: The revolutionary offensive

The first year of the war was characterized by rapid escalation, the expansion of revolutionary territorial control, and the emergence of separate regional fronts.

In the northwest, revolutionary forces launched offensives intended to isolate Ba Sing Se and weaken the Royalists' control over the surrounding countryside. Fighting approached the city's defensive perimeter, and sections of its western walls were destroyed during the campaign. The survival of the capital became a major political and military concern for the Royalist leadership.

In the central theater, the fighting developed into a prolonged struggle involving forces equipped with weapons and matériel inherited from the Hundred Year War. Neither side secured a decisive advantage during the early months, and the front became increasingly costly to maintain.

In the eastern provinces, the conflict assumed a particularly violent character. Revolutionary and royalist forces fought over strategically important towns and transport routes, while political intimidation and reprisals against civilians intensified. Yuanping, Zhaomen, and Sanjiang became associated with extreme violence and were subsequently described in accounts of the war as martyrdom cities.

The fighting demonstrated that the revolutionary movement had developed beyond a collection of isolated underground organizations. Its forces could coordinate operations across several theaters and exploit the weakness of the central state.

However, the Royalists also demonstrated their capacity to recover from the initial crisis. Their survival in Ba Sing Se, combined with the continued existence of the Western Army, prevented the revolutionary coalition from achieving a rapid and decisive victory.

Kuvira's rise

Kuvira's emergence as a leading Royalist commander was one of the most consequential developments of the opening campaign.

Initially serving as a captain in the 85th Infantry Division from Omashu, she became prominent during the fighting surrounding Ba Sing Se. Her actions during the initial uprising and subsequent operations brought her to the attention of senior Royalist officers.

By the end of 171 AG, Kuvira had been promoted to general. She became the first woman in the Earth Kingdom to attain that rank, marking a significant institutional milestone within the kingdom's military establishment.

Her rise was based on a combination of operational effectiveness, organizational discipline, and the willingness to employ severe measures against revolutionary forces. As the Eastern Army's influence expanded, Kuvira became increasingly associated with a centralized, military-led conception of national reunification.

At this stage, her public objective remained the restoration of order and the defeat of the revolutionary coalition. The political consequences of her growing authority would become clearer in the final stages of the war.

172 AG: The struggle for the initiative

By 172 AG, the revolutionary coalition faced mounting difficulties. Its forces had expanded rapidly, but maintaining coordination across the different fronts became increasingly challenging.

In the northwest, Royalist operations sought to divide revolutionary formations and prevent them from concentrating their forces against Ba Sing Se. Fighting in the northeastern mountains placed additional pressure on insurgent supply lines and communications.

In the eastern theater, Royalist troops conducted operations in difficult jungle terrain. The campaign imposed heavy logistical demands on both sides, and the revolutionaries eventually lost ground as their forces struggled to sustain the fight.

The Western Army simultaneously conducted a major campaign in the Si Wong region between May and December. The fighting represented an important effort to recover territory and disrupt the revolutionary coalition's regional position. Royalist estimates placed rebel casualties at approximately 90,000 and Royalist casualties at approximately 10,000. These figures remain unverified and should be treated as wartime estimates rather than established totals.

The year also exposed the political costs of foreign assistance. In January, student demonstrations in Omashu escalated into major riots directed against the presence of foreign troops. The disturbances became the largest civil unrest since the reign of Kuei and revealed that opposition to the revolution did not necessarily imply support for foreign intervention or the Royalist military establishment.

The Royalists increasingly faced a dual problem: defeating the revolutionary armies while preventing their own political coalition from losing popular legitimacy.

173 AG: Fragmentation of the revolutionary coalition

The balance of the war shifted further toward the Royalists during 173 AG. Revolutionary forces lost territory, suffered from organizational breakdown, and increasingly struggled to coordinate their operations.

The People's Republic continued to field substantial forces, but the coalition's political disagreements became more damaging as its military position deteriorated. Rival factions disputed command authority, strategic priorities, and the distribution of resources. Local commanders increasingly pursued their own objectives, sometimes at the expense of the broader revolutionary effort.

The resulting fragmentation undermined the coalition's ability to organize coherent defensive lines or mount sustained counteroffensives. In some areas, armed factions fought one another while Royalist forces advanced against them.

Civilian populations suffered as the conflict became more fragmented. Revolutionary groups resorted increasingly to coercion and attacks against civilians, while Royalist operations and reprisals inflicted further destruction. The distinction between organized military fronts and local political violence became progressively less clear.

The Eastern Army acquired a particularly feared reputation during this period. Its operations, together with Kuvira's growing prominence, contributed to the image of a force capable of pursuing revolutionary formations relentlessly. The 37th Armored Division, known as the Sand Stalkers, became associated with hit-and-run operations developed during the Si Wong campaign.

The division's methods reflected the increasingly mobile character of the fighting. Rather than relying exclusively on static territorial defense, its units sought to exploit gaps in revolutionary deployments, disrupt movement, and strike vulnerable formations.

By the end of 173 AG, the revolutionary coalition remained dangerous but had lost much of its ability to act as a unified political and military organization.

174 AG: Royalist reunification and Kuvira's coup

The decisive phase of the war began in 174 AG, when the Eastern and Western Royalist commands undertook major operations to reunify their forces and destroy the remaining organized revolutionary resistance.

The Reunification Blitz, conducted between April and June, restored coordination between the principal Royalist armies. Subsequent operations in the southeast further weakened the revolutionary position and contributed to the collapse of the People's Republic's remaining institutions.

The destruction of the revolutionary coalition did not resolve the political differences within the Royalist alliance. The Eastern Army under Kuvira and the Western Army under Guan Shikaei had cooperated against a common enemy, but their leaders held competing visions for the postwar state.

The central question was whether the Earth Kingdom would return to monarchical government or be reorganized under a more centralized political and military system. Guan Shikaei retained his own regional authority and political following, while Kuvira's influence rested increasingly on the Eastern Army and her claim to be the principal architect of reunification.

The dispute escalated into a struggle for supreme authority. Guan Shikaei was killed during the resulting political crisis, and Kuvira seized power.

Her coup ended the effective unity of the Royalist coalition. The monarchy was displaced by a military dictatorship that presented itself as the necessary instrument of national reconstruction. The new regime subsequently became known as the Earth State, developing into the Earth Empire proclaimed in 176 AG.

The Royalists had defeated the revolution, but their victory did not restore the political order that had existed before 171 AG. Instead, the destruction of the old monarchy and the defeat of the People's Republic created the conditions for Kuvira's consolidation of power.

175–176 AG: The final campaigns

After Kuvira's seizure of power, the remaining revolutionary forces continued fighting across several regions. Their resistance no longer posed the same conventional threat as the armies of the People's Republic during the early years of the war, but isolated formations remained capable of prolonging the conflict.

In late 175 AG, Royalist forces captured the Eastern Air Temple, which had become one of the remaining centers of organized resistance.

In the central regions, Harmonist forces continued holding an urban stronghold until February 176 AG. Its eventual fall marked another stage in the destruction of the revolutionary coalition's remaining territorial bases.

In the northwest, Royalist operations pushed Equalist formations toward the Northern Air Temple. The remaining groups increasingly relied on guerrilla tactics rather than conventional operations, exploiting remote terrain and fragmented local authority.

Qianchan, which had initially maintained neutrality, eventually intervened on Kuvira's side in the southeast. Its decision reflected growing concern over the consequences of prolonged instability and the emergence of a powerful, expansionist military government along its frontier.

On 30 November 176 AG, Kuvira proclaimed the Earth Empire on Victory Day, formally declaring the end of the principal civil war. The declaration presented the new regime as the culmination of national reunification and the restoration of state authority.

Isolated revolutionary guerrilla units continued operating into 177 AG. Their eventual neutralization marked the end of the principal organized resistance associated with the First Earth Civil War.

Foreign involvement

United Republic

The United Republic supported the Royalists by dispatching expeditionary forces. Its intervention reflected concern that the collapse of the Earth Kingdom could destabilize neighboring territories and threaten regional security.

The Republic's involvement was politically complicated. The Earth Kingdom's crisis involved revolutionary movements whose ideologies had connections to radical organizations operating within the Republic itself. Supporting the Royalists therefore offered an opportunity to contain the spread of armed revolutionary movements, but it also associated the Republic with a government widely criticized for authoritarianism.

The presence of foreign troops generated opposition in parts of the Earth Kingdom, most notably during the Omashu riots of 172 AG. This demonstrated that military assistance could strengthen the Royalist position without resolving the political grievances that had contributed to the rebellion.

Fire Nation

The Fire Nation, under Fire Lord Izumi, provided medical supplies and firearms to the Royalists. The weapons included outdated matériel inherited from the Hundred Year War.

Its assistance contributed to the Royalist war effort while limiting the extent of its direct commitment. The Fire Nation's position also reflected the broader strategic interest in preventing a revolutionary victory that might produce further regional instability.

Qianchan Republic

Qianchan initially maintained neutrality. It allowed Royalist forces and refugees to use its borders but did not immediately commit itself to the conflict.

This policy allowed Qianchan to preserve flexibility while the outcome remained uncertain. The deterioration of the revolutionary coalition and Kuvira's growing military dominance eventually changed the strategic calculation.

Qianchan entered the conflict on Kuvira's side during the later stages, particularly in the southeast. Its intervention helped bring the war to a close, but it also placed the Republic in a difficult relationship with the emerging Earth Empire.

Qianchan's late intervention did not necessarily indicate ideological agreement with Kuvira's government. Rather, it reflected the difficult choices facing neighboring powers when confronted with a powerful military state emerging from a prolonged civil war.

Ideology and political character of the conflict

The First Earth Civil War was not simply a contest between monarchy and republicanism. It involved competing visions of social equality, economic organization, national unity, regional autonomy, and the legitimate use of state power.

The revolutionary coalition drew support from groups that had been marginalized by the monarchy, but it never developed a universally accepted political program. The Equalists, Harmonists, and Collective could agree on the destruction of the existing order without agreeing on what should replace it.

This contradiction became increasingly important as the People's Republic gained territory. A movement capable of uniting opponents of the monarchy proved less capable of governing a diverse country once the immediate threat of royalist authority had been removed.

The Royalists, meanwhile, fought under the banner of territorial unity and public order. Yet their victory also destroyed the institutional arrangements that had justified the monarchy. Kuvira's coup transformed the Royalist war effort into the foundation of a new authoritarian state.

The conflict therefore produced an outcome different from either the restoration of the old monarchy or the revolutionary transformation promised by the People's Republic. The Earth Kingdom survived as a territorial entity, but its political system was replaced by a centralized military dictatorship.

Aftermath

Proclamation of the Earth Empire

Kuvira's proclamation on 30 November 176 AG formally ended the principal phase of the First Earth Civil War and established the Earth Empire as the successor to the wartime Earth State.

The new regime justified its authority through the promise of national reunification, administrative efficiency, and the prevention of renewed fragmentation. Its emergence reflected the destruction of the monarchy, the defeat of the revolutionary coalition, and the consolidation of military power during the final years of the war.

The proclamation did not immediately eliminate political opposition. The continuation of guerrilla resistance into 177 AG demonstrated that military victory had not produced universal acceptance of the new government.

Casualties and destruction

The total number of military and civilian casualties remains undetermined. Existing accounts describe extensive fighting across several theaters, the destruction of urban districts, and severe losses during the Si Wong campaign and the battles around Ba Sing Se.

Royalist estimates of approximately 90,000 rebel casualties and 10,000 Royalist casualties during the Western Army's 172 AG Si Wong campaign are frequently cited in accounts of the war. However, these figures have not been independently established and should not be treated as a comprehensive casualty count for the entire conflict.

The war also produced large-scale displacement, disruption of regional trade, destruction of infrastructure, and the weakening of institutions responsible for civilian administration. Political purges and reprisals continued during and after the collapse of the revolutionary coalition.

Political consequences

The principal consequence of the war was the destruction of the prewar political order. The monarchy failed to survive the crisis that began with Hou-Ting's assassination, while the People's Republic failed to establish a durable revolutionary state.

The Royalist victory was itself incomplete. Kuvira's coup ended the alliance that had defeated the revolution and replaced it with a new centralized dictatorship. The political grievances that had contributed to the war were not necessarily resolved by the destruction of the revolutionary organizations.

The conflict also transformed the regional balance of power. The United Republic, Fire Nation, and Qianchan had all become involved in determining the future of the Earth Kingdom, while the emergence of the Earth Empire created a new strategic challenge for neighboring states.

The war is consequently regarded as a decisive turning point in the political history of the Earth Kingdom: the end of the monarchy, the destruction of the People's Republic, and the rise of Kuvira's military state.

Open questions

The casualty figures, the battle accounts and the part of Qianchan and the United Republic are not yet written.

earth_empire.html:

Earth Empire
Flag[flag image: green and white; a sun with a metal-bending emblem. Flag art will be linked later]
Founded30 November 176 AG (as the Earth State, 174 AG)
CapitalBa Sing Se
RulerEmpress Kuvira, the Great Uniter
GovernmentMilitary dictatorship with a cult of personality
PredecessorEarth Kingdom

The Earth Empire is the militarist state that Kuvira founds in the Earth Kingdom's lands after the First Earth Civil War. It lies outside the 170 AG of the country profiles and appears here as a later development.

The Earth State, 174–176 AG

After the coup against King Wu, the kingdom was renamed the Earth State and ruled as a military dictatorship by Generalissimo Kuvira. Propaganda and censorship covered the coup and the killing of King Shikaei, claiming a Fire Nation spy had done it. A victory parade in Ba Sing Se celebrated the state, and the regime purged officers and officials loyal to Shikaei or Wu in the Green Terror: arrests, tortures and disappearances in secret prisons, among them Lake Laogai. The Earth State restarted a nuclear weapon project and was xenophobic toward the western countries.

The Empire

On 30 November 176 AG, in the square where the Earth Queen was killed, Kuvira declared the birth of the Earth Empire and denounced King Wu as a traitor and a puppet of the western nations. She united most of the kingdom by offering protection and stability in exchange for loyalty, and ruled with an iron fist. Those who refused to join, among them the city of Zaofu and the United Republic of Nations, were oppressed.

Flags

The flag of 171 AG, still in use, has a metal-bending emblem in a sun, which denotes the military faction Kuvira led. Two horizontal lines above and below the emblem are the walls of Ba Sing Se, the last stronghold of the kingdom in the Hundred Year War. Six vertical lines stand for the six military factions that backed order after the Earth Queen's death, and four pillars for the four great cities, probably Ba Sing Se, Omashu, Huamu and Shaozu. The sun is the hope and future of the country. The Earth State (174–176 AG) had a green flag with a white flower around the seal.

Flags proposed and rejected: the Royalist Proposal (171 AG), turned down by the other factions; the “New” Earth States Proposal (172 AG), by a civil servant, similar to the Earth Republic flag in a green scheme, rejected by Ba Sing Se as a bad omen, and the civil servant was later executed; the Si Wong Proposal (172 AG), by a general of Kuvira's fighting the Sand Union, which she thought needed more green; and the Unificationist Proposal (173 AG), by a general who wanted to annex the southern lands to the kingdom, which she rejected as insane and impractical. The Navy, Air Force and Army have their own flags, each with the coat of arms, and the Army has a variant without it. The 85th Mechanized Infantry Division (“Kuvira's Arms”), the 3rd Airborne Division (“Ghosts”) and the 37th Armored Division (“Sand Stalkers”) are the “Big Three” that won the civil war.

Open questions

The structure of the government, the size of the army and the relations with the United Republic and Qianchan are not yet written. A coalition with Qianchan is working to restore the kingdom or the confederation of King Wu.

unrest_of_167_171_ag.title: Unrest of 167–171 AG
unrest_of_167_171_ag.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Unrest of 167–171 AG
Date167–171 AG
WhereThe United Republic, the Earth Kingdom, the Fire Nation and the Water Tribes
MovementsEqualists; Harmonists; Collective; Thunderbolt sect; Red Sun Group; Red Lotus
BackgroundThe spread of the Salvationists after the Fire Nation Civil War

The unrest of 167–171 AG is the wave of radical movements that rose in all four nations in the years before the Earth and Water Tribe civil wars. Several descend from the Salvationists, whose members spread across the world during and after the Fire Nation Civil War.

The events of July to October 170 AG are covered at Republic City crisis of 170 AG.

Year by year

YearEvents
167–168 AGThe Equalists are founded; their masked leader holds the first peaceful rally. He claims to be the victim of a firebender triad, but is Yan the Unfortunate, a former Harmonist, whose Water Tribe father was executed by the republic in 126 AG.
168 AGThe Harmonists, suppressed for 42 years, secretly revive. The Equalists escalate and target big companies that employ mostly benders; in September and October they bomb rural police stations.
169 AGA faction of the Salvationists breaks away as the Thunderbolt sect. In the Earth Kingdom the Collective revives among peasants and workers who are dissatisfied with Queen Hou-Ting's reversal of King Kuei's reforms.
170 AGKorra finishes her training in three elements and goes to the United Republic to learn airbending from Tenzin. The United Republic declares the Equalists a terrorist organization after they attack the probending arena in Republic City and begin a guerrilla war. The Thunderbolt sect clashes with the Salvationists over their founder's legacy.
171 AGJanuary–July: a few reports of non-benders gaining airbending. January: the Red Lotus attacks prisons holding its members. The Red Sun Group emerges in the Water Tribes, and its crisis lasts until November. June: Red Lotus bombings in the Earth Kingdom, which kill the Earth Queen and start the First Earth Civil War.

The Salvationist thread

The Salvationists spread across the world during the Fire Nation Civil War, and after 120 AG the survivors fled to the United Republic or to Qianchan's southern island chain. See Salvationists. The Harmonists, the Collective and the Thunderbolt sect have Salvationist roots, and so does part of the Red Lotus, an international network that also draws on White Lotus dissidents and links the leftist groups. The Equalists and the Red Sun Group do not necessarily.

Open questions

Who funds the movements, how far they cooperate and what the governments knew are not yet written.

Died29 November 174 AG (assassinated at a military parade in Omashu)
RuleBecame king in 159 AG at sixteen (some accounts say 161 AG)
AlliesThe United Republic and the Fire Nation

Guan Shikaei (“the warrior”) was the young king of Omashu and the commander of the Western Army, the other Royalist force of the First Earth Civil War.

Career

Trained at the Omashu Military Academy, he became the youngest general in the kingdom's history at twenty-eight and led the Western Army against the rebels. He was a loyal supporter of the monarchy and a fierce opponent of the leftist movements. He was determined to eradicate their ideology from his region and used violence against the rebels and the Equalists, and he was condemned for it by some media. His line was “No traitors states, they deserve death!”

Rival of Kuvira

The Western Army fought with the support of the United Republic and the Fire Nation, and was joined by foreign volunteers. After the two Royalist armies united in 174 AG he argued that the monarchy should be kept and King Wu's authority respected, against Kuvira. An Equalist university student shot him at a parade in Omashu in November 174 AG. Kuvira's regime claimed a Fire Nation spy had killed him.

Honors

The restored kingdom of 171–176 AG gave him its highest honor after his death.

Open questions

His family and who ordered the assassination are not yet written.

FateDissolved in 176 AG, defeated by the Royalists

The People's Republic of Earth was the provisional state of the rebels in the First Earth Civil War, set up in the first weeks of the war by the Equalists, the Harmonists and the Collective.

Structure

The state was led by the three factions, each with its own army (the Northern, Central and Eastern armies) and its own commissars. They were united under a “popular front”. In fact it was a puppet of the international leftist groups, which had more power than the provisional government and quarreled with each other.

Decline

Its internal conflicts and executions grew in 172 AG, and the factions became greedy and corrupt. In 174 AG they tried to unify in a one-state party, which failed. The state shrank, and was dissolved in 176 AG when the Royalists, supplied by the United Republic and the Fire Nation, defeated the last rebels. A historian called it “a burning mess in summary”.

Open questions

Its capital, its leaders and its laws are not yet written.

Kiko, known as Princess Ayako, is the younger daughter of Fire Lord Izumi and one of the best-selling music artists of the Fire Nation. She is the second non-bender born into the royal family in over five hundred years.

Early life

She is the second child of Izumi and Ryota, born in the reign of her grandfather Zuko. She was educated, with her brother, at the Royal Gakusiyo Academy and the Royal University of Mutsukawa, where she studied fine arts and graduated with honors in 175 AG. She signed with AZura in 170 AG.

Marriage

She met Kei Seinaka, a law student, at the university, and the engagement was kept secret for several years to protect her career. They married in 175 AG, and she took the stage name that she still uses.

Zaofu is the autonomous region and city of the Beifong family in the Qianchan Republic, the home of metalbending. It writes its own rules on police, education and land.

Heritage District

The Heritage District is the old quarter, where families that came from the Earth Kingdom and Qianchan's other regions kept their houses and their relatives. It was the site of the Red Lotus bombing in about 156 AG.

Military research

Zaofu's metalbenders are restricted to trained personnel, and the Iron Guard fields its Tiejia-III power armor, which was developed here.

zaofu_heritage_district_bombing.title: Zaofu Heritage District bombing
zaofu_heritage_district_bombing.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.

Datec. 156 AG
LocationThe Heritage District, Zaofu (Qianchan)
PerpetratorsA Red Lotus cell, including a young Zaheer
TargetThe military research of the Zaofu Iron Guard: secrets and technology
CasualtiesNot established. Among the dead were the parents of an eight-year-old girl, Kuvira

The Zaofu Heritage District bombing was a Red Lotus attack in about 156 AG in which a residential building exploded. It looked at first like an attack on civilians, and it turned out to be a terrorist plot to steal Zaofu's military secrets and technology.

The attack

A building in the Heritage District blew up in the middle of the day while a family from out of town was visiting its old relatives. The dead included the parents of Kuvira, who was eight, and who survived.

The plot

The investigation found that the Red Lotus had infiltrated Zaofu to steal secrets and technology from the Iron Guard's research, and that the explosion was meant to cover the theft and draw the guards away. A cell led by a young Zaheer was identified. Whether it got away with anything, and how many escaped, is not settled.

Aftermath

Zaofu tightened its security, and Suyin Beifong took the orphaned girl in and adopted her. The attack is the origin of the Red Lotus's long enmity with the Beifong family.

Open questions

The exact date, the casualty count and what was taken are not yet written.

Yakone was a Water Tribe dock foreman in Republic City who was convicted in 126 AG of spying and treason and executed by the forces of the United Republic. He was found to have killed one of the Republic Council's members. He was the father of Amon.

Charges

The prosecution said that Yakone passed harbor and shipping information to a foreign power, which the wiki has not yet named, and that he killed a Council member in the Dock Bombing. His guilt rests on a military tribunal and little else, and the Harmonists said he was framed.

Execution

He was shot after a short military trial, and the Council used the case to ban the Harmonists. His son, then about eight, grew up as an orphan of the movement.

Open questions

The foreign power he spied for, the name of the dead councillor and whether he was a Harmonist himself are not yet written.

The Dock Bombing of 126 AG was an attack on the Republic City docks, during a dock strike, that killed a member of the Republic Council. The republic blamed the foreman Yakone, executed him as a spy and a traitor, and banned the Harmonists.

Background

The strike of the Republic City dockers was organized by workers close to the Harmonists, the movement of the Fire Nation exiles of the Salvationists and the republic's labor.

The attack

A bomb went off at the docks where the Council member was visiting. The councillor died. The republic held that Yakone had planted it and that he had been passing information abroad.

Aftermath

The Council banned the Harmonists in 126 AG and the movement went underground for 42 years. The son of the executed man, Yan, later founded the Equalists.

Open questions

The councillor's name and seat, the bomber and the casualty count are not yet written.

republic_city_crisis_of_170_ag.title: Republic City crisis of 170 AG
republic_city_crisis_of_170_ag.html:
Dates marked c. are reconstructed. The sources give most events only relative to one another ("three weeks after", "six weeks since"), and they disagree in places; see Sources and discrepancies. Casualty figures are in-universe estimates.
Republic City crisis of 170 AG
Datec. 7 July – c. 1 October 170 AG
PlaceRepublic City (Jianyu, Longshore, Asagawa, Wada); Yu Dao; the Fujishihoro highlands and the Hengdong agricultural belt
ContextThe unrest of 167–171 AG; the constitutional reform of the United Republic
PartiesThe Republic Council and National Assembly; the Metropolitan Police and the United Forces; the Equalists under Amon (Yan)
AttacksAsagawa transit hub (16 Aug); Pro-Bending Arena (17 Aug); Yu Dao exchange (c. 11 Sep) and police station (18 Sep); a device in a bending school
Deaths31 at the arena; at least 237 at Yu Dao; 412 in a month by the Council President's count; the real total is unknown
OutcomeMartial law in three zones (22 Sep); the Raiko Amendment in 171 AG

The Republic City crisis of 170 AG was a twelve-week sequence of a police killing, mass demonstrations, bombings and emergency measures in the United Republic of Nations. It began with the death of the textile worker Dava in early July and ended, in the sources that survive, with a police raid on an Equalist communication hub in the Longshore district. In between, the republic passed the constitutional reform that bears the name of Raiko, put its army on the streets of its own capital and received the Avatar Korra, who had come to learn airbending and spent the autumn trying to find a place in the argument. It is the immediate background of the civil wars of 171 AG.

Background

The Council and the reform

The United Republic was governed in 170 AG by a Republic Council of six: Tarrlok (Northern Water, Council President), Viku (Southern Water), Ilama (Fire, from Yu Dao), Zi (Earth), Tenzin (Air) and Ujo, the only non-bender, who sits for the non-bending majority. Five of the six seats belong to benders, and by 170 AG it was the Equalists' loudest complaint that the republic's non-benders had one voice in six.

Raiko, a member of the National Assembly, proposed to replace the council with a presidential system modeled on the Qianchan Republic, without Qianchan's federal states. He had first proposed a single-chamber parliament; the final text kept the Assembly and added a Senate elected by proportional representation. The opposition, led by the firebender Zoltan, called him a would-be dictator; the independent Xinwan thought the reform right but risky. A referendum and several months of review by the Supreme Court preceded the Council's vote on 18 July. The Council had governed for "seven decades" by Tarrlok's reckoning, counting from the start of the War of Independence in 100 AG.

The eastern districts

The districts east of the city centre (Jianyu, Longshore, lower Asagawa) are mill and dock districts with a non-bender majority, bordered on the north by Kennouchi, which is old Fire Nation heritage and voted against the reform, and on the east by the Hengdong agricultural belt, which is of Earth Kingdom heritage. The Fujishihoro highlands, a range that runs east to west across the main island, were the stronghold of the resistance of the War of Independence and of the highland insurgencies of 118–124 AG. Officials who knew the map saw that the attacks of 170 AG did not fall on one side of that line.

Chronology

DateEvent
c. 7 July 170 AGDeath of Dava. Dava, a twenty-three-year-old non-bender textile worker from the mill on Harbor Approach, is shot dead by Officer Han of the Metropolitan Police at a labor demonstration over shift lengths at Jianyu Square. The government says she rushed a police line; her coworkers say she had her hands raised. A blurred photograph and four and a half minutes of footage circulate and every side reads them as proof. Han is suspended and sent out of the city to relatives near Juniper. See Dava.
Early July 170 AGThe Equalists send a coordination notice to their eastern-district cells four days before the demonstration is announced publicly. It describes the demonstration as an opportunity and names the pharmacy corner of Jianyu Square, where Dava and her friend Fen will stand.
18 July 170 AGConstitutional vote. The Speaker of the National Assembly announces that the Republic Council has voted 4–2 for the constitutional reform proposed by the Assembly member Raiko. Councillors Tenzin (Air), Ujo (non-bender), Ilama (Fire, of Yu Dao) and Zi (Earth) vote in favor; the Council President Tarrlok (Northern Water) and Viku (Southern Water) vote against. The Supreme Court had found the reform constitutional after several months of review. The Council of Six signs the text the same day on Air Temple Island. The reform replaces the council republic with a presidential system, adds a proportionally elected Senate beside the Assembly, and takes effect after a transition period. Raiko challenges the opposition leader Zoltan, a firebender, to a presidential election.
18 July 170 AGThe Avatar Korra lands at Republic City and is flown to Air Temple Island with Varrick and Zhu Li and a White Lotus escort, to begin airbending with Tenzin. A crowd of children and fans meets her. RCNN broadcasts the signing and her arrival in the same bulletin.
c. 28 July 170 AGJianyu Square demonstration. A permitted gathering, estimated at 400–500 by dispatch, grows to 600–800 by nightfall and chants Dava's name; leaflets reading Equality. Rights. Dava. and bearing a circle-and-wheel symbol have been left in an alley behind the pharmacy. After dark a sharp sound from the western side sends the crowd into motion; a mill worker is taken to Republic City General at 21:47 and three people are arrested. The press, the police and the demonstrators disagree about what started it. (In a separate incident, three shots were heard near Jianyu and Sixth on a morning in the same weeks.)
c. 1–5 August 170 AGAt a closed meeting on paper maps, Chief Lin Beifong tells General Tao of the city garrison, Councillors Ilama and Zi and Tenzin that there have been eight incidents in four districts in three weeks: five on infrastructure (substations, a rail switching station, Hengdong water pumps), three on benders, and a device in the ventilation of a bending school in the Fujishihoro foothills, found by a twelve-year-old student. It is judged "meant to be found". Tao says the pattern recalls the highland resistance networks of the War of Independence. Tenzin names Yan; Beifong answers that Yan is the name used while the structure is not understood. Tarrlok's chair is empty. Korra, who attended, then watches rival crowds, Equalist and pro-bending-fan, chant across Jianyu boulevard.
16 August 170 AGAsagawa transit hub bombing. A bomb wrecks the eastern dispatch building of the metro authority. The first reports call it a gas line failure; the casualty figure is never stated and rumors range from 12 to 40. Metro service is suspended in the east.
17 August 170 AGPro-Bending Arena bombing. At about 08:47, on a match day, a device explodes in the VIP level, followed by a secondary device. The radio gives 19 dead, then 43; the press runs Dozens feared dead. At 14:00 Beifong confirms 31 dead and about 104 injured, both devices in the VIP level, no claim of responsibility. The tournament is suspended. Asami Sato and the pro-benders Mako and Bolin leave through the maintenance exit.
18 August 170 AGBeifong sends units into three zones (Jianyu, Longshore, lower Asagawa) with target lists: twelve detentions, four with actionable links and eight by proximity. She releases six. At 22:00 she orders a curfew in the eastern districts for an initial 72 hours. The curfew is renewed four times by the end of September. A night patrol recalls the Wada district emergency of 155 AG, which lasted three weeks and left two dead on each side.
c. 11 September 170 AGYu Dao exchange bombing. The lower three floors of the Yu Dao exchange building, on Nanaka island on the harbor front, are destroyed; the trading floor is lost. A fourth-floor office loses eleven people. The exchange moves to Shicheng, volume falls by sixty percent, and Qianchan institutions begin to route trade around it.
14 September 170 AGIn closed session the transitional authority amends Article 14, subsection 3 of the transitional constitutional framework: the 72-hour civilian review of emergency deployments is removed and unilateral authorization extended. The amendment is not published.
18 September 170 AGYu Dao station bombing. At about 07:55 a bomb destroys the front of Yu Dao Central Police Station on Harbor Front, built in 128 AG. Sergeant Polo dies in the second-floor briefing room; Constable Park is hurt; Constable Hwan was upstairs; Officer Sera Lim, seven minutes late, is on the pavement. The Assembly is later told that the Yu Dao toll stands at 237 and will rise.
22 September 170 AGMartial law vote. The Assembly meets at 09:03 before three foreign missions, with Korra in the public gallery. Ilama calls the attacks an act of war; Zoltan demands full authorization without review; Assemblyman Cho and Assemblywoman Dae speak; Raiko, citing "over four hundred" dead in a month, supports it "with oversight"; Tenzin opposes it, warning against turning the army on citizens. Tarrlok, who has had his motion drafted for three days, moves martial law in the eastern districts, the Fujishihoro highland zone and the Hengdong agricultural belt, with a 72-hour review. It passes with 81 percent. Tenzin is the only councillor against; the Assembly members from Hengdong (three), Longshore (two), Shicheng (one) and Jianyu vote no. It is signed at 10:47; orders go out at 11:00 and troops are in the eastern districts by noon. (A General Staff colonel gives the interval after the bombing as 41 hours, which would make it 20 September.)
23 September 170 AGAt 06:03 military personnel carriers relieve the police at the Jianyu-adjacent checkpoint; Officer Kwan's unit is reassigned at 07:00. The photographer Yuna photographs the handover. In the Longshore district she interviews Sera Lim, whose brother farms in Hengdong.
Late September 170 AGAt the Caijia facility General Ta Min of the United Forces' southern theater, Colonel Fenn and the civilian Shen ask Hiroshi Sato for the current mechanized suits in six weeks at reduced specification, and for a new-generation exosuit (¥8,000,000). On 28 September Asami Sato confronts him with the ¥20,000 the company gave the police memorial fund, proposes that ten percent of defense revenue go to victims, and demands that the posted notice at the mill be taken down. Hiroshi locks the blueprint in a drawer.
c. 29 September 170 AGA typewritten Equalist leaflet found at the Jianyu checkpoint at 06:15 cites the unpublished Article 14 amendment and states that Dava "was there about wages". The journalist who finds it, Yuna of Republican Daily, reasons that the author has a source in the government and one in the movement, and that Yan "is deciding what you find".
c. 30 September 170 AGRepublican Daily publishes Who Was Dava, 800 words, built on the account of Fen and on the labor notice, the mill's shift logs and a coworker's injury report. The Equalists claim the story as theirs. The notice about "personal responsibility" posted at the mill after the injury comes down on the Tuesday, following a telephone call to the floor supervisor from a source never identified. Beifong orders the two Jianyu detainees she had held reviewed for release.
c. 1 October 170 AGAn Equalist, Rill, of the Longshore cell, comes to the paper with three things: the coordination notice and its pharmacy corner, the district and type of the network's communication hub (Eastern Longshore, a commercial building with a ground-floor business as cover) and a warning that something operational is coming. Her building matches the middle of three possible sites that Beifong has been narrowing, which a four-line intercept now confirms. The hub is a laundry on Fengdao Street. At 22:00 Beifong briefs Dren's unit and Korra, who has left the observer pass behind; they move forty minutes later. The sources end here.
171 AGThe Raiko Amendment takes effect and the United Republic becomes a presidential state under President Raiko. The Equalists are a declared terrorist organization. See Unrest of 167–171 AG.

Casualties

No complete count exists. Beifong confirmed 31 dead and about 104 injured at the arena by 14:00 on the day. The transit hub toll was never stated. The Assembly was told on 22 September that Yu Dao had cost at least 237 lives, a provisional figure. In the same debate Tarrlok gave 412 deaths in a month across three coordinated strikes and Raiko "over four hundred"; the two do not agree with the arena and Yu Dao figures when summed, and no source reconciles them. The Metropolitan Police treated figures from the radio (19, 43) as unreliable from the first day.

The Equalist network

The police believed the attacks came from the Equalists, whose leader, Amon, appears in police briefings as Yan. The Equalists did not claim the arena or Yu Dao attacks. Beifong and her intelligence officer Sho told her superiors that the structure was unknown: it could be Yan, someone near him, or someone using his name and network to a different end. The network distributed through a laundry on Fengdao Street in Longshore, whose owner Chu asked no questions in return for a share of his rent, and was organised in cells of about seven people. Rill, a Longshore organiser who had joined through the dockworkers, concluded from the pharmacy-corner notice that the leadership had known where Dava would stand, and asked for a week to find out; she took her evidence to the press before the week was over.

The government response

Three measures followed one another: the police detention drive and curfew of 18 August, the Assembly authorization of 22 September and the deployment of the United Forces to the eastern districts, the highlands and the Hengdong belt. The authorization rested on the amended Article 14, subsection 3, adopted in closed session on the 14th, four days before the Yu Dao station was bombed. The veteran constitutional correspondent Hemi, of Republican Daily, confirmed from a source in the government that the amendment was real and described it as housekeeping; the source did not address the timing. A later claim that Tarrlok had written his motion three days before the Yu Dao station bomb is recorded, but not documented.

The deployment reached the Hengdong villages within weeks. Checkpoints lengthened the farmers' market runs; a village school ran half days; children drew soldiers beside their houses and animals. A farmer there told the Avatar to "work faster".

Industry

The United Forces' demand for mechanized equipment, first placed with Future Industries before the crisis, was accelerated after the arena bombing. The company's chairman, Hiroshi Sato, suspected that his contact in the military coordination office, Shen, represented a faction inside the government with its own interest in the "post-deployment settlement". His daughter Asami persuaded him to withdraw the exosuit proposal from the table and to review the shifts at one of his supplier mills, the mill where Dava had worked.

The press

Republican Daily's photographer Yuna, embedded with the police, photographed the transfer of the checkpoint to the army and a portrait of Sera Lim's hands that was widely reprinted. Her story Who Was Dava changed what the republic thought the demonstrations had been about, from the Equalists and the police to twelve-hour shifts and a posted notice about personal responsibility. Rao, her editor, noted that Yan had left the leaflet where she would find it and that the story was true.

Consequences

  • Constitutional. The emergency provisions of 170 AG became part of the presidential constitution that took effect in 171 AG; the Raiko Amendment is the best known of them.
  • Political. The Equalists were declared a terrorist organization; Raiko, who had supported the deployment "with oversight", won the presidency.
  • Social. The curfew and checkpoints taught a generation in the eastern districts that the republic and its army were the same thing. The movements in the unrest recruited there.
  • The Avatar. Korra concluded that observing was not enough and that the Avatar ought to be "in the room".

Sources and discrepancies

The main narrative source is the serial Dawn of a New Revolution, which this article follows wherever the wiki's other pages differ; see About Avatar: New Red Dawn. The accounts disagree on a few points:

  • The place of Dava's death. Official statements say the harbor district; Fen and the leaflets say Jianyu Square.
  • The vote. The press gives 22 September; a colonel's briefing gives 41 hours after the bombing.
  • Seven decades. The Council counted from 100 AG, the start of the War of Independence; the formal union dates from 105 AG (Treaty of Qinglan).
  • Korra's time in the city. "Four months" in one briefing; the raid is only about two and a half months after her arrival.
